, m. or nt. (from prec. plus suffix ka), in ekālop˚ and saptālop˚, the practice of eating only (one, or seven) mouthful(s) of almsfood:, ekālopakair, and saptālopakaiḥ; so read for ˚lāp˚ of both edd., no v.l.; cf. Pali ekālopika, sattālopika, and 12, one who adheres to these respective practices. Confirmed by Tib. kham.
(f.; = Skt. āvali, ˚lī), row, line: chattrāvaḍibhir anvitāḥ.
, m. pl., v.l. (read by) for Avantaka, q.v.:.

, nt. (= Pali id.; see also an-āv˚ and āvṛti), hindrance, obstruction (= pratighātaḥ; in Tib. standardly rendered sgrib pa, darkness, obscuration, hence sin);, note. Two kinds, kleśāv˚ (moral faults) and jñeyāv˚ (intellectual faults); gotra of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas free from the former, that of bodhisattvas, only, free also from the latter,; the two kinds mentioned also;;; āvaraṇa-dvayam; karmāv˚, obstruction due to past actions,;;;; six obstacles to samādhi, samādhy-āv˚ (kausīdyaṃ mānaṃ śāṭhyam auddhatyam anābhogaḥ satyābhogaś ceti); general,;; āvaraṇāṃ (acc. pl.) vinivartiya sarvāṃ; sarvāvaraṇa-vivaraṇa-; -āvaraṇāya (see s.v. vimātratā), etc., common.

, adj., pertaining to (causing) obstruction (āvaraṇa, q.v.): of karman;; of dharma conditions, states of being;; of thoughts (citta); as quasi-subst., without noun, things that cause obstruction, viśodhakāni … āvaraṇīyānām.

, nt. (to āvarjayati, q.v.; see also āvarjanā; substantially as in Skt., once, das Sich-geneigt-Machen, Gewinnen,), wrongly defined for and in; attraction, winning to oneself: (dhyānagocarāṇāṃ ca rūpāvacarāṇāṃ) ca devānām dhyānaviśeṣopadarśanād āvarjanaṃ kuryām (by performing severe austerities; said by the Bodhisattva); devānāṃ cāvarjanārtham; āvarjana-saṃpanno (doué de bonne grâce, dʼaffabilité; i.e. gifted with winning ways; followed by mārdavasaṃpanno aparuṣo); especially (cf. āvarjayati) conversion: āvarjanārhāṇāṃ sattvānām āvarjanāya (contrasts with preceding uttrāsanārhāṇāṃ sattvānām uttrāsanāya); often this is accomplished by miracles, because, as says, āśu pṛthagjanāvarjanakarī ṛddhiḥ, magic converts the vulgar quickly; virtually the same words;;; and ṛddhy-āvarjanatā, process of conversion by (exhibitions of) magic; tad atyadbhutaṃ devamanuṣyāvarjanakaraṃ prātihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā; the same etc.

= āvarjana, winning to oneself, the making kindly disposed: in read: bodhisattvo rudrakasya rāmaputrasya saśiṣyasyāvarjanāṃ (so 2 mss. incl. the best; ed. ˚janī-)kṛtvā … prakrāmad. (The gen. requires noun āvarjanāṃ.) Tib. ḥdun par byas nas, which is wrongly rendered by; it appears to mean lit. having made reconciled or desirous, i.e. having made to be of good will (towards himself, the Bodhisattva).

(Skt., sich Jmd geneigt machen, für sich gewinnen,), in BHS specifically converts; cf. prec. two (Pali āvajjeti not recognized in this sense; but acc. to often rendered in comms. by pariṇāmeti, which could surely mean brings to religious maturity): (bhagavān … nirvāṇe pratiṣṭhāpayanto) āvarjayitvā aṅgamagadhāṃ [Page107-b] etc. (long list of peoples), having converted …; closely similar is; Vāsavadattā saṃsārād udvignā buddhaguṇānusmaraṇāc cāvarjitahṛdayovāca, … her heart converted, turned (to religion); nāvarjayati, does not convert (people); often this is done by miracles, yan nv ahaṃ Pūrṇa-brāhmaṇam ṛddhiprātihāryeṇāvarjayeyam; prātihāryair āvarjitāḥ; (prātihāryeṇ-)āvarjitamānasā(ḥ); āvarjitamānasaḥ; see under āvarjana.

, m., n. of a sea and of a mountain:;. Note: as common noun, āvarta seems to me to have only meanings which it has in Skt., as turn, turning, turning-place (dhāraṇyāvartāṃ … dhāraṇīṃ etc.); eddy, whirlpool (); etc.; in, several times, probably of turns (curves, or the like) of alphabetic signs; see utkṣepa-lipi.

, nt., (1) wandering, straying about (= Pali āvattana; in Skt. not after.): (= skor ba; followed by parivartanam); adrākṣīc Chakro … taṃ devaputram atyarthaṃ pṛthivyām āvartanaṃ parivartantam; (2) devious winding, with implication of deceptive, wily movements (= Pali āvaṭṭana): sarvamārapathāvartana-vivartanajñānānugataḥ, pursuing knowledge of all the devious windings and turnings-back of the paths of Māra.

, seems = āvartana, q.v., wandering, (re-)turn, in sarvalokāvarty-anupravartana-karuṇāgarbha, n. of samādhi, full of the compassion (born of) following the wanderings (rebirths) of all (the) world (s).

, nt. (to next with -ana; cf. Pali abbāhana, extraction, as of thorns; but the real Pali equivalent is abbhāna), removal, freeing (of a monk from certain penances): = Tib. dbyuṅ ba, removal, also freeing; (requires a quorum of twenty monks);;.

, also ābrah- (on origin and Pali relations see s.v. ābṛhati), frees a monk from religious disabilities (cf. prec.): ābrahitavya, gdve.,; ābṛhyāt, prec., 2; ābṛhita, ppp., 3; āvarhata; ˚hatu; ˚het; āvarhitavya, gdve.,; ˚hitum, inf.,; ppp. āvarhitaḥ;; āvrīḍhaḥ;, etc. (cf. ābrīḍha to ābṛhati, extracted, s.v. ābṛḍha-).
(from avasāna plus -ika), of the end, final: tatra bījam āvasānikasya svaphalasyākṣepahetuḥ.

(m.; rare in Skt. except in cpds., cf. durāvāra,), guard, in ˚ra-nibandhana, nt., imprisonment under guard: (vs) kṛtvāvāranibandhanam, making (i.e. applying to his victims) … (so mss., possibly intending vāra˚, but this word is hardly used except at the end of cpds.; āvāra occurs also in Pali; emends to kārā-nib˚).

(once acc. ˚riṃ, otherwise all unambiguous forms show ā- and -ī; Skt. Lex. āvāri; avārī and avāra), shop, bazaar, only noted in : ˚ryāṃ vyāpāraṃ kuru;; ˚rī-samutthitaṃ dravyam; kāśikavastrāvārī, and other cpds. in ˚rī, etc.; ˚rī-gataṃ kṣetragataṃ ca śasyādidhanajātaṃ tad apy agninā dagdhaṃ; bhāṇḍāvārīṃ (in 15 ˚riṃ) gatvā.
, m. pl., a class of gods, = śuddhāvāsa, q.v.; only in vs, presumably m.c.: ˚ddhā upagatā devaputrāḥ.

, adj. (= Pali id.), resident? (in a monastery; said of a monk) or possibly servant, see s.v. navakarmika: sa cāvāsiko bhikṣus tatra nāsīt … bhakte sajjīkṛte āvāsiko bhikṣur āgataḥ (in and called naivāsika, q.v.); ˚kaḥ so 'stu mahāvihāre; āvāsika-naivāsikair bhikṣubhir.

(Skt. ifc.), dweller (with, near, in the confines of; [Page108-a] with gen.): brāhmaṇagṛhapatayaḥ (sc. varṣāḥ, see) upagatakānām (sc. bhikṣūṇām) āvāsī (n. pl.) … anuprayacchanti, brahmans and householders living (in the confines settled {{apon->upon||20210831||https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/80|}}) for (the monks) that have entered into residence (for the rains) …

, m. (= Pali id.), taking in marriage, taking to wife; as in Pali, compounded or associated with vivāha (q.v. in) giving (a girl) in marriage: = Tib. bag mar blaṅ(s) pa (vivāha = bag mar btaṅ ba); āvāha-vivāha-, cpd.,;, taking and giving in marriage; often rendered, approximately, marriage of a son and of a daughter; āvāho vā vivāho vā;. Skt. vivāha marriage seems usually to have no such limitation of meaning, but perhaps āvāha and vivāha have the BHS mgs. in (otherwise).

, f. ˚ikā, adj. (to Skt. ā-vah-), bringing in, introductive, inductive: āvāhaka-hetuḥ (one of 10 kinds of hetu); (tat punar bījanirvṛttaṃ) phalam uttarasya bījākṣiptaphalasyāvāhakahetuḥ; (… tasyāḥ sasyaniṣpatteḥ sasya-)-paripākasyāvāhakahetuḥ; (sā … prajñāpāramitā na kasyacit dharmasyāveśikā) vā … āvāhikā vā nirvāhikā vā.

, perhaps slightly (ā) fallen down (see vigalita):, a corrupt and dubious line of vs: kiṃ dāni āvigalitā (mss. ˚to) vara- (mss. vana-)-keśa- (so 5 mss., with 1 ms. kośa-)-bhārā (mss. ˚ro) vāṣpaughasaṃstaragatā madanābhibhūtā; said of the harem-womenʼs expected reaction to the Bodhisattvaʼs impending departure. If -keśa- be adopted, possibly with their beautiful masses of hair somewhat loosened (dishevelled).

, ppp. of ā-vyadh, in vihāraḥ … āviddhaprākāratoraṇo, prob. (with walls and arched gateways) fastened on, attached, or possibly pierced. Acc. to curved, crooked; he refers to, but here the word is applied to a potterʼs wheel and means whirled, set in motion, made to revolve.]

, m., in (prose) ˚kā(ḥ), n. pl., n. of some kind of tradesman or artisan; in a long list of such. also reads so by em. at, where mss. ācambika or āvambikā. In both followed by guḍapācakāḥ. Obscure and prob. corrupt.

, is tired or aches (Tib. mi bde, not well), only in pṛṣṭhī me ˚ti = Pali piṭṭhī me āgilāyati (stock phrase). The seeming denom. from Skt. āvila is prob. a corruption or rationalization for āgilāyati, q.v. (MIndic form, perh. deliberately made over).
= avīci, n. of a hell: ˚cim ādiṃ kṛtvā (prose), so both edd. without v.l.; but reads avīci, referring to this passage.
= āyus, life? () So acc. to, (prose) samaye ca āvusā (one ms. āyusā, dental s) dayanto (mss. ˚nte), presumed to mean and on occasion giving alms with their lives. Doubtful.

, and other forms based on Pali āvuso, brother! (see s.v. āyuṣmaṃ): āvusa, as if voc. to a stem of that form, is used repeatedly as an address in, e.g., etc. In (vs) reads āvuso; meter needs ‒ ⏑ x; mss. āyuṣaḥ (note that no form of āyuṣmant is metrically possible), ānuṣaḥ, onuṣaḥ, ānuṣa; in (prose) āvusāho (for ed. āyuṣmanto), certainly to be read (voc. pl. of a stem āvusa, as in, with ending āho,); in (prose) āvusāvo seems to be found in the same sense (mss. unanimous on -vo; see; in 16 mss. ānusāvo or anu˚, but no v.l. in 15).
, ppp. of ā-vas (= Pali āvuttha), inhabited: so read for avustaṃ (both edd., no v.l.) (vs; meter indifferent).

(see ābṛhati, ābṛṃhaṇa, etc.), removes, tears away: (prose) teṣām āvṛṃhitaṃ (v.l. [Page108-b] āvṛh˚) tac chavimānsalohitaṃ vyavadahyati; in read with mss. āvṛṃhato (pres. pple.) chavimānsarudhiraṃ vā prasāraye, tearing off the very skin, flesh, and blood, would remove them.

, ppp. (corresp. to Pali ovaṭa, as), forbidden (also an-ā˚, q.v.): āvṛtam ānanda bhikṣuṇyā bhikṣuṃ codayituṃ () … anāvṛtaṃ bhikṣor bhikṣuṇīṃ codayituṃ …, it is forbidden for a nun to warn a monk, not for a monk to warn a nun.
, f. = āvaraṇa, q.v.: (vs) kṣapayaty āvṛtī sarvā(ḥ); cited with āvṛtīḥ; Tib. sgrib pa, regularly = āvaraṇa.

, ppp. (= Pali id.; see veṭhayati), put around: (prose) āveṭhita- (but only by em.; mss. āveṭī-)prākārā, fig. of Buddhas, having encircling (moral) walls. Could āveṭhī be defended, as a noun, from the same root?

, adj. (= Pali id. or ˚ṇiya; etym. obscure; see also āveṇīya, āvedanika, and,), peculiar, individual, particular, special: (a cliché, practically identical with etc.) pañcāveṇikā dharmā ekatye paṇḍitajātīye mātṛgrāme, there are five peculiar characteristics in every intelligent woman (listed in the sequel); ˚kā ime svārthā anuprāpto bhaviṣyāmi, I shall have attained these special purposes of mine (iti saṃpaśyatā paṇḍitenālam eva pravrajyādhimuktena bhavitum); ye te sattvā āveṇikā bhavanti, evaṃrūpāḥ sattvā (sc. Buddhas, special creatures) āryadharmacakraṃ pravartenti; there are three āveṇika smṛtyupasthāna (q.v.) in a Buddha,;; listed; (referred to without the adjective āveṇika,;;) especially used of the 18 āveṇika buddhadharma of a Buddha, listed (Tib. ma ḥdres pa, unmixed, unadulterated, pure); the list here is, (1) nāsti tathāgatasya skhalitam, (2) nāsti ravitam, (3) nāsti muṣitasmṛtitā (or ˚tiḥ), (4) nāsty asamāhitacittam, (5) nāsti nānātvasaṃjñā, (6) nāsty apratisaṃkhyāyopekṣā, (7) nāsti chandasya hāniḥ, (8) nāsti vīryasya hāniḥ, (9) nāsti smṛtihāniḥ, (10) nāsti samādhihāniḥ, (11) nāsti prajñāyā hāniḥ, (12) nāsti vimuktihāniḥ, (13) sarva-kāya-karma jñānāpūrvaṃgamaṃ jñānānuparivarti, (14 and 15) id. with vāk, manaḥ, for kāya, (16—18) atīte (17 anāgate, 18 pratyutpanne) 'dhvany asaṅgam apratihataṃ jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate; similarly (here they constitute the 5th cakṣuḥ, q.v., viz. buddha-c˚); =; =; =; =; (substantially as in; two obvious errors); in comm. (before the vs called āveṇika guṇa, but after it āv˚ buddhadharma) divided into groups, called six cāra-saṃgṛhīta āv˚ bu˚ (=), six adhigama-saṃgṛhīta (=), three jñāna-saṃgṛhīta (=), three karmasaṃgṛhīta (=); Appendice IX, cites a late Pali list from the Jinālaṃkāra, which substantially agrees in order with that of (but the category is unknown to older and genuine Pali Buddhism, cf., l. c. above); references to the 18 āv˚(bu˚)dh˚,;;; (text corrupt, see and);;;;;;;;;; āveṇika bu˚ dh˚ (no number given);;;; eighteen āveṇika (no noun expressed); āveṇika, without number or noun but obviously meaning the same 18,;; acc. to and āveṇika buddhadharma, listed (incl. the 32 lakṣaṇa, 80 anuvyañjana, etc., but not the 18 usually recognized); in a totally different list of 18 āveṇika bodhisattva-dharma.
, adj. = āveṇika, q.v.: and [Page109-a] pancāveṇīyā dharmā ihaikatye paṇḍitajātīye mātṛgrāme, see the same cliché under āveṇika.

, adj., used in for āveṇika, by false Sktization (, and loc. cit. s.v. āveṇika; for MIndic (Pali) āveṇiya, ‘analyzed as āveyaṇiya from āvedanika’): aṣṭādaśasv āvedanikeṣu buddhadharmeṣu; etc., regularly; yet in āveṇika (still in text of).

, (1) (m.?; not in this sense Skt. or Pali; not in Pkt.), depth (of a sea or river; lit. penetration? cf. udvedha): mahāsamudrāc caturāśītiyojanasahasrāṇy āvedhena tiryag-aprameyāt, from the great ocean, 84,000 yojanas in depth and immeasurable across; (santi yāvad …) -pañcāśadyojanavistārā (sc. mahānadyo) yāvad dvādaśayojanāvedhāḥ, (there are great rivers, up to) 50 yojanas in width, up to 12 yojanas in depth; (2) m., continuing force, as of an arrow that has been shot, or as of the shoot of a plant growing forth, and fig. of the continuative force of life which manifests itself in the skandha, see; pūrvāvedhāt = pūrvābhyāsāt, from the continuing force of past activity: nikāya-sabhāgasyāvedhaḥ, the continuative force of the common element in the class (of living beings, sattva; see sabhāga 2), which causes rebirth; Tib. ḥphen pa, something like projection. So also āvedhaḥ = Tib. ḥphen pa, or śugs, inherent power, energy (). In āvedhaḥ (between ākṣepaḥ and prasabham), physical projection, penetration (cf. Pali id.); Tib. also ḥphen pa.

, in (vs) āveśād (but best ms. ādeśād) … jinottamānāṃ, equivalent to buddhānām … adhiṣṭhānena (q.v.: by the supernatural power of the Buddhas) in 9—10 above. Our phrase, as in text, could mean because of entrance, possession, on the part of the Buddhas (s.v. 2 and 3); or, reading ādeśād, by command of them. Tib. mthu, power (esp. of magic).
) f. ˚ikā, adj., introducing, bringing in; one who or that which introduces: (sā) khalu punar iyaṃ subhūte prajñāpāramitā na kasyacid dharmasyāveśikā vā niveśikā vā …

= āyūhati, exerts oneself towards, carries out, performs, with acc.:; sa na kaṃcid dharmam āvyūhati nirvyūhati tasyaivam anāvyūhato 'nirvyūhatas traidhātuke cittaṃ na sajjati. Is nirvyūhati a near-synonym of āvyūhati, as niryūhati certainly is of āyūhati in ? Or is it (as assumed by Tib. and) an antonym of āvyūhati, as niryūhati is of āyūhati in, and as (a)niryūha is of (an)āyūha? See s.vv anāyūha, anāvyūha, anirvyūha.
(-sahavratā), (mss. āśaṅkitavyaṃ or āsakitavyaṃ sahavratāyai), is certainly a corruption for ākiṃcanyāyatana- (sahavratā), q.v., as in; cf. =.]
, food-bowl: in (cf.) read sauvarṇāśapātrī (= ˚ṇā āśa˚), for text ˚ṇā sapātrī.

, as in Skt., and Pali āsaya, mental disposition, intent ( intention); common, but not specifically Buddhist, except the adverbs āśayena heartily, earnestly (ms. āśrayena; cf. adhyāśayena), and āśayataḥ ibid.;;;. The mgs. abode, basis etc. are also standard Skt. Cf. adhyāśaya, which is specifically Buddhist. If is right in keeping āsayāni in, it would have to be understood as = āśayāni, (evil) intentions or inclinations; but see āsaya. Often cpd. with anuśaya, q.v.

, (1) n. of one of four daughters of Indra:; all four are among eight devakumārikā in the northern quarter, =; (2) n. of a [Page109-b] female lay-disciple (upāsikā): In mg. 1 certainly a personification of āśā hope: the other three are Śraddhā, Śrī, and Hrī, qq.v.
, conjectured () to mean great wood: yāvad anyatamāśāṭavī praviṣṭā (mss. ˚ṭāḥ). Tib., cited by, shows true reading, ˚tamā śālāṭavī.]
(dental t; = Pali āsāṭikā), egg of a fly or other insect; nit (compares Marathi āsāḍī); as vermin afflicting cattle, (, cf., with comparison of corresponding Pali text).

, f. (once in Skt., Gebet; from ā-śās, wish, desire), desire: sarvā hy āśāstaya(ś) chit(t)vā, = Pali ( et alibi) āsattiyo, but this Pali word = Skt. āsakti, attachment, and so substantially the same as longing, desire. Is āśāsti false Skt. for Pali āsatti (used in the Pali form of the same verse where it occurs in)?
, (vs), ʼs em.; read with most mss. (some āsā-)āśāvrate, in the solemn-undertaking of his aspiration (āśā, proved by Tib. bsam pa). Cf (vs) prapūrṇā ti āsā (= āśā).]

, the a-stems being prob. m. (); the Pali equivalent is āsītika, m. (not ˚kā, f., as stated in), n. of some plant; occurs, regularly in comp. with -parvāṇi (as in Pali with -pabbāni, =), in the account of the Bodhisattvaʼs emaciated state after his long fast, his members being compared to the joints of this plant. The reading asita(ka) is prob. due to popular etymology, association with asita black; kāla, q.v., occurs in the context, and note kālāśītako (perhaps read ˚ke with v.l.). Other cases, all in comp. with parvāṇi: āsītakī-; āśītakī- (all mss.; inexplicably reads āsitakī- here!); aśītaka- (v.l. asita-); in omits the word with one ms., but the other ms. has aśita-parvāṇi; aśitaka- (one ms., the other omits, em. aśītaka-); aśīta- (v.l. asita-). The evidence points, on the whole, to āśītaka- or ˚kī- as the original form.

, m. (in Skt., and Pali-Pkt. āsīvisa, only serpent; so also here, even in, e.g.;), serpent-venom, repeatedly in : ˚ṣān vamanti sma, ˚ṣān … bhakṣayanti sma 14; ˚ṣān niścārayanti sma, … vamanto 21. In āśīviṣapariveṣṭitaśarīrāḥ is taken by in this sense, le corps enduit de venin de serpent; but surely it is rather having bodies entwined by serpents, despite neighboring passages showing the other mg. See sumbhalikā.
, f. pl., n. of certain rivers: ˚nadīnāṃ tīre śālmalīvanam. See Saptāśīviṣa-, and next.
, n. of a river: ˚ṣāyāṃ, loc.,;. See under prec.

: and, assumes use as ‘expletive’, ‘to strengthen the force of the verb,’ ‘in epic and Buddhist Skt.,’ and suggests relation to the Pali particle assu. He so interprets āśu in. I disagree on all this; it seems to me that there is no reason to assume any āśu except the adj. and adverb, quick(ly). Tib. renders quickly at.]
, n. of a former Buddha: (n. sg., mss. ˚rīḥ or ˚riḥ, em. ˚rī; prose, followed by dh-).
, n. of a king, former incarnation of Buddha:.
, nt. (also aśrāddhya, q.v.; = Pali assaddhiya), disbelief, lack of (true) faith:; acc. to text of Kyoto ed. and v.l. of; text of aśraddhya; Index to Kyoto ed. cites both.

, m. (Skt., basis etc.), (1) in, acc. to, the ālaya-vijñāna (q.v.) as basis of all vijñānas; one must make it converted, in revulsion (parāvṛtta, cf. parāvṛttāśraya); anyathā dṛśyamāna ucchedam āśraye (so read with v.l. for ˚yo, text ˚yaḥ), if the basis is otherwise regarded (loc. abs.), (there is) destruction (it is fatal to the holder of such a view); (2) acc. to citation in, six āśraya = the six sense organs (as one of the three groups constituting the 18 dhātu); this is said to be attributed to the Yogācāras in ‘le commentaire de LʼAbhidharma’; it does not seem to occur in and I have not noted precisely this usage in any text, but cf. next; (3) acc. to, le corps muni dʼorganes, qui est le point dʼappui (āśraya) de ce qui est appuyé (āśrita) sur lui: à savoir de la pensée et des mentaux (cittacaitta). Is the obscure passage somehow concerned here? It reads, in a verse (see my Reader, Four Sights [],) describing disease (vyādhi): … śokānāṃ prabhavo rativyupasamo (i.e. ˚śamo) cittāśrayāṇāṃ nidhi, dharmasyopaśamaḥ (lacuna of 6 syllables) gātrāśritānāṃ gṛhaṃ, yo lokaṃ pibate vapuś ca grasate etc. I should be inclined to emend to cittāśravāṇāṃ (cf., below), but for the phrase gātrāśritānāṃ gṛhaṃ, which implies support for āśraya; refers to (l. c.), but finds it hard to apply āśraya and āśrita as used in that passage; (4) commonly, body (cf. prec.): (vs) subhato (= śu˚) kalpayamāna āśrayaṃ vitathena, falsely imagining the body to be handsome; lakṣaṇaiś ca pratimaṇḍitāśrayo; me jvalita āśrayaḥ, my body was burned; me tyakta varāśrayaḥ;;;; pretāśrayasadṛśāḥ; pretīṃ vikṛtāśrayāṃ;;;;;;; see also cañcitāśraya; [in āśraya(-kṣaya-jñāna-) without v.l., but Tib. translates āśrava, which must be adopted: knowledge leading to destruction of the impurities, not … of the body]. See next.

(ppp. of ā-śri); see s.v. āśraya 2, 3; acc. to, there cited, the 6 āśritas are la connaissance produite par la vue et par les autres sens …; acc. to, = citta-caitta; what gātrāśritānāṃ gṛhaṃ means (), as applied to vyādhi, is not clear.

(Pali assāsa-passāsa), m. dual or pl., breath; usually used without clear indication of difference between the two terms, like ānāpāna, q.v.: nāsikātaś cāśvāsapraśvāsāv uparuddhāv abhūtāṃ; ˚sā ūrdhvaṃ śiraḥkapālam upanighnanti sma; as separate words, āśvāsaviprahīnaḥ praśvāsavarjitu; mukhato nāsikāśrotrehi ca āśvāsapraśvāsā uparundhi (1 sg. aor.); ˚sehi tathāgataṃ upahanati; kāyasyāśvāsapraśvāsakṛtyaṃ; ˚sādikam; the verb uśvasati, q.v., [Page110-b] corresponds to āśvāsa in āśvāsapraśvāsā uparuddhā … no pi uśvasati na praśvasati (the two verbs repeated twice in lines 8, 9), cf. ucchvasantaṃ praśvasantam, rendered by Tib. dbugs dbyuṅ zhiṅ rṅub breathing out and in, but in line 15 below praśvasantaḥ is rendered dbugs dbyuṅ, breathing out (implying that ucchvasantaṃ was understood as breathing in); ucchvāsapraśvāso (sg.) also occurs, seemingly = āśvāsa-pra˚,; in it is entirely certain that praśvāsa is understood as outbreathing and āśvāsa inbreathing, tadanu tan mithunaṃ praśvāsavāyurathārūḍhaṃ nāsikāvivareṇa niḥsṛtya … sattvānāṃ kāyavākcittāni viśodhya gṛhītvā ca punar āśvāsavāyum āruhya tenaiva pathā svahṛtkamalakarṇikāyāṃ praviśet; consistent with this is AMg. ussāsa (and relatives), which BHS usage would clearly have associated with āśvāsa, and which acc. to means breathing in; Pali tradition is indeterminate, see which states that defines assāsa as outgoing, passāsa as incoming breath, but that in Sutta comms. (Suttantaṭṭhakathāsu) the reverse is taught (the passage is misunderstood by and; uppaṭipāṭiyā = Pkt. upparivāḍi, inverted, transposed). Tib. regularly āśvasati = dbugs brṅubs (or cognate) breathe in, etc., praśvasati = dbugs phyuṅ (or cognate) breathe out, etc.; it therefore supports, and incidentally the equation of āśvāsa with āna and praśvāsa with apāna (see ānāpāna). How old this interpretation is remains uncertain, esp. in view of the fact that in Pali the comms. differed; Buddhaghosa himself, in the passage cited, declines to arbitrate between the two opposing views. Whatever may have been the meaning of the two terms, it seems clear that the cpd. (like ānāpāna) was commonly used in the sense of breath, collectively and as a whole.

, nt., in hitvā ālayāni (see ālaya) āsayāni (v.l. āsanāni); the Pali parallel reads āsavāni = BHS āśravāṇi, ās˚, which must probably be read, since āśaya (q.v.) seems not to be used in a pejorative sense, and no other interpretation for āsaya seems possible.

, nt., and niḥsarita, nt.; ˚taṃ respectively: the first two of ten ‘bodily conditions’ (śarīrasthā dharmāḥ), the other 8 being cold, heat, hunger, thirst, delight, anger, birth-old-age-disease-and-death, and pain (pīḍā). Context throws no further light. Interpretation of these two terms obscure. Are they somehow related to āsario = saṃmukhāgataḥ, and ṇissariaṃ = srastam ibid. ? Something like slack condition, slumped-down state might be intended by niḥsarita; would āsarita be its opposite, a state arrived at the right point?

(perhaps oftener written āśrava), m. (= Pali āsava), evil influence, depravity, evil, sin, misery; s.v. anāsava, intoxicants, i.e … passions;, Lʼécoulement (āsrava) est le mouvement qui porte la pensée à se répandre, comme une eau qui fuit, vers les choses du dehors;,, note: the influences which attach a man to the saṃsāra; hence sāsrava and laukika are equivalent, as are anāsrava and lokottara; Tib. (e.g. on āśravaḥ) zag pa, misery, also sin: anupādāyāsravebhyaś cittāni vimuktāni, see anupādāya; āśravakṣayajñāna is [Page112-a] the sixth abhijñā, q.v.; śuṣkā āśravā na puna śravanti (with play on etym., root sru), the āśravas, dried up, flow no more; getting rid of them is arhatship, prāptaṃ mayārhatvaṃ kṣīṇā me āśravā(ḥ); jinā … ye prāptā āśravakṣayam; arhantānāṃ kṣīṇāśravāṇām; the Buddha is sarvāśravāntakaraṇaṃ =; prahīnasarvāśravabandhanasya Buddhasya; kṣīṇāśrava (or ˚srava), said of a bhikṣu,, of a muni; equivalent to duḥkha, in formula of 4 noble truths: (after idaṃ duḥkham) ayam āśravasamudayo 'yam āśravanirodha iyam āśravanirodhagāminī pratipad; in, after statement of all four truths as usual with duḥkha, they are repeated with āśravāḥ (pl.), ime āśravāḥ, imo (mss. ime) āśravasamudayo ayaṃ āśravanirodho etc.; nirvāsyanti anāśravāḥ; there are four āśrava (also = ogha, yoga), listed, viz. kāma-, bhava-, avidyā-, dṛṣṭi- (so also in Pali, kāma, bhava, avijjā, diṭṭhi, but also a list of only three, omitting diṭṭhi); very common is anāsrava (= kṣīṇā˚ above), free from the depravities or from evil; pure (less commonly nirāśrava,, of Buddha), sometimes contrasted with its opposite sāśrava: nāpi ye dharmā anāśravāḥ te sāśravā ti deśayāmi (and vice versa); sāsravānāsravāḥ (dharmāḥ); devamanuṣyasarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhakuśalāni sāsravāṇy anāsravāṇi vā (all of little value); anāsrava (or ˚śrava), of persons, (read here adya me with mss. for adyeme);; jñānaṃ vipulaṃ anāsravam; anāśravaṃ te caraṇaṃ, thy conduct is pure; āśravāṇāṃ kṣayād anāśravāṃ cetovimuktiṃ (acc. sg.); anāśravasadṛśaṃ prathamadhyānaṃ; sāśravaṃ cittaṃ; sāśravānāṃ (dental n) … dhyānasamādhisamāpattīnāṃ (of the false teacher Rudraka) doṣo; unlike anuśaya, with which it is sometimes associated or even equated (), it is always used with evil connotation; in kalyāṇamitrādhīnāḥ … bodhisattvānāṃ sarvabodhisattvacaryāśravāḥ, the last cpd. contains -bodhisattvacaryā plus śravāḥ (= sravāḥ, streams; cf. -praṇidhāna-śrotāṃsi, line 6), not -āśravāḥ.

, a large number or method of computation:; no v.l., but, citing this passage, iṭṭā; Tib. for both gtan la ḥbebs pa (v.l. in gdan for gtan), which regularly = viniścaya; is it intended here to render the root iṅg in the sense of separation? Cf. the phonetic-grammatical use of the root, esp. s.v. iṅgya in.
= (and prob. false reading for) itthatva, q.v. However, if were right in his interpretation of icchantika, q.v., this would support derivation of icchatva from itthatva.

, adj. or subst. m., acc. to (,), one destitute of Buddha-nature: = Tib. ḥdod chen (po), (subject to) great desire (somehow based on pres. pple. of icchati); katham ˚ko bhavet; ˚kānāṃ … anicchantikatā-mokṣam (read as one cpd. word) kena pravartate; and often in., as cited by l. c., thought that the word was derived from *itthaṃtvika (cf. itthatva), worldly; Tib. does not support this.

, gdve., to be accepted, recognized (as in Skt. icchati): na khalv ayaṃ gharāvāso vā icchitavyo yasyedṛśo upabhogaparibhogo; niḥsaṃśayaṃ ayaṃ kumāro … kṛtādhikāro icchitavyo … Acc. to, MIndic for īkṣitavya, to be regarded. But in Pali and Pkt. icchati and derivs. seem always to represent Skt. iṣ, desire [except that derives some forms from īps, seek], while only ikkh- seems to represent īkṣ-.)
= iñjati, which perhaps should be read:, tasya romāṇi neñcati; Pali equivalent na saṃ lomaṃ pi iñjayuṃ.

(= Pali iñjati, iñjamāna), moves, stirs (intrans.); caus. iñjayati, moves, disturbs (trans.); frequently spelled in mss. and edd. iñjya-, also ijya- (esp. in, often kept by, as in anijyamānair indriyaiḥ, but elsewhere, as; he reads with mss. aniñja- in the same cliché); these readings are probably only corruptions, but see s.vv. aniñja, aniñjya, and other forms there referred to: na ceñjate balavān (of Bodhisattva); na ca iñjate bhramati vā (id.); an-iñjamānāś ca (Bodhisattvas); an-iñjamānam (bhikṣum); romaṃ na iṃjeya (opt.), a hair would not be moved (or caus., it would not move a hair; mss. iccheya, but em. proved by); an-iñjamānena kāyena sthito 'niñja- (v.l. 'niñjya-, q.v.) -prāptena ca cittena, and so read (omitting ca; see critical note); an-iñjamānena cittena; an-iñjyamānena (see above; vv.ll. ˚iñja˚, ˚ijya˚) kāyena; an-iñjamānair (text sometimes an-ijya˚, see above) indriyais;;, etc. (in a cliché, see Index); caus., inf., … me te romāpi neñjayituṃ [Page113-b] samarthāḥ syuḥ, they would not be able to move even my hairs; also iñjitum (caus. inf.), na ca samarthā mama romam imjituṃ = (and cf.); cf. s.v. iñjitatva. See also next entries.

, nt., or ˚nā, f. (both = Pali id.; cf. an-i˚, prec., and next), motion, wavering, vacillation (of mind; body; hair, as a very small and delicate part of the body): (vs) na ceñjanaṃ nāpi manyana-pracāraṃ (so read, see s.v. manyanā); (prose) na ca śakitaṃ bhagavato romeñjanam api kartuṃ; (prose) sarveñjana-manyana-(read so with 2d ed.) -spandana-prapañcanāpagatacittam; (vs) na ca tubhya iñjana (could be nt. or f.) … manyana-spandanā na ca prapañcā; (the rest are fem.) (vs) no ca kāyeñjanā (n. sg.); (vs) na sattvasārasya karonti iñjanā (acc. sg.; em. ˚nāṃ); (vs) cittaiñjanā (read as cpd.); (vs) citteñjanā; (vs) sarveñjanā-manyana-vipramuktaḥ; bhāvi tatha abhāve iñjanā nāsti kācit.

(= Pali id.), (1) primarily ppp. of iñjate, q.v.; see iñjita-tva; (2) subst. nt., motion, movement (literal and physical): (vs) prāsādikeʼ iṃjitena (read ijitena;; cf. ijya- forms s.v. iñjate) praviśantāṃ (buddhasya śrāvakān), entering with serene walk; (3) subst. nt., mobility, vacillation, unsteadiness; = iñjana or ˚nā, and like these often associated with manyanā (or manyita), spandita (miswritten sya˚), and other qualities deprecated in religious life: ˚tam = Tib. gyo ba, foll. by syanditam; (vs) varjitvā iñjitā (v.l. ˚tān) manyitāni ca; (prose) iñjita-manyitaprapañcitāni jñāsyati; sarveñjita-manyanāsyandita-vikalpāpagato bhavati; (prose) (-abhiniveśa-, q.v.) -sarveñjitāni … prahīyante; sarvābhiniveśeñjitaprahāṇataś ca. See also an-iñjita.
, nt. (to prec.), state of being moved: (nāpi bodhisattvasya) romasyāpi iñjitatvam, and not so much as a hair of the Bodhisattva was moved.
,, prob. error for iṅgā, q.v.; cf. however aṭṭa.

, adj., commonplace, low, vulgar, = Pali itara and ittara, but also Skt. itara,; hence not a specifically Buddhist word; doubtless specialized semantic development of itara, other: e.g. itara-jātīyāḥ, commonplace, vulgar people. No *ittara has been recorded, but see itvara, which is presumed to be its Skt. original.)

, adj. (= Pali itarītara; the Skt. word not in this sense but only reciprocal, cf.), any sort of, this or that, any at all, miscellaneous, hit-or-miss: netaretareṇa saṃtuṣṭiḥ; ˚reṇa ca piṇḍapātreṇa saṃtuṣṭo bhaveyaṃ; alpecchā itaretarair abhiratā(ḥ), pleased (satisfied) with anything at all; bhavati ca itaretareṇa tuṣṭaḥ.
(nt. or m.), = next (rarely): nidānetivṛtta- (prose), in list of canonical writings.

, nt. (in m.; = ityukta, ˚taka, qq.v., = Pali itivuttaka, which seems clearly based on iti vuttaṃ = ity uktam, but in BHS has been blended formally, by Hypersanskritism, with Skt. itivṛtta, nt., see; Tib., see below, proves that at least for Tib. translators the word was connected with vṛtta rather than ukta), n. of a canonical work or type of literature, story of past events (associated with jātaka): = Tib. (de lta bu) byuṅ ba (-ḥi sde), story, history (root ḥbyuṅ, happen, take place, = vṛt); here itivṛttakam is foll. by jātakam; (vs) sūtrāṇi (or, with v.l., sūtrānta) bhāṣāmi [Page114-a] tathaiva gāthā itivṛttakaṃ jātakam adbhutaṃ ca; (wrongly punctuated) … prakāśayati (comma, or no punctuation) itivṛttakāṃś ca pūrvayogapratisaṃyuktāṃ (= ˚tān; end of sentence!); tathāgataḥ pūrvānte itivṛttakāṃś ca jātakāṃś ca smṛtvā … Cf. vṛttaka.
, nt. (! = Skt. itihāsa, m.), history, story, legend: ˚kam, n. sg. (follows purāṇaṃ; gender influenced by this?).

, nt. (= Pali itthatta), the being in this world: (kṣīṇā me jātir …) noparim itthatvam iti prajānāti. Recorded as icchatva devanikāyato cyavitvā icchatvam āgacchanti, and in similar phrases;;. allows icchatva to stand, regarding it as a genuine phonetic alternative form (); and all mss. read so in these passages. But in view of it seems to me likely that icchatva is a mere graphic corruption,. See however icchatva.
(nt.), cited by, and; not noted in texts; = next.

(nt.; cf. prec.; = itivṛttaka, q.v.; a more historical Sktization of Pali itivuttaka), sayings (sc. of the Buddha), n. of a canonical work or type of literature: gāthoddānanidānatyuktaka- (read ˚nidānetyuktaka-)-jātaka-.

, adj. (= Pali ittara; Skt. Lex., rare and late in lit., see; cf. itara, which in Pali is commonly treated as the same word but seems to be unrelated in origin; possibly secondary blending has occurred between the two words), slight, small, trivial, unimportant; brief, momentary (of time): ˚ram (n. sg.); ˚raṃ khu ayaṃ tāpo, this (sunʼs) heat is a trivial thing; (vs) kiṃ tasyābharaṇebhir (so, as one word) itvaraiḥ, what need has he of trivial (ordinary, worthless) ornaments?; asāram itvaraṃ ca lokam (acc. sg.); mahākāruṇyacittotpādenetvareṇa kāmopasanihitena, by an impulse of pity, tho vile (? better trivial, slight), and full of desire (); of virtue, merit, etc., itvara-guṇa-saṃtuṣṭair, satisfied with slight virtues; (vs) itvarapuṇya devamanujā; itvara-kuśalamūlānāṃ devamanuṣyāṇāṃ (of those who do not follow the Mahāyāna); itvara-kuśalamūlāḥ; of time, itvarakālābhyāsāt (short), contrasted with dīrghakālābhyāsāt line 3; vijñāyate netvaradarśanena = Pali (momentary, fleeting glance); of gifts, kiṃ punar me itvareṇa dānena pradattena.
, adj. (= Pali idappaccaya, e.g.), having this (or that) as its cause: … gambhīredaṃpratyayānubodhanena pratyekabuddhayānaṃ saṃvartayanti.

(= Pali idappaccayatā; abstr. from prec.), state of having this (or that) as its cause; generally in comp. with pratītya-samutpāda, dependent origination owing to the state of (etc.); so also the Pali equivalent is usually cpd. with paṭiccasamuppāda (or ˚panna), tho the editions wrongly separate the words, as in : idaṃpratyayatā-pratītyasamutpādam;;; ˚pādena; ˚pādānulomāḥ.
(MIndic for ˚nīm; cf. dāni), now: (vs, m.c.); (vs, m.c.; v.l. idānī, unmetr.)
(= Pali-Pkt. id.; MIndic for ṛddhi), magic power: (vs; read) marūṇa rājā vaśir iddhiprāpto (or perhaps vaśi riddhi˚, see this; text divides wrongly, va śiriddhi˚).
, adv. (= Pali id., Skt. iha,), here: (all mss. but one); (4 of 6 mss.); (no v.l.).

, m. (1) as in Pali (Sakko devānaṃ indo), the deva who in Skt. is named Indra (but frequently also [Page114-b] called Śakra) is in BHS often called Śakra, devānām indra, Śakra king of the gods, the word indra being clearly a common, not a proper, noun; so;;; etc., passim; this is specially clear when the n. pr. Śakra is omitted but the gen. devānām retained, as in devānām indra, O king of the gods! (2) a high number: indraḥ = Tib. dbaṅ po, lord (regularly = indra); (3) n. of a yakṣa:;; (4) n. of a brahman:; (5) n. of a king:.
(= Pali -indaka), at end of Bhvr. cpds., = indra (either as n. pr. or in the sense of lord, king): (vs) devadānavagaṇāḥ sa-indrakāḥ; (vs) devāḥ sa-indrakās; (prose) sendrakā devā.

, m. (= Pali inda˚, also ˚khīla; not recorded in this sense in Skt., where it appears to mean bar, bolt to a gate or door; AMg. indakhīla, said to mean a portion of a city gate; a door bolt …,; qy: was the ‘bolt’ fastened under the door, in the pavement? cf.), threshold slab, a stone imbedded in the ground at the entrance to a city gate, or to a palace, house, or apartment: ˚laḥ = Tib. ḥkor gtan, lit. circle bar, or Tib. sgoḥi them pa, threshold of a door; cites both these Tib. phrases as synonymous renderings of indrakīla, and defines them as steps at the threshold or at the entrance of a house; cf., three indrakīlas, viz. nagare indrakīlo, rājakule …, and antaḥpure …, thresholds to a city, a royal palace, and a harem; this passage is a comm. on (yaḥ … bhikṣur …) rājñaḥ … indrakīlaṃ vā indrakīla-sāmantaṃ vā samatikrāmed, if any monk crosses a kingʼs threshold or its environs; generally referred to as located at a city gate; in entering the city one steps upon it: samanantaraṃ indrakīlaṃ pādena cokramati (= ca-avakr˚), and as soon as he (Buddha, entering a city) stepped on the i˚ with his foot; (Bhagavatā) sābhisaṃskāra (q.v.) indrakīle pādo vyavasthāpitaḥ (in entering a city); (Buddhā …) indrakīle pādau vyavasthāpayanti (in entering a city by the gate); yadā ca bhagavatā indrakīle pādo nyastaḥ (in entering a city; the gate is not mentioned); rājadhānīṃ praviśata indrakīlam ākrāmataḥ, as (a Buddha) was entering the capital, as he stepped upon the threshold (pres. pples., gen. sg.); (vs) so indrakīle (mss. ˚kīlo) sthita, standing on the threshold, apparently of the city (rājadhānī) mentioned line 2; used in comparisons as type of immobility, recommended in religious life: yathendrakīlo pṛthivīsaṃniśrito syā … asaṃprakampi, as an i˚ should be fixed in the earth, (so …) immovable; indrakīlopamā; in this sense applied to the mind or thoughts of a Buddha or Bodhisattva, and (Bodhisattvas) indrakīlopamacittatāṃ ca anuprāpnuvanti; indrakīlopamacittā (of Buddha); bhagavān … indrakīla iva (here physically and literally motionless, like a threshold-stone) tasmin pradeśe sthitaḥ.
, m. = prec., q.v.: (prose) teṣāṃ … dvārāṇāṃ caturṇāṃ varṇānāṃ indrakīlakā abhunsu, these gates (of a city) had threshold-stones of four colors.
, n. of a brother of Kuśa:.
, (1) n. of a samādhi: (not in); (2) n. of a former Buddha:; (3) n. of a yakṣa:.
, n. of a Buddha:; (the same?) of a Buddha in the zenith:.

, in comp. with śiras or śīrṣa(n), redheaded, said of (miraculous) elephants: (prose) indragopaka-śirāḥ, n. sg., of the Bodhisattva in the form of a small elephant, about to enter his motherʼs womb (in vs line 7 replaced by suraktaśīrṣaḥ); (prose) indragopa-śīrṣam, of another magically created [Page115-a] elephant. The words ˚pa and ˚paka denote a red insect in Skt. and Pali; acc. to the cochineal insect.
, n. of a capital of the former Buddha Indradhvaja:
, n. of a former Buddha: ˚jaḥ, n. sg.
, n. of a ‘virtuous man’ (satpuruṣa, q.v.):.
, (1) n. of various former Buddhas:; (with capital Indratapanā);; 84,000 former Buddhas of this name,;; a Buddha in the southwest quarter,; (2) n. of a nāga:.
, n. of a Tathāgata:; same as Candradhvajaśrīketu.

, nt., acc. to, Luftgewand, so v.a. Nacktheit: ˚ṭaṃ śvetapaṭaṃ dhyuṣitapaṭaṃ; but can indra- have this mg. (= sky, air, as in digambara)? I find no basis for the theory. All the context shows is that persons dressed in these garbs should not be consecrated (dīkṣ). What the garb of Indra (? of a prince) means is not clear. It is true that śveta-paṭa is recorded as used of the Jain sect otherwise called śvetāmbara; doubtless this was the reason for Boehtlingkʼs conjecture, based on the assumption that this word equals digambara; but I doubt that this is sufficient to support it. That a real sort of cloth is meant is suggested by nānā-paṭeṣu, line 6.

, f. (nowhere recorded in this sense, which = Skt. indra-cāpa etc.), (1) rainbow: (vs) ke cāgatā vimalaketu yathendrayaṣṭyaḥ, bright-colored as rainbows; (vs) yatha naru iha indrayaṣṭi (Tib. ḥjaḥ, rainbow) dṛṣṭvā vimṛśati aṅgaśu (= ˚śas) niḥsvabhāva śūnyam; (2) n. of a nāga:.
, as n. of a mountain, recorded in, only as Buddhist, but occurs in Skt., see; noted by me in; and see next.)
, n. of a locality (cf. prec.): ˚guhā, n. sg.
, (1) m., n. of a Buddha: (vs) ˚śiri, n. sg.; but see s.v. Citrārtha; (2) m., n. of a Bodhisattva: ˚śriyo, gen. sg.; (3) f., n. of a gandharva maid:.

, m. (˚taḥ, n. sg.),, or ˚stā, f. (n. sg.),; Tib. in both dbaṅ poḥi lag (pa), a literal rendering of the Skt., which says means ‘a plant the viscid aromatic root of which resembles the human arm in shape’; in both and one item in lists of herbs, oṣadhi (auṣadhayo, n. pl.). has other Tib. renderings, apparently foreign words and not in Dictt., ḥab śaṅ tse ḥu (which also renders prativiṣam,) and ḥa ba śa tshe ḥu.

, (1) nt. (Pali also uses the word of this group, see s.v., B, Nos. 15—19), one of the five moral faculties (śraddhā, vīrya, smṛti, samādhi, prajñā), to which correspond five powers (bala) with the same names: listed; (and cf.,);; each treated as a dharmālokamukha,; mentioned, with balas, but not listed,;; (2) a high number, sattvendriyasya.
, loc. sg. of idam, = iha, here; repeatedly in, e.g.;; see.

, adj., of such an extent, so great, or (here) so small: (prose) tad yathā sa ekavindur iyaṃtataḥ sa prathamasaṃnipāto (see saṃnipāta) 'bhūt. Could this be an error for iyantaḥ = Skt. iyān, n. sg. m. of iyant? But I have not noted such MIndic morphology in the prose of. Emendation to iyattakaḥ (Vedic only and rare) is not attractive.
, adj., having torments to this extent (iyaṃ for Skt. iyat, see):; ˚khā hi bhikṣavo nārakāḥ (or narakāḥ).
, n. pl. pres. pple. = Skt. īrayantaḥ (), setting in motion: (vs) paripācayanti jagu dharmaprabhām iranta (imu …) Cf. iryati.

(= Pali iriyati; cf. Vedic īrte), wanders: vanād vanaṃ iryasi (so mss., em. īr˚) caṃkramanto. The ya-present formation is doubtless due to influence of the noun iryā (see īryā), commonly in the cpd. īryāpatha or iryā˚.

= Skt. īrṣyā, jealousy: all mss. at;. would em. to īrṣyā; but this may be only Sktization of semi-MIndic ir˚, cf. iryā- etc. As notes, irṣyā is found as v.l. in some mss. of (;, four of six mss.;;); tho in all these cases at least one ms. has īr˚, the form ir˚ may have been original.
, n. of a devakumārikā in the northern quarter: =.
, n. of a nāga: (but Īśā˚); Tib. gśol madaḥ ḥdzin, plow-holder (implying Īṣā˚).
, m., n. of one of the seven mountains (or mountain ranges) surrounding Sumeru, = Īṣādhara, q.v.; read so at where the only ms. reads iyaṃdharā (em. iṣāṃdharo).
, m., n. of a region, in the south: dakṣiṇāpatha ˚ṇo nāma janapadas;.
, v.l. in for Īṣādhara, q.v., n. of a mountain. See also Īṣādhāra (2).

, nt., or iṣikā, f. (perhaps also iṣīka, nt.; cf. Pali esika, ˚kā, interpreted in Dictt. as pillar, post), signpost: iṣikā māpitā bhavanti (Tib. śiṅ-rtags, tree (or wood) sign; Chin. app. sign-post or the like): and dvārāṇāṃ purato iṣikāni ( iṣī˚, v.l. iṣi˚) māpitāni abhūnsuḥ; iṣikā-padaṃ vā dadyāt, or should present a sign-post (at the caitya of a past Buddha, marking the holy spot; otherwise but implausibly).

(= Pali Isi˚; semi-MIndic for Ṛṣidatta, q.v., also Riṣi˚), n. of a sthapati of King Prasenajit of Śrāvastī (Kosala):;, in both read, substantially with mss., (gṛhapatir) Iṣidattaḥ Purāṇaḥ sthapatī (dual).
, nt. (in Skt. only m., f.), arrow: and 5 iṣu kṣiptaṃ (n. sg.).
, m. pl., n. of a brahmanical gotra:.
(cf. AMg. iṭṭā, with non-aspirate, beside iṭṭayā = Skt. iṣṭakā), brick: (vs) iṣṭā-mayā (ed. em. ˚yān) … stūpān. Perhaps loss of suffixal ka m.c.;.

(= iṣṭī, istrikā, istrī, iṣṭiyā, all semi-MIndic forms of strī; for i- see; cf. Pali itthikā, AMg. itthiyā, etc.; no MIndic *iṭṭhī or *iṭṭhikā, with domal stops, seems recorded), woman: (vs) puruṣaiṣṭika- (m.c. for ˚kā-)dārakāś ca; (vs) iṣṭikān (acc. [Page116-a] pl.) evam āha; (prose) iṣṭikāye (gen. sg.), v.l. for text istrikāye; (vs) iṣṭikāsu (no v.l.).

, v.l. for text istriyā and ˚yo at, see s.v. istrī. If iṣṭiyā is correct, it corresponds to iṣṭī, q.v., as striyā (n. sg.), q.v., does to strī. It would be n. sg. (while istriyo, at least, is n. pl.).

(Pali itthi, itthī), = iṣṭikā, istrī, qq.v., woman: (vs) ye ca iṣṭidārakā suduḥkhitā (wrongly ˚dārakāsu duḥ˚), and what women and boys …; (vs), perhaps read ima iṣṭi˚, cf. ms. A imeṣṭikāmaratiṃ (= imām plus iṣṭi˚), for ima istri˚; (vs) iṣṭibhāvaṃ, state of (existence as) a woman; other instances as v.l. for forms of istrī, q.v.
(= Skt. icchati; acc. to, used in certain cpds. E +), seeks: (na) mama … kiṃcid evam iṣye (1 sg.); (vs) yadi tvaṃ prītim iṣyasi.
= istrī, istri, q.v., woman: (vs) [Page116-b] istrika (n. pl., or stem in comp. with foll.) dārakāś ca; (prose) istrikāye (v.l. iṣṭikāye), gen. sg.

(= Aśokan id. [, ]; Skt. strī; see s.v. iṣṭikā, iṣṭī), woman:;;;; (istriya gen. pl., = striyām);;;;;;; all the prec. vss; (prose) istriyā (instr. sg.; v.l. iṣṭiyā) sma parājitā, na ca kahiṃcit istriyo (n. pl.; v.l. iṣṭiyā, q.v.) rājā, sarvatra puruṣo (˚ṣā) rājā; istriye (instr. sg., v.l. iṣṭiye); istrī-(v.l. iṣṭī-)sahasraiḥ; istriye (oblique case); istrīhi (instr. pl.); (vs) istriṇāṃ (gen. pl.); (vs) istri-koṭi; (vs) istri-gaṇaś ca.
, adv. (iha plus the suffix of amutra, which is the next word in; cf. AMg. ihaiṃ, from iha plus another loc. ending), here, in this world: (foll. by amutra).
, f. ˚kī, adj. (cf. Skt. īdṛśaka; no form in ˚ika seems recorded), such: (vs) kriyām īdṛśikīm (no v.l.).

(chiefly the latter, semi-MIndic, has been noted; = Pali and AMg. iriyā) = the much commoner īryā-patha (or iryā˚), deportment, behavior, particularly good, dignified, proper deportment: iryaṃ (mss., īryāṃ) paśyitvā (of a Pratyekabuddha); (kalyāṇā) punar iyaṃ pravrajitasya iryā (īryā); iryā (īryā); (vs) teṣa (gods) yathā ca iryā; (vs) yatha irya netra vimalāprabha, since he possesses proper deportment and an eye of pure splendor (so better than taking irya-netra as cpd. with); (vs) īryāṃ (no v.l. in mss.) caryāṃ ca prekṣate, he (Bodhisattva) regards (considers duly) proper deportment and conduct; (prose) tayā īryayā caryayā.

, m. (= Pali iriyā-patha, AMg. iriyāvaha; in mss., esp. of and, often written iryā˚ or iryyā˚, semi-MIndic, which usually keeps but emends to īryā˚; once, at least, iriyā-patha, as in Pali,, prose, kept by; also airyāpatha, q.v.; see prec. and next), much commoner than the synonymous īryā, (1) movement (of physical movements of any sort): (prose) chinna-iryāpathā (all mss., em. ˚īryā˚) gacchanti (mss. gacchati), sinners in hell, confined in huts (gharakehi oruddhā), go with (freedom of) movement cut off, i.e. suffer restraint of movement (but possibly more specifically, suffer restraint of posture, see 4 below, e.g. are not allowed to sit or lie down); (2) applied to any particular course of religious, esp. ascetic, performance, and specifically to disapproved ascetic practices of heretics, such as the ‘five-fire’ practice (mentioned in the prec.): (sa) teṣāṃ-teṣām (of heretical ascetics) īryāpathān vikopayitum ārabdhaḥ; (3) generally less specific, behavior, deportment, good or bad, of people in general; but esp. of the approved deportment of pious Buddhists, of monks, or of Bodhisattvas or Buddhas; most commonly with favorable implication; but this may be made clear by an adjective, esp. prāsādika, gracious, (religiously) attractive: prāsādikena īryāpathena (v.l. iryyā˚), of a Pratyeka-buddha; in prāsādika and aprāsādika īryā˚, good and bad deportment, contrasted; śānteneryāpathena, [Page116-1b] of Mahākāśyapa; praśānteryāpathaḥ, and 19 sarveryāpathacaryāviśeṣasamanvāgataḥ, attended by all excellent deportment and behavior, of the Tathāgata; creatures in general vary in deportment, yathādhimukta-sattveryāpatha- (v.l. cited ˚iryyā˚)-saṃdarśanāya; sarvasattvādhimuktisamair īryāpathaiḥ; specifically good deportment, (vs) ˚pathaṃ yo mama rakṣamāṇo bhaveta bhikṣū …; (vs) iryāpathe-ṣṭhā, abiding in …; (bodhisattvo … sarvāntaḥpurasya …) īryāpatham upadarśya, having displayed proper behavior to all the harem (so Tib.); īryāpathebhyaś (most mss. iry˚) cyutāḥ, fallen away from right behavior; tathāgateryāpathacaryācāritrānugato; (prose) iriyāpathasaṃpanno, perfect in deportment, of a monk; (vs) īryāpathena su-upeta (with mss.) satvā, (there are no evil-doers here;) creatures are well endowed with proper deportment; (corrupt); (vs) īryāpathe (3 mss. iry˚) ca vīrye ca dhyāne jñāne śame dame; iryāpathe (so mss.) ca vīrye ca dhyāne jñāne tathaiva ca; often it is said that a newly-initiated person (of superior character) shows the īryāpatha, deportment, of a monk of long standing, tad yathāpi nāma varṣaśatopapannasya bhikṣor īryāpathaḥ saṃvṛtto 'bhūt; iryāpatho (em. īry˚) sānaṃ saṃsthihe sayyathāpi nāma varṣaśatopasaṃpannānāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ; similarly; (iryā instead of iryāpatho);;;;; (varṣaśatopasaṃpannasya) bhikṣor īryāpathenāvasthitaḥ; (dvādaśavarṣopasaṃpannasyeva) bhikṣor īryāpathena … avasthitaḥ; (4) as in Pali iriyāpatha, also used of four postures or bodily attitudes, that is modes of physical behavior, viz. walking, standing, sitting, and lying down: vihāyasābhyudgamya caturvidham īryāpathaṃ kalpayati, mounting in the air, displays the four … (one of the abhijñākarmāṇi); (vs) īryāpathāṃ (3 mss. iry˚) darśayanti catvāraḥ puruṣottamāḥ, no ca pariśramas teṣāṃ …, Buddhas display the four modes of behavior (like other men), and yet they are never weary (i.e. do not need to sit or lie down); dvābhyām everyāpathābhyāṃ sthitvā, sthānena caṅkrameṇa ca (only standing and walking; he vows not to sit or lie down) kālam atināmayeyaṃ, repeated (var.), which is cited dvābhyām everyāpathābhyāṃ …;, īryāpatha repeatedly of physical movements (walking, standing, and sitting, line 22) of ordinary (not [Page117-a] religious) men; caturīryāpatha-vinayanopavana- (so read, text ˚naupavana-)-suvardhita-taror (Tib. lus, body, for -taror, implying -tanor), (of the Bodhisattva) who possessed a ‘tree’ (body?) well-raised in the grove of (by?) exercise of the four modes of behavior; (ṣaḍvarṣā bodhisattvo yathā niṣaṇṇa evāsthāt paryaṅkena) na ca īryāpathāc (all mss. ca iry˚ or cery˚) cyavate sma, and did not abandon the posture (of sitting cross-legged); (here mss. iry˚) = (vs) īryāpathaṃ … sarvābhibhuno (mss. ˚to) na vijahante (i.e. they walk and stand still when he does, see prec. line); only three, tribhir īryāpathair … sthānena caṅkrameṇa niṣadyayā.

, cpd. with -pāda (or -caraṇa), (= Pali ussaṅkha-pāda,) ep. of a mahā-puruṣa [Page118-b] (esp. Buddha), no. 7 of the 32 lakṣaṇa; orig. form, etym., and mg. obscure; acc. to Pali it means that the soles of the feet can be seen as they walk, because ‘the ankles are fixed high’; if from utsaṅga, having feet characterized by a ‘lap’ (an up-curve under the foot, making the sole visible?). Tib. on says having the ankle-bone (or, joint of the ankle-bone) not visible (so one Chin. version, and Jap.); but Tib. on, cited by, having feet not uneven; another Chin. gloss (also cited in, and elsewhere, infra) refers the epithet to the knees; glosses suvyaktaparamopaśobhitopari-pādacchavikusumagarbhātirekaprabhāsvarā (not very clear or specific). These northern interpretations make the impression of floundering in a morass of ignorance. See,. Forms: utsaṅga-pāda (but ucchaṅkha-);; (v.l. utsaṅkha-); utsaṅga-caraṇa;;;; ucchaṅga-pāda; ucchaṅkha-pāda, (see above);;; (the mss. clearly intend this all three times! correct ʼs text); (note also v.l. utsaṅkha- in, above). This form ucchaṅkha is closest to the Pali; the very obscurity of its etymology may argue for its originality.

, (1) (= Pali ussada; = ucchādana, q.v.), shampooing, rubbing down: ucchada-snapanaparimardana-bhedana-vikiraṇa-vidhvaṃsana-dharmaḥ (of the body); (2) in -sāntarocchada-paṭikobhayakṛtopadhāneṣu paryaṅkeṣu śayitvā; app. understand ucchada as some kind of cloth (cf. ucchadaka); but the preceding sāntara, which certainly goes closely with what follows it, is hard to interpret on that theory, and suggests em. to sāntarottara (q.v.), a cpd. known to Pali; it might mean here … having cushions made on both sides with woolen cloths inside and outside; (3) in ʼs em. is certainly wrong. The ms. is quoted as prāptaucchadakāyaś ca; certainly ucchada = utsada (1), Pali ussada, elevation on the 7 parts of the body which show this feature in a mahāpuruṣa; Tib. mtho ba confirms this. Acc. to, Tib. has mdun, fore-part, before that word; but surely Tib. read, or intended, bdun, seven, and we must read sapto- for prāptau-; the cpd. means with a body possessing the 7 high places or protuberances (see under utsada (1), and cf. saptotsadakāyaḥ). —Add to (2): my suggestion on is made dubious by sottarocchadapaṭa (ms.; ed. em. sottaracch˚), adj., and 69.

(= Pali id., also Skt., but see below), [Page119-a] in and, ucchādana-(in em. āchādana-)-parimardana-svapna- ( supana-)bhedana-vikiraṇa-vidhvaṃsana-dharma, ep. of the body; corresp. to Pali anicc'ucchādana-parimaddana-bhedanaviddhaṃsana-dhammo, e.g., of which I believe the true interpretation was given by,; ucchādana and parimardana are primarily shampooersʼ terms, shampooing and rubbing down (so Skt.), but with double entente (not recognized in Pali comms.) also destruction and wiping out; suggested that Skt. ucchādana was MIndic for utsādana, which means both rubbing down and destruction; Skt. śātayati, cuts off, destroys (n. act. śātana), and root śad-, fall (n. act. śādana, das Ausfallen), may also be concerned, at least in part; see śatana, used in a cpd. very similar to that of above; parimardana is noted in Skt. and MIndic only of shampooing (so also), but the verb Skt parimardati means also crushes, destroys. In ucchada (q.v.) must have been limited to its shampooersʼ mg., since snapana follows. But in some BHS texts śatana, q.v., is substituted, eliminating that mg. and bringing in exclusively what I (with) regard as the secondary, punning mg. of the Pali cpd. renders {{erasion->erosion||20210831||https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/80|}}, abrasion, admitting that the pun is untranslatable. In American gangstersʼ jargon, to rub out means to obliterate, kill. We might render : (the body) which is characterized by rubbing down (‘off’), wiping away (‘out’), sleep (or dreams, often symbol of impermanence; here, too, a sort of word-play), breaking up, scattering, destruction.

(= Pali ussāpeti; ucchrāpaya, isolated; caus. to ud plus śri; see also ucchrāyayati, ucchrepayati), raises, sets up: (vs) prākāra ucchrāpitā(ḥ); (vs) ucchrāpita-dharmadhvajā; patākān ucchrāpayanti; (vs) (dhvajāna koṭīnayutāsahasrā) ucchrāpayetsu (aor.); patākāḥ … ucchrāpitā(ḥ).
(caus. to ud plus śri; = ucchrāpayati, q.v.), raises, sets up: (yaṣṭir) ucchrāyitā;; śarīrasaṃghāta ucchrāyitaḥ (in; ed. em. ucchrāpi˚).
(nt.; nom. act. to next), the lifting up: (bhaiṣajyaṃ ca) dattvā vyādhy-avanatocchrepanān mātrāśī ca …

(= ucchrāpayati, q.v.; cf. prec.; on form see), raises, sets up: ˚pitaṃ vaijayantāsamaṃ; ˚pito dharmadhvaja(ḥ); (vs) ˚payasva mahadharmayūpaṃ; (vs) ˚paya … tathāgatadhvajaṃ; (prose) ˚paya mahādharmadhvajam; (vs) ˚pitaṃ dharmadhvajam (note in prose ucchrayiṣyasi, v.l. ucchrăpayiṣyasi).

(only Vedic, and not quite in this sense; here perhaps back-formation from ppp. ucita, the only form known in Skt. and MIndic), suits, is pleasing: (prose) tad yuṣmākaṃ kiṃ varam ucyati, so what boon seems good to you?

, some kind of attitude or behavior which monks must avoid in begging food: nojjaṅkikayā (instr.). Tib. ḥjol thabs su (? perhaps with robe dragging, sc. on the ground?); Chin. (here) apparently pulling at clothes while walking; elsewhere, acc. to, Chin. walking on tiptoe, and so Jap. on. The says the ‘correct’ reading would be ujjakṣikā, and, suggests that the corresponding Pali is ujjhaggikā (or rather, by em. ujjagghikā),, which means laughing, derision, see uccagghati; this seems indeed quite possible.

, adj. (= Pali id.; defined by visama, by jaṅgalaṃ, lūkhadhūsaro [Page120-a] anudako bhūmippadeso … jaṅgalato pi ukkaṃsena jaṅgalaṃ, on), desert, waste (land): ˚le pṛthivīpradeśe; (pṛthivīpradeśā ya) ūṣarā ujjaṅgalā(ḥ); (vss) ujjaṅgalo ca jaṅgalo (,, treats ujj˚ as n. pr.).

, pres. pple. (cf. Skt. Gr. ujjighra; otherwise no form of ud plus ghrā seems to be recorded), sniffing, smelling (at food): nojjighrantaḥ piṇḍapātaṃ paribhokṣyāmaḥ. (Same passage cited from a,, top.)
(mss. mostly Ujita˚; Ujjhita˚, which seems implausible), n. of a former Buddha:.

, adj. (= Pali id., beside uju; Skt. ṛju; cf. next, ṛjju, and anujjuka), straight, right; usually in vss where jj could be m.c., but once in prose in ujjucittā; the rest in vss: ˚gateṣu; ujju karitva kāyaṃ; ujju-bhraṣṭā; sadojjupraṣṭho (so read; = sadā ujju˚).
(= prec., q.v.; also ṛjuka; Pali id., beside ujuka): (vs) dṛṣṭiṃ kurvāmi ujjukām; in ms. Ḱ indicates ujjuka for text -rjuka (ṛj˚).
, n. of a king: (prose); called Toṇehāra (vs).
, ifc. Bhvr. (to *ujñā = Pali uññā for Skt. avajñā; see), contempt, in a-śaṭh'-ūjñakāś ca (ū may be in saṃdhi for a-u), free from deceitfulness and contempt:.

, some kind of attitude or behavior which monks must avoid in begging food: noṭṭaṅkikayā (instr.). Tib. braṅ bas (? braṅ breast; also dwelling); Chin. (here), perhaps walking with the palm of the foot (? or, with hands touching the feet?); acc. to, another Chin. renders limping (das Hinken); Jap. squatting (at the entrance of a house).
(m. or nt.; = AMg. id., Skt. uṭaja), hut: ekānte uḍayaṃ kṛtvā prativastavyam;;;;;;;.
(or oḍi˚?), only in gūthoḍi˚, q.v. See,, where Dravidian origin is suggested: Telugu oḍagala-vādu (= Hindi -wāla), sweeper (in the Indian sense, cleaner of toilets); Tamil oḍugāl, conduite dʼeau.
, in ˚ra-dharma-vihāriṇam (acc. sg.),, cf. (from Ratnarāśi Sūtra), conjecturally rendered (practising) heretical (principles).

,, is prob. a mere corruption: yo rāgam utacchiyam aśeṣaṃ = Pali, yo rāgam udacchidā asesaṃ, who has cut off passion without remainder. If a substitute for ud-acchidat is intended (which should end in a long syllable; ˚yaṃ?), it would seem to show t for d (by hyper-Sktism?) and y for the second d (Pktic). I do not understand ʼs note.
, m.c. for Skt. utta˚, glowing etc.: utapta; ˚ta-vatī (= uttap˚ 7, where meter also requires uta˚).
, onomat., a sound said to be uttered exceptionally by a tittira bird; see;. (Tib. says only a different sound.)
, adj. (in Skt. rare and doubtful in mg.), with hair standing up:;; (see s.v. prakaca).

, m., nt., or ˚ṭā, f., n. of a town (droṇamukha, ˚khya, q.v.): ˚ṭo nāma droṇamukham; ˚ṭaṃ nāma droṇa˚ (acc.), 28 utkaṭadroṇamukhyaṃ; yenotkaṭaṃ droṇamukhaṃ (nom., nt.), 19 ˚ṭān [Page120-b] (abl.); fem. ˚tāṃ nāma droṇamukhaṃ (acc.), ˚ṭā 26. From a verbally close Pali parallel it appears that the town called in Pali Ukkaṭṭhā (see) is the same; see Puṣkarasārin.

(see s.v. kaṭṭati), takes out: yamalakāto (see yamalaka) modakaṃ ukkaṭṭetvā; taṃ bhāṇḍaṃ sarvaṃ ukkaṭṭitaṃ (sc. from a river); in read mama hṛdayo udumbare utkaṭṭito sthapito (with one ms. utkaṇṭhito, v.l. utkarito; in the other two passages above em. ukkaḍḍh-).

, and ppp. utkaṇṭhita (cf. next; in Skt. only longs for; longing; but Pali ukkaṇṭhati also is annoyed, ˚ṭhita annoyed), is annoyed; annoyed; the ppp. in rājā śrutvā utkaṇṭhito evaṃ jāto, the king, hearing (this), became annoyed, as follows (here certainly not desirous!); similarly so utkaṇṭhito (context makes desirous impossible). In (tair bodhisattvaḥ lūhaiḥ stokair asatkṛtya dhandhaṃ) ca labdhair notkaṇṭhyate na paritasyati, prob. is not made annoyed (pass. of caus.). There may be other cases; many are ambiguous.
(see prec.; Pali ukkaṇṭhā), possibly annoyance, mental distress:, see s.v. paritasana.

, n. of a merchant: tatrānyataraś cotkariko nāma baṇig … Cf. Otkarika (the same person as Utk˚). There seems to be no reason to connect this n. pr. with aukarika (okkarika), qq.v., as has been assumed by, (on, s.v. okkarika) and. But perhaps we should read cautk˚ in and assume Otk˚ as the name.

(nt.), ˚ṇā, and ˚ṇa-tā (= Pali (att-)ukkaṃsana, ˚nā; cf. next), praise, laudation, exaltation (regularly of oneself, or oneʼs own): ātmānutkarṣaṇa-tā (i.e. ātma-an-utk˚); (vs) ātmotkarṣaṇi (loc.); (prose) ātmaśīlotkarṣaṇā; ātmotkarṣaṇā; svapakṣotkarṣaṇa-(vacana).

(cf. prec.; not in this sense Skt.; = Pali ukkaṃsati, ˚seti), exalts, i.e. praises: gdve., sacec cañcalendriyo (rājā) bhavati, utkarṣayitavyaṃ (sc. bhikṣuṇā), if (the king) is flighty (unstable), praise must be bestowed (saying: It is very meritorious on your part that your kingdom contains so many worthy monks and brahmans who live undisturbed by thieves etc.). Acc. to, Tib. has bstan par bya ḥo, and accordingly renders ‘the Brother should admonish him’ (more exactly, the Tib. means elucidate, make intelligible). But I do not see how the BHS word can mean this. The mg. of the Pali word is appropriate here; by encouraging flattery the king is to be strengthened in a good course.

, m., the expression evam: = Tib. de bzhin no zhes bya ba (Chin. similarly). There is a var. udgārikaḥ (cf. Skt. udgāra, sound, utterance?), but utkā˚ without v.l. I do not understand the etym. (ut-kṛ, ˚karoti, or ˚kirati?).
(˚rayati, ˚rati?), ger. ˚ritvā, having emptied: (prose) (bhājanāni …) pūretvā utkāritvā, having filled and emptied the pots. The mg. is clear; etym.? to utkirati? em. utkiritvā, without good reason.

, m., see next. Perhaps utkāśaḥ, alone, is to be read in this sense for text utkāsaḥ in (prose); after a Tathāgataʼs parinirvāṇa, by a follower of his, udvegasaṃjananārthaṃ dhārmika utkāsaḥ (i.e. ˚śaḥ?) kṛto 'bhūt: aho bateyaṃ … mahādharmolkāntardhāsyatīti saṃvegajananīyā kathā kṛtā. But cf. utkāsa.
, m. (ud plus kāś; cf. next), conspicuous, vigorous pronouncement (so Tib. on):; bhagavatotkāśaśabdaḥ kṛtaḥ … parivrājako (26) bhagavata utkāśanaśabdaṃ śuśrāva; also 27.
, m. = prec., q.v.:. See also utkāśa, m., perhaps used in this same sense.

, (1) (m.), clearing of the throat (= Skt. utkāsana): (vs) utkāsaśabdu napi śrūyati tanmuhūrtaṃ (mss. vary greatly, but Tib. lud paḥi sgra confirms this form and mg.); (2) m. utkāsaḥ, see s.v. utkāśa; if the theory there stated be rejected, the word would have to be classed with (1) and would seem to mean something like hemming and hawing, or rather ominous sound (calling attention to the future disappearance of the dharma), in.
, m. (in Skt. adj., aufhäufend). heap, something thrown or dug up, in mūṣī-utkira, see s.v. mūṣī.

(= Skt.,, also utkīlita; wrongly defined in and for passage in), opens: nagaram (a stronghold of ogresses) utkīlayitvānyatra gacchatha (11 gatvāvasthitāḥ), having opened up the city …; sādhakecchayā utkīlayati mocayati yathāvyavasthāyām upasthāpayati, opens, frees, etc.)

(? reading stated in note to be ‘not clear’; cf. utkuṭuka?), seems to designate some kind of entertainer: (vs; after naṭa-nartaka jhallaka-mallāḥ) utkuṭa-śobhika-hāraka (qq.v.) … (Tib. cited as bzhugs; not clear to me.)
(cf. prec. and next), lit. remaining in a squatting position(?), designation of certain ascetics, app. Ājīvikas (cf. note in ed., and): ˚yina ekacarāṇāṃ.

, adj. (cf. utkuṭa-; acc. to, occurs in Skt. (Suśruta) only as utkaṭuka or utkuṭaka; the Pali form is app. only ukkuṭika; AMg. usually ukkuḍua, ˚ḍuga, ˚ḍuyā, but also ukkaḍuya), squatting on the heels (see s.v. ukkuṭika for detailed description); as adj. applied to persons, to postures, also in comp. either adjectivally or adverbially; adv. utkuṭukaṃ(?), ˚kena, in squatting posture: ˚kā niṣaṇṇā (n. sg. f.); ˚kāṃ niṣādayitvā having made her sit squatting, but in 10b.3 ˚ṭukena niṣadya, sitting in a squatting posture (adv.); in 10a.4 ˚ṭukăṃ niṣādya, in sense = 16a.1, ˚kaṃ either adv., or MIndic (or corruption?) for ˚kāṃ; ˚kena adv. also (na …) bodhisattvā mātuḥ kukṣigatā utkuṭukena (so read, ˚ṭakena, mss. utkutumbakeṇa) pārśvena vā yathā kathaṃcid vā sthitā bhavanti (but paryaṅkam ābhuṃjitvā); in; situation is the same, but adj. is used, na utkuṭuko (so with both mss.; in ˚ṭiko, but one ms. has -uko); in cpds., ˚kāsanam, Tib. tsog tsog por; ˚ka-sthaḥ, Tib. cog (read tsog) bur; see next; ˚ka-prahāṇam (see this), an ascetic exercise, = Pali ukkuṭika-(p)padhānaṃ, (vs) = = Pali; ˚ka-sthaṇḍila-śayanaiś ca, and by sleeping in a squatting posture or on bare ground; (vs) utkuṭuka-dhyāyi (so read with best mss., metr. superior to ʼs reading utkuṭa-dh˚), meditating in a squatting posture; ˚ṭuka-sthitena, adv., while sitting in a squatting posture,;.
(to prec.), squatting posture: notkuṭukikayā (instr.); Tib. rtsog (read tsog?) bus ma yin. (and record tsog pu, squatting; the tsog pu or ˚bu; see prec.)
, caus. (to Pali denom. ukkujjati), causes to be set (right side) up: ˚yiṣyatha.

, prob. rears (of a balky horse; so guessed from context): (yatra …) aśva(ḥ) skhalati utkumbhati vā khaḍunka- (q.v.)-kriyā vā karoti, when a horse stumbles or rears or acts viciously. Tib. seems to have no correspondent for this word; the several Chin. versions, likewise, fail to clarify it; they seem to have only two verbal expressions for three of the BHS.

, adj., high, rising; only with nikūla, low, [Page121-b] descending, and usually in cpd. utkūla-nikūla (cf. Pali ukkūla-vikūla, interpreted as high and low,), high and low, hence uneven: ˚lam, and nikūlam (the Tib. definitions, śaṅ ṅam śoṅ, ḥbar ḥbur ram mtho dman, seem to refer confusedly to the pair of words together, and mean uneven, high-and-low); utkūlanikūlāś ca pṛthivīpradeśāḥ samāḥ samavasthitāḥ, and the high-and-low (uneven) places became even; utkūla-nikūla-sama-karacaraṇa-gatiḥ (of the Bodhisattvaʼs gait), … making even places that were uneven; (as an ādīnava). The cpd. utkūla-nikūla occurs, where it is unexplained in comm. and not definable by context; utkūla occurs once or twice besides; nikūla is hardly recorded otherwise, and seems to be unknown in MIndic (Pali has vikūla instead, above).
, m., n. of a mountain (= Kūlaka, q.v.):. Cf. preceding.
, adj. (compv. of utkṛṣṭa plus ka), rather superior: (prose) utkṛṣṭatarakebhyo guṇebhyo na vicchandya … nihīnatarakeṣu guṇeṣu samādāpayati.

, prob. cocking or throwing back or up (of the head): notkṛṣṭikayā; Tib. (mgo mi gyog, head not covered; or) mgo mi brdze (= our def.); ˚kā-kṛta, one who has adopted the above attitude: ˚kṛtāya (Tib. only brdzes, or rdzes, pa, as above); ˚kṛtasya (but here Chin. is said to mean qui a la poitrine découverte).

, nt. (see below), or (var. in Kyoto ed.; and without v.l.) khoṭana, nt.: ˚nam. Both form and mg. obscure; occurs between bhikṣupaiśunyam and duṣṭhulārocanam. Tib. skyo sṅogs (var. brṅogs) byed pa, causing quarrels; Chin. disturbing the saṃgha; Jap. raising questions about a matter already decided. The last implies derivation from utkoṭayati, q.v. Skt. has nothing helpful on either reading. Pali ukkoṭana-ka,, means reopening a settled question (wrongly), just as the verb ukkoṭeti seems always so used. But ukkoṭana is defined by as taking bribes (to obstruct justice), which finds support in AMg. ukkoḍā, bribery (), and seems to fit better the Pali occurrences; it is always found in a list of instances of trickery and deceit (typical is ukkoṭana-vañcana-nikati-sāciyogā paṭivirato); cf. the Skt. root kuṭ. If khoṭana (Skt. Gr., limping) is the true reading, I know of no plausible interpretation.
(= Pali ukkoṭeti; cf. prec.), reopens a question already legally settled: (yaḥ punar bhikṣur jānaṃ saṃghena yathādharmaṃ) nikṣiptam adhikaraṇaṃ punaḥ karmaṇy utkoṭayet, pātayantikā.

, m. (to ut-kruś; nowhere recorded except as n. of a bird), outcry: (vs) utkrosu (n. sg.) mukto, and 8 utkrosu (acc. sg.) kṛtvā aho mama ekaputro!; (vs) utkrosu (mss. utkrāsu, utkāsu) kṛtvā dharaṇitale nirasto; mahāntam ārtasvaram utkrośam akārṣuḥ. Uncertain is (in a list of five individuals who sleep little at night) utkrośa (v.l. utkoṇa) ṛṇī; possibly a debtor in case of an outcry (made against him by his creditor? understanding utkrośe). But Tib., as translated in the, is said to render utkrośaḥ the red duck (see below; in Skt. a bird, Seeadler), and seems to omit ṛṇī; probably read for this prāṇī (below). watchman(?); implausible; compares this word with Pali ukkusa, a bird, apparently osprey (= kurara). Lacuna in this story;, on basis of Tib. srog chags (living being) ṅur pa (red duck), conjectures utkruśa-prāṇī. Should not Tib. be corrected to ṅu ba, weep(ing), = ut-kruś-?
(not recorded in this sense), cries for, demands (alms): (Śakro …) dvāri sthitvā bhaikṣyam utkrośate.
(nt.; = utkrośa, q.v.), outcry: mahāntam ārtasvaram utkrośana-śabdaṃ śrutvā.

(denom. to AMg. ukkosa, see below), exalts, magnifies: ātmānam utkrośayati parān paṃsayati. The AMg. ukkosa is derived by and from utkarṣa (or utkṛṣṭa) and defined as adj., highest, supreme, or, as n., pride. If this is the true etym., our word would be a hyper-Sktism, by false etym. Possibly, however, the AMg. word may really represent a Skt. *utkrośa, which, like Eng. a crying-up, could conceivably have meant glorification. To be sure I find no record, otherwise, of such a mg. in any deriv. of ut-kruś.
(nt.; from ut-kṣip plus -ana, but new MIndic formation, like Pali ukkhipana; cf. Skt. utkṣepaṇa), lifting up, nom. act.: (vs) caraṇotkṣipaṇe, in the lifting of their feet.

(Skt. in mg. lifts up, etc.), (1) lets up in sense of permits to ascend, opp. nikṣipati: ekaikasya ca prāsādasya sopānāni pañca-pañca puruṣaśatāny utkṣipanti sma nikṣipanti sma (let go up and down); teṣāṃ tathotkṣipyamāṇānāṃ nikṣipyamāṇānāṃ ca śabdo 'rdhayojane śrūyate sma; (2) (= Pali ukkhipati) suspends (from the order of monks); ppp. utkṣipta: utkṣiptānuvartaka (see anuvartaka); similarly utkṣiptānuvṛttiḥ, the following (cleaving to) a suspended (monk), so Tib. spaṅs paḥi …; (3) averts (the senses, particularly the eyes, from forbidden objects): indriyāṇy utkṣipati, and in the following lines; indriyāṇy utkṣipyāvasthitāḥ, stood averting their eyes (in embarrassment); in this sense = Pali (indriyāni) okkhipati from avakṣipati, see avakṣipta; apparently BHS utkṣ˚ is false Skt. for MIndic okkh˚; acc. to Chin. (eyes not cast to one side), anutkṣiptacakṣuṣo would belong here; curiously the Pali equivalent, okkhittacakkhu (note lack of negative!), appears to mean with downcast eyes, which the old comm. interprets by observing that it is a sin to enter a house or sit down looking around at this or that (tahaṃ tahaṃ olokento), so that okkhitta-, as opposite of this, would mean essentially the same as BHS an-utkṣipta- as interpreted by Chin. But for this evidence, an-utkṣipta-might be interpreted, in accordance with Skt. usage, as not lifted up (thus in another way = okkhitta-).
, m. (˚pta, see prec. 2, plus specifying ka; = Pali ukkhittaka), (a monk) that has been suspended:, etc. Read this for utkṣepaka(-tva); cf..
, m. (= Pali ukkhepaka,; to utkṣipati 2 with -aka), one who moves suspension (of a monk):; See prec. for.

, adj. (gdve., to utkṣipati, 2; = Pali ukkhepanĭya, with kamma), with karman, (ceremony) of suspension (from the order): ˚ṇīyam (doubtless supply karma); kurutāsyotkṣepanīyaṃ (so text) karma; yasya bhikṣoḥ samagreṇa bhikṣusaṃghenotkṣepaṇīyaṃ karma kṛtam;;; penalty for refusal to recognize or correct sins, (as in Pali), or for heresy, ib.

, n. of a kind of script:; followed by nikṣepa˚, vikṣepa˚, and (6) prakṣepa-lipi; also, line 7, utkṣepāvarta-lipi, and (in some mss., supported by Tib.) nikṣepāvarta-lipi. All these terms seem to be intended to refer to the shape of the letters, rather than to the countries where they are used. It is hardly possible to guess what the author meant by them, and the woodenly literal Tib. translations give little help; Tib. renders utkṣepa, gdeg pa, elevation (and āvarta, skor ba, turn); nikṣepa, bzhag pa or bzhog pa, putting down; vikṣepa (which Tib. transposes to the point in line 6 where ʼs [Page122-b] ms. A has it), rnam ḥthor, scattering; prakṣepa, bsnan pa, addition, increase.
, m., n. of one of the 16 devaputra guardians of the Bodhimaṇḍa:. (Tib. ut-ka-li.) Cf. next.
, n. of a goddess, attendant on the Bodhisattva in his motherʼs womb:. Cf. prec.

, m. (cf. khāḍayati = bhedane? is there some confused relation to Pali ukkheṭita,, abandoned?), one who causes to depart from (abl.), to abandon: (kalyāṇamitrāṇi) … ˚tāro lokaniketāt (sc. for a Bodhisattva).
, implied in (duḥkhena) cotto; read either cātto = ca-ātto, with ms. A, or cārto = ca-ārto (one ms. cited as cortto); affecté par la douleur, which must be substantially the meaning.]

, adj. ifc., perhaps made, produced: (prose) hastiśālāya paṭalāni ghanāni mahantāni bahujanauttakāni, (when a fire had broken out in the elephant-stables) … the thatches of the elephant stable, thick, great, made by many people … This assumes a ka-extension of AMg. -utta in deva-utta, bambha-utta, produced (created) by (the) god(s), by Brahmā (see citation in s.v. utta). The origin of the word is obscure; and regard it as identical with Skt. upta, sown. has no suggestion as to mg. or etym.
, adj. (ut plus tanū˚), with hair erect (thru joy): mudottanūruhāḥ.

, ppp. (to Skt. uttapati, cf. BHS uttāpayati), orig. (and in Skt.) purified by fire (of metals; so also BHS, suvarṇam uttaptam); here fig., purified, pure, of food: uttaptottaptair upakaraṇa-viśeṣair;; of mental and abstract qualities, uttapta- (so mss., em. ˚taṃ) jñānaṃ teṣāṃ pravartate; smṛti-mati-gati-dhṛty-uttapta-vipulabuddheḥ, of vast enlightenment purified by …; -prāmodyottapta-vipula-smṛti-saṃjanane; uttapta-kuśalamūlās te; ˚ta-kuśalamūlena;;; ˚taṃ (mss. uptaṃ, but Tib. and Chin. render uttaptaṃ) kuśalamūlaṃ; ˚mūlānām; uttaptaḥ, where context suggests earnest, strenuous, and one of three Tib. renderings, sbyaṅs pa, means primarily purified, but also exercised, trained; uttapta-tā, abstr., state of being purified, (vs) tena hitakareṇa uttaptatā-prāpta (so read, as cpd.) bodhiḥ śivā, … attained thru being purified.
, ʼs em. at for mss. Āttapta˚, Attapta˚, see s.v. Ātapta˚. But the em. may be right: having a pure rule or kingdom, see uttapta.
, n. of a previous incarnation of Buddha:.
