, adj. (or subst.; from ˚patha plus ka), of the north country; one who lives in it: (prose) ˚pathakau dvau bhrātarau trapuṣa-bhallikanāmakau; ˚pathakaṃ bhāṣyaṃ, northern dialect; ˚pathakā vayam. (They came from Taxila, takṣaśilāto.)

(apparently the usual form; also uttarī, chiefly if not wholly m.c.; uttariṃ, once uttarīṃ; uttare, ˚reṇa; possibly uttaraṃ, but use of this as separate adv. uncertain; in prior part of cpds. uttari-, ˚re-, ˚raṃ-, besides normal Skt. uttara-; Pali apparently only uttariṃ as separate word, uttari- in prior part of cpds, besides uttara-) adv., and prep. or postposition with abl. or gen., further, beyond, of time, space, number, etc.; synonym of bhūyas; all the forms enumerated seem to be equivalent and interchangeable to the extent indicated above; none seem recorded in these uses in Skt. or Pkt. acc. to the dictionaries; once uttarī may be intended as n. sg. m. of an adj., (prose) na ebhya uttarī na ebhyo bhūyān anyo hetur vidyate, no other cause is found beyond these, greater than these (cf. the next passages); with dependent abl., usually atas, tatas: nāsty ata uttari nāsty ato bhūyaḥ (cf. prec.) (prose); nāta uttari nāto bhūyaḥ; (cf., without dependent, kutaḥ punar uttari kuto bhūyaḥ;) tatottarī (m.c.?) agaṇiyu tasya āsīt saṃghas … (vs; for tata uttari), beyond that (number), incalculable was his assembly; ataś [Page123-b] ca bhūya uttari viśiṣṭatarāṃ (both edd. as cpd. uttari-vi˚) … pūjāṃ kariṣyāmi (prose); tata uttari (of time) (prose); ato 'py uttari (of serial numbers) (prose, and repeatedly in sequel); tatottari (prose! for tata ut˚); tata uttarīṃ (this form is isolated) bahukalpaṃ, many kalpas beyond this; ata uttari; (both prose; to corresponds and where uttari has no dependent form); ato ca uttari (prose); tato vottari tiṣṭhet (prose), or should remain (a time) beyond that; ato bahū uttari lokadhātu (vs); varṣaśataṃ vā tato vottari (prose); tata uttare (prose); atottareṇa (vs; for ata ut˚); uttari manuṣyadharmād … jñānadarśanaviśeṣaṃ sākṣātkartum ( ˚śeṣaḥ sākṣātkṛto); (both prose; cf. the cpd. uttari-manuṣya˚ below), … beyond human conditions; with dependent gen., mama uttari yo (ed. uttariyo) viśiṣṭo (vs), who is distinguished beyond me; naitasya (ed. ne˚) ācariya uttari (vs), there is no teacher higher than he; tasyottareṇa, em., but read with mss. pratyot˚, q.v.; (śloka vs) dīpaṃkarasya ottareṇa (see this; bad meter), prob. read ˚karasyottareṇa, which may mean ˚sya-ut˚, after Dīpaṃkara; uttareṇa Vairambhasya mahāsamudrasya (prose) beyond …; adv., without dependent: form uttari, uttari cābhyanumodayiṣyanti (prose), and further they will …; yad uttary arhattve pratiṣṭhāpayet (prose), if further he should establish them in arhatship; dānanisargaḥ punar uttari pravartate sma (prose); (tathā) cottari paryeṣate (prose); uttari senām āmantrayate sma (prose), (Māra) further addressed his host; and (parallel to, above, where ata uttari); uttari viśeṣaṃ (˚ri-viś˚ as cpd.) ārabheyam (prose), may I attain further (exceptional) distinction (as compared with the retinue, who were now his equals); (prose; parallel to Pali, where uttariṃ, v.l. uttari); (prose); (vs); (prose);;; in some of the preceding uttari occurs in situations where we should except an adjective, which seems even more called for in the next, where, however, f. or m. gender would be demanded: (na sā strī … saṃvidyate) yā tasyā rūpeṇa samā kutaḥ punar uttari (prose) … no one who would be equal to her in beauty, how much less beyond (superior to) her!, and parallels in the sequel with masc. for fem., but always uttari,, etc.; uttarī (prob. m.c., but cf. above), na uttarī prārthayi (ger., or aor.?), not asking (or, we did not ask) further; uttariṃ (not m.c., tho in vss!),; te kalpakoṭīm athavāpi cottariṃ …; uttare, sometimes, as in the first two, interpretable as n. sg. m. of uttara (), but so closely parallel in use to uttari that it is better taken as adv.: jātyā ca so viṃśatir uttare vā (vs); sadṛśo 'sti na te kutottare (with mss. kutontare, cites kutottare from a ms., and this is certainly meant); na me 'sty ato 'rtha(ḥ), ata uttare gaṇana apratimasya jñānam (so read) (vs); kaścid uttare naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanasamāpatter mārgaḥ (prose); uttare vai nānāmiṣeṇa saṃtarpya, similarly; (all prose); te kalpakoṭīr athavāpi uttare (cf., above; vs but end of pāda), they, for crores of kalpas or even further …; in (vs) reading uncertain, kuta uttaraṃ (so with ms. A, other mss. ˚ri, unmetr.; Calc. ˚rī, perhaps rightly) vā, how could there be one higher (prob. adverb); [in (prose) ed. tasya pañjarasya uttariṃ sthitvā, but read with v.l. upari, on top of the cage; this mg. is not found for uttari(ṃ);] in composition, uttari-jñāna-viśeṣasūcanatāyai (prose; apparently substantially = uttara); note esp. [Page124-a] uttarottari-(v.l. ˚ra-)-viśiṣṭatara-kuśalamūla- (prose), more and more exceedingly superior roots of merit; (ekam pudgalaṃ sthāpayitvā) śaikṣapratipady uttarikaranīyaṃ (prose), (except one person) who had something left to do in the śaikṣa course (the rest all being arhats); note that Pali has the same cpd. uttarikaraṇīya, but acc. to only as a karmadharaya, an additional duty, not as a bahuvrīhi as here; in some of the above it is not certain whether uttari- is compounded with the following word or a separate adverb; in;, above, uttari must be prep., governing manuṣyadharmād; to these passages correspond; uttari-manuṣyadharmasya jñānāye darśanāye saṃbodhāye; takes the word as a cpd., depending on jñānāye etc., prob. rightly, tho the gen. manuṣyadharmasya might be dependent on prep. uttari; the latter construction is impossible, and a cpd. (= Pali uttarimanussadhamma, superhuman faculties or conditions; the analysis of the Pali comm. cited by is inconsistent with that indicated by and) must be assumed in kaṃcid uttarimanuṣyadharmaṃ; and uttarimanuṣyadharme (so with mss., ed. wrongly em. uttare man˚); uttarimanuṣyadharmair; besides this, the same cpd. is recorded in BHS (not in Pali) as uttara-manuṣyadharma-(-pralāpa, m.),, declaring (falsely the possession of) superhuman faculties (one of the parajika sins); also uttaraṃ-man˚; (mss., in ed. em. ˚re);; uttare-man˚;; (in all these read as cpd.; ed. takes uttare as separate adj., misled by the fact that the cpd. is a loc., ending ˚dharme; see above for evidence that uttare = uttari as adv. and prep.); in apparently anuttare is used as synonym of uttare in this cpd. (taken by ed. as separate adj.), yady ekaṃ śramaṇo Gautamo 'nuttare-manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyati vayaṃ dve (see anuttara; but this word does not fit and must be either a corruption, or a sign of misunderstanding by the author of the passage; elsewhere in the same passage only forms of uttara-, uttari- etc. are used).

(Pali, see below), in (vs) ăjīvikadharma-carāṇāṃ uttarikāṇa anuttarikāṇāṃ, of Ājīvika-sectarians, superior and not superior(?); acc. to, those who have or those who have not the higher aim, which is hardly illuminating. See in Text for report of a Chin. interpretation, for which I find no basis in Indic. In Pali uttarika is reported only ˚kānaṃ phalānaṃ pattiyā; obviously superior or the like. Pali has no anuttarika.
(to Skt. uttara), superiority, in bhaktottarikā, superiority of food: yo ˚rikayā jeṣyati …; na kvacid ˚kayā parājayati;.
, see s.v. uttari; uttari-manuṣyadharma, and other cpds. of uttari-, see id.
, and their cpds., see s.v. uttari.

, nt., and ˚ryā, f. (cf. Skt. and Pali uttarīya, AMg. uttariya; perhaps a hyper-Skt. form for the latter?), apparently a covering (for a part of the body: hands, ears, or back), but cf. 2 uttarya: karṇa-pṛṣṭhottaryāṇi stambhāni (!?) maṇiratnakaṭakakeyūrakāṇi pralambitāni saṃdṛśyante sma; in in a long cpd. describing ornaments and clothes of girls, keyūra- … kaṭimekhalā-hastottaryā-karṇapṛṣṭhottaryā-hastāṅgulīyasamāyuktānāṃ (kumārīṇāṃ); in at end of a long cpd., list of ornaments and garments, maulīkuṇḍala- … ratnahāra-skandhopariṣvajānika-(corrupt?) pṛṣṭhottaryāṇy anguṣṭha-vibhedikāny (q.v.) anyāni ca vividhāni vastrāṇi.

, ger., in vāmanakarūpam abhinirmāya, mṛgājinenottarya, veṇudaṇḍam upagṛhya …, evidently covering (with a deerskin). Cf. 1 uttarya. As a ger. the form seems inexplicable, unless as an extension of the Skt. usage with ut-thā-, ut-tambh-; is a MIndic uttharya intended (to utstarati, see s.v. uttharati, = stṛṇoti; or to Skt. ava plus stṛ-)? Note that is also the only text where 1 uttarya is recorded; has the noun influenced the form of the gerund?

, adj. (= Pali id.; in this sense hardly Skt., but see for approximations; cf. uttānī-karoti), open: of the face, in uttāna-mukha-varṇa (= Pali uttāna-mukha, wrongly defined), of open (frank) countenance (suggesting accessibility, friendliness; so Pali, contrary to),; (in both foll. by smitapūrvamgama); clear, manifest, of dharma,; (with vivṛta); uttāna-kriyām āgamya, coming to manifestation; ˚nāṃ dharmadeśanām, ˚nām avavādānuśāsanīm; te (sc. doṣāḥ) … uttānā viśaditāḥ prakāśitāḥ; of doctrines that are obvious and so simple, easily comprehensible, in contrast with such as are profound (gambhīra) and hence comprehensible only to superior minds,;.

, adj. (= Pali id., Skt. uttāna), supine, on the back; upturned (with back down): (prose; parallel ottānako, q.v.) na uttānako (tiṣṭhati; the Bodhisattva in his motherʼs womb); ˚kā prapatetsuḥ;; (bhūmāv …) ˚kān pratiṣṭhāpya (these all prose); ˚kān kṛtva … bhūmau (vs); hastau … ˚kāvasthitau (prose; the hands upside down, in a mudrā); ˚kaḥ (vs).

(= Pali id.; to uttāna; in Skt. mukham ˚nīkṛtya, opening the mouth, see), publishes, makes known: (āryasatyaṃ …) ˚roti prakāśayati; ˚kariṣyati (sc. dharmam); karma … prakāśitam uttānīkṛtam; atyayam … vivṛtam uttānīkṛtam; vibhajaty ˚roti; (dharmaparyāyam …) ˚romi vivarami; ˚kurvatām, gen. pl. pres. pple.

(caus. of Skt. ut-tapati; on mg. see uttapta; Skt. caus. not recorded in this sense, even of metals), purifies (orig. of metals; here fig.): (bodhisattvavimokṣam …) uttāpayan, purifying.

(nt.; in this sense not Skt. or Pali; see uttarayati), carrying out (of a promise): pratijñottāraṇavacanā vā; a neg. is needed; either delete preceding punctuation and understand a-prati˚, in samdhi with preceding vā; or read with ms. of on (ed., with note) pratijñānuttāraṇavacanā; in either case, not carrying out oneʼs promise. erroneously corrects to the reading of ʼs text of.

(special use of Skt. sthā plus ud, q.v. in s.v. 3), arises = is being built, of a house: (anyatarasya gṛhapater gṛham) ˚te.

(= Pali uttiṇaṃ karoti; implies adj. *uttṛṇa, deprived of thatch), makes (a building) roofless, object āveśana-mālām (so read with mss., see s.v. mālā): ˚kṛtvā; (in the last two read with mss. ˚mālām ut˚kṛtvā); ˚karetsu (v.l. ˚suḥ) (here one ms. uttīni-k˚, apparently intending the MIndic uttiṇī˚).
, m. (Skt. Lex.; = Pali uttāsa, utrāsa; cf. an-u˚, nir-u˚), fear: ˚sa-bahulā(ḥ); sūkarasyeva uttrāso; na cāsyāpārime tīre uttrāso bhavati; śrotṝṇām uttrāsaparivarjanārthaṃ.

(ger. ˚ttitvā(na), ppp. ˚ttita; app. blend of utpatati with a quasi-denom. from utpatti, or modification of utpatati by confusion with utpatti;), springs up, goes forth, flies up: ˚tvā (prose), six times, subject rays of light, arci(s), as also with ppp. ˚tā (prose; in same line nipatitāyo, fallen down); ˚tvā (prose), subject śakuntako, hence clearly to root pat, fly; ger. ˚tvāna,, subject inhabitants of hell; in parallel to this,, reads utpatitvāna, but mss.
