[Page126-a] boils and abscesses, or boils and abscesses due to the (above-described) omens; but Tib., if I understand it, fails to interpret the word.,, note on, assumes this mg. also in pūrvotpāda-saṃpanno bodhisattvo, which however seems to me to mean simply perfect in (or, as a result of) previous births; so agrotpāda-saṃpanno; and cf., also of bodhisattvas, pūrvotpāda-saṃpanno … kalyāṇotpāda˚ agrotpāda˚ jyeṣṭhotpāda˚ śreṣṭhotpāda˚ praṇidhi-pūrvotpāda˚; a very similar list If I am right, utpāda here has its normal Skt. mg; (3) calamity (due to bad omens; development of 2): ˚dam āpadyeyur (otherwise).

, with object citta, saṃjñā, manasikāra, or the like, produces an intention, resolution (cf. cittotpāda): cittam,; (to become a Buddha);;; (read -cittam utpādayanti);; ppp., spṛhācittam utpāditam abhūt; manasikāram,, duḥkhamanasikārasaṃjñām,; bhūtasaṃjñām,.
, nt., condiment, relish (going with food):. So, apparently, Chin. and Jap., also, Zuspeise; Tib. sbags pa, or nos pa, which are not clear to me.
, mocks; rare in Skt., see s.v. root as plus ut-pra; but cf. Skt. utprāsa, utprāsana: (prose) tvam apy asmākam utprāsayasi; utprāsyamānasya, pres. pple. pass., of one that is mocked.)

, m. (cf. Pali uplavati, uppilavati; and see the foll. items), joy: (utyavaḥ, clearly nonsense; Tib. dgaḥ yal yal, extreme joy (?); Chin. and Jap. joy); manasa utplavaḥ, in a list of synonyms for joy and gladness.
(m.; = Pali ubbilāpa, v.l. uppilāva, ‘which is probably the correct reading,’; cf. prec. and next three), joy: mana-utplāva-karī (vāc).
, adj. (to utplāvayati, q.v.), deceiving: pareṣām utplāvakaṃ vicitrābhūtaguṇākhyānam.
(nt.) and ˚nā (connected with utplava, utplāva, qq.v.), joy: prīti-bahula utplāvanābahula; manautplāvana-karī manaḥprahlādanakarī.

(cf. utplāvaka; in this sense seems unrecorded except in BHS; perhaps caus. to Pali uplavati, uppilavati, rejoices [cf. utplava, utplāva, and prec.], caus. makes happy [for insufficient reasons], so wheedles; or else belongs to Pali uplāpeti, immerses, ducks in water, and so tricks, gets the better of), seduces, leads astray: (vs) yathāpi bālaḥ puruṣo bhaveta utplāvito bālajanena santaḥ, in parable of the prodigal son; seduced, confirmed by Tib. bslus.

(cf. Skt. utphalati, recorded in this sense,), jumps up: (prose) (tato vānaro tasya śuśumārasya) grīvāto utphāritvā (so, or uṣphār˚, mss.; upphār˚; but not causative; prob. read utpharitvā, or upphar˚?) taṃ udumbaraṃ prakrānto.

, (so), or utpika (m. or nt.?), (and v.l.), n. of a disease; Tib. either glo baḥi (of the lungs), or mgoḥi (of the head), glog pa (on which see rajata; ulcer? cancer?). Chin. apparently a disease characterized by insanity. See also uvyadha.

, perhaps attitude of head thrown back or held up stiffly: notsaktikayā, instr. (of monkʼs behavior); ˚kā-kṛta, one who is in that attitude,. In the former, Tib. mgo mi (g)zar, with the head not stiff or abruptly straight, so also in the latter except that mgo, head, is lacking; Chin. acc. to with robe inside-out.

, nt. or m. (var. ucchaṅga), a high number = 100 vivāhas: utsaṅgenotsaṅgam, by myriads; ˚gam, n. sg., cited from by as ucchaṅgaṃ; but utsaṅgaḥ (same both times); Tib. phaṅ, or paṅ, steṅ = lap-top; (hiranya)-suvarṇasya utsaṅgāṃ kṛtvā; ˚varṇasya utsaṅgaśatāni dattvā. Cf. mahotsaṅga.
(if not a misprint, MIndic for utsṛjati; cf. sajati which supports this), abandons: (vs) utsajitva (ger.; final a m.c.) amaropamaṃ gṛham.

, m., and adj. (see also ucchada, ˚daka; = Pali ussada, used in all mgs. here recorded), (1) elevation, prominence, protuberance, swelling, esp. one of 7 such on the hands, feet, shoulders, and back of the neck of a mahāpuruṣa, constituting the 16th of the 32 lakṣaṇa, q.v. (and cf. Pali sattussada): saptotsadakāyaḥ (Bhvr.), saptāsyotsadāḥ kāye jātāḥ, dvau hastayor dvau pādayoḥ dvāv aṃsayor eko grīvāyām; cf. the list, … two aṃsakūṭayoḥ, one pṛṣṭhato grīvāyām; utsadāḥ, subst.; in Bhvr. cpd. saptotsadaḥ;;;; ˚daṃ; acc.,; saptotsadāṅga; and in other lists of lakṣaṇa, q.v.; (2) addition, supplement, in connection or composition with naraka, hell, one of the 16 supplementary hells which belong to each major hell (mahānaraka; = Pali ussada-niraya, not well defined): aṣṭasu mahānarakeṣu pratyeka-ṣoḍaśotsadeṣu; kuṇapāto muktā (n. pl.) narakotsadā (abl. sg.); aṣṭasu mahānarakeṣu ṣoḍaśotsadeṣu, and same; pratyekaṣoḍaśotsadā; (aṣṭa mahānarakā …) pratyekaṃ ṣoḍaśotsadā; (3) adj., abundant, and n. abundance (distinction between the two often not clear; generally used in prior or posterior part of cpds. where either could be assumed); certainly adj. in prabhūtenotsadena viśadenānnapānena (3 synonymous adj., see viśada); utsadānnapāno bhavati, has abundant food and drink; nāty-utsadamāṃsā tanugātrī, of not excessive flesh, slender-bodied; (prose) utsada-pātracīvaradhāraṇatayā (an [ākāśa-] -paligodha, q.v., for an ascetic); (vs) tatotsadaṃ cīvarapātradhāraṇaṃ (Tib. lhag par, surpassing, modifying dhāraṇaṃ); yadi … lābha utsado bhavet, if the profit should be abundant (but, should amount to a surplus); doubtless subst. in (bodhicittaṃ …) utsadabhūtam akṣayajñānatayā, it is an abundant store …; but 2d ed. utsa-bhūtam, spring, source; in most of the rest adj. seems simpler, but subst. possible: (vs) utsada-prāptaṃ (here perhaps better subst., attained to abundance, sc. of creatures, viz. of the followers of Māra, as following mārāṇa koṭī … shows; not reduction of utsadakuśalaprāptaṃ with); utsadakuśala-saṃcayo;;; abstract in -tva, (yasya, sc. tejodhātoḥ) cotsadatvāj jvarito jvarita iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati, and thru the abundance of which a feverish man comes to be called feverish; (vs) pradoṣa vardhenti vitarka utsadā (adj. with vitarka, or subst. in comp. with it? the latter, but text prints as two words!); kaṣāyotsada-kāla-tāṃ, condition of time abundant in kaṣāya; niṣkaṣāyānutsadakaṣāya-kāla-tām (… free from, or not abundant in, kaṣāya); (sattvā …) utsadalolā (so em., mss. all corrupt; but read ˚lobhā, proved by) utsadadoṣā utsadamohā, cf. Pali (sattā …) lobhussadā dosussadā mohussadā, having abundant (Pali, abundant in, or having abundance of) lobha, doṣa, moha; (vs) apāyabhūmīs (so all Nep. mss.) tada utsadāsi, the stages of misfortune were then superabundant; utsadamaṇimuktivaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravāḍarajatajātarūpyaṃ (? v.l. ˚rūpaṃ; sc. lokadhātuṃ); (vs) asaṃyatā uddhata unnatāś ca, agauravā mānina lābha-utsadā [Page127-a] (cpd.) … sudūra te tādṛśa agrabodhaye (either abounding in profit or having abundance of profit). Peculiar is saptotsada in (Utkaṭaṃ nāma droṇamukhaṃ paribhuṅkte sma) saptotsadaṃ satṛṇakāṣṭhodakaṃ dhānyasahagataṃ … brahmadeyaṃ, and, similarly, with sa-saptotsadam; a close parallel in Pali, Ukkaṭṭhaṃ ajjhāvasati sattussadaṃ (comm. sattehi ussadaṃ, ussannaṃ bahujanaṃ ākiṇṇamanussaṃ … anekasattasamākiṇṇaṃ ca) satiṇakaṭṭhodakaṃ sadhaññaṃ … brahmadeyyaṃ; cf. also sattussadan ti pāpakārīhi sattehi ussannaṃ (this, in line 16, = uparūpari nicitaṃ). It seems clear that this sattussada in Pali = Skt. *sattvotsada, abounding in living creatures. It seems to have been falsely Sktized in (which, or its source, obviously followed closely a MIndic original very close to the Pali of) to saptotsada, because the adapter knew familiarly this cpd. as one of the 32 lakṣaṇa (above, 1). Presumably he thought it meant here containing seven elevations of some sort, but I see no use in speculating further as to his intentions.

, nt. (= utsīdana; with mg. 1 cf. Skt. utsīdati; with mg. 2 cf. prec. and an-utsanna), (1) coming to grief, ruin: sthale utsadanam (in 2 above read utsatsyati for utpat˚); (2) superfluous abundance, excess, in ˚na-dharmakaṃ (bhaktaṃ), of food offered to monks and not fully used by them, of the nature of excess ( zum Wegräumen bestimmt). For utsādanam = Tib. dril ba (rolling, in sense of rubbing down, massage; so Skt.), and read utsadanam, apparently a faulty reading.
(= Pali ussanna), excessive; see an-u˚. Cf. prec. 2.
, nt., ascent, marching up, in pipīlikotsaraṇam = Tib. grog ma gyen du ḥdzeg pa, ants marching up hill (a term used in logic).

, adj. (ppp. of ud plus sṛp, caus.), app. laid by as balance, left over (from a sum of money): aparam utsarpitam; (nāsmābhiḥ kiṃcid uddharīkṛtaṃ) kiṃ tv aparam utsarpitaṃ tiṣṭhati, (we have not incurred any debt,) but the rest remains put aside as left over.
(semi-MIndic for utsāryate,, pass. of utsārayati, also Skt., q.v.), is put aside, is violated: kathaṃ tu utsaryati dharmaśāstram.
, adj. (Skt. utsava plus ika), pertaining to festivals: vastrā ca utsavikā, holiday clothes; vyayakarmeṇa (em.) utsavikena, matters of expense due to festivals.

(to Skt. utsahati; cf. next), fortitude, persistent energy, endurance: (a Bodhisattva resolves to endure infinite torments in hells to bring creatures to enlightenment: evaṃ yāvat sarvasattvānāṃ) kṛte yāty utsahanatā aparikhedaḥ (are the two last words a cpd.? lack of weariness in fortitude, endurance?).
(to Skt. utsahati; but perhaps better read utsāhanā, to caus. utsāhayati, encouragement), enthusiasm, energy (?): kiṃ nv ayam utsahanā-vineyaḥ āhosvid avasādanā- (q.v.)-vineyaḥ.
, m. or f. pl., n. of a class of malevolent superhuman beings:; foll. by mahotsārakā(ḥ); in a long list of demons etc.
, nt. (to next with -ana), acc. to (Introd. xxii) = āvarhaṇa; it seems, at any rate, to mean removal of religious disabilities from a monk, cf. the following osāraṇa ():.

(specialized mg. of caus. of Skt. utsarati; see also utsaryati), frees (from religious disabilities), see prec.:; Tib. seems to be cited as smoṅ (zhig), which I cannot interpret; ib. (see Corrigenda), cf. osāray˚ etc. See (v)osārayati.
(nt.; cf. utsahanā, and next), inspiration, [Page127-b] the making energetic: in title of chap. 26, samantabhadrotsāhana-parivarta,.
(cf. prec. and next), in either noun, energy, or adj. with ūtir, energetic or inspired, inspiring: ˚ny ūtir aprativāṇiḥ (qq.v.) smṛtyā saṃprajanyenāpramādato (see saṃprajanya) yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ.

(caus. to utsahati), (1) considers (lit. makes) capable: (prose) te sarve … mahāprajāpatīṃ gautamīm utsāhayanti sma, they all considered Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī capable (of tending the Bodhisattva); (2) tests the capacity of: karmakārikayā … utsāhayitavyā: utsahase tvam, etc., she is to be tested as to her capacity by the karmakārikā (nun, saying): Are you capable …

(Skt. utsiñcati not in this sense; = Pali ussiñcati;), bales out, exhausts: (prose) etaṃ samudraṃ utsicāmi (mss., em. utsiñcāmi), 17 (prose) utsicāmi (kept by) mahodadhiṃ; (prose) utsicituṃ (inf.; mss. unsic˚, em. utsiñc˚); (vs) mss. unsici, ˚ciṃ (opt. 1 sg.; em. utsiṃci, which this time seems required by meter) mahāsamudraṃ.
, ppp. (hyper-Skt. for ucchiṣṭa,), (something) left over: raha utsiṣṭaṃ kṛtvānutsiṣṭāhāreṣv adadataḥ pretagatiḥ paṭhyate; utsiṣṭasyāpy aśucer na doṣaḥ.

(nt., quasi-MIndic formation from utsīdati plus ana; unrecorded; = utsadana 1 and 2; cf. saṃsīdana), (1) destruction (of a ship, on land, sthale, i.e. by running aground in shipwreck): sthala utsīdanabhayaṃ; (2) ˚na-dharma = (2) utsadana-dharmaka, of the nature of superfluity:.
, error for aut˚, in gamanāyotsukyamanā, read ˚yaut˚.]
= Skt. utsuka, longing, desirous: ity utsukheṣu (so also 2d ed.). Perhaps error; but cf.;.

(f.?), n. sg. ˚ḍhiḥ, (1) = Tib. spro ba, joy; so (v.l. both edd. utsṛcitaḥ); (2) = Tib. mthan pa (?not in Tib. Dictt.; perhaps = ḥthan pa, firmness, but Chin. obscurity, confusion, hence Kyoto ed. suggests em. unmūḍhiḥ). Probably = utsoḍhi, q.v.; both firmness and joy are meanings of Skt. utsāha, from the same root.

(cf. Skt. utsarjana; semi-MIndic formation in -ana on the pres. Skt. utsṛjati), letting loose, letting fly (pennants, in the wind): utsṛjana-nānāratnadhvaja-patākam, with various … pennants for flying (in the wind). See also anutsṛjanatā.

, adj. (hyper-Skt.,, for Pali ussita, Skt. ucchrita, for which utsṛta is recorded rarely, at least as v.l., in Skt.; cf. ucchṛta), high: ˚ta-dhvajāṃ (note in ucchrita-dhvajā, of the same entity);, read dvau-m-utsṛtāu (text ˚mṛsṛtau), and dvi-m-utsṛtai(ḥ) … tri-m-utsṛtaiḥ (in all with hiatus-bridging m).
, f. (?m.; = Pali ussoḷhi; cf. also utsūḍhi; in mg. = Skt. utsāha), exertion, strenuosity: (prose) bodhisattvānām ˚ḍhir ājāyate.
, trips, stumbles: ppp. ˚lita, as active, (prose) brāhmaṇagṛhapatikā nigamajānapadā utkhalitā (so with 1 ms.; v.l. uskha˚, intending utskha˚).

, m., (1) the moon in water, as symbol of deceptive and unsubstantial things: (among {{svnonyms->synonyms||20210831||https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/80|}} for māyā); also uda-candra, daka(-candra), [Page128-a] qq.v.; no such form noted elsewhere; (2) n. of a former Buddha:.
, m. pl., n. or ep. of a class of nāgas, who are wardens (rakṣa) of the Trayastriṃśa gods:
(nt.? cf. next), a kind of jewel: (prose) ˚da-maṇiratna-.
, n. of an upāsaka at Kiṭāgiri:
, m. (cf. Skt. bhrama, perhaps a conduit,), gutter for waste water (from a bathroom): = Tib. gtor (stor) khuṅ; udakabhrameṇa vārāṇasīṃ nagaraṃ praviśitvā. Cf..

, m. (Pali ˚rakkhasa), water-ogre, who lives in water and devours bathers: tatra ca udakahrade udakarākṣaso (mss. ˚sa) prativasati punar-punaḥ janaṃ snapayantaṃ māreti (and in foll. lines); satkāyadṛṣṭy-udakarākṣasa-gṛhītāḥ. Also dakarākṣasa; see s.v. daka.
(= Pali ˚vāhaka), flood: ˚ha-bhayaṃ vā, in a list of dangers to a caravan.
(= Pali ˚sāṭikā), water-garment, to be worn while bathing (= varṣā-śāṭī):;
, n. of a gem which keeps people from dying in the water: tad yathā kulaputrodakasaṃvāsamaṇiratnāvabaddhe (read ˚ddho?) kaivarta udake na mṛyate (so text).
, m., ˚hārī, f.; ˚hāri(ṃ), see under 2 hāra, -hāri, and cf. uda-hāraka.

, (1) adj. (= Pali udagga; not in this sense in Skt. or Pkt.), joyful, delighted: esp. often in formula, tuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajātaḥ,; (udagraḥ);;;, etc.; plurals,; also with variations, hṛṣṭatuṣṭaḥ udagra etc.; hṛṣṭā abhūṣi udagrā pramuditā prītisaumanasyajātā; in (e.g.) repeatedly in the form (hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramudita) udagraprītisaumanasyajāta; (hṛṣṭa-)tuṣṭodgraprītisaumanasyajāta; (tuṣṭa) udagraḥ; hṛṣṭā udagrāḥ (vs); miscellaneous,;;;;;; =;;;; udagra-citta;;;; (2) noun, prob. nt. (cf. Pali odagya), joy: na ca te paśyāmi abhiratiṃ (so read with mss.; em. ˚taṃ) na udagraṃ; and udagram anubhavāhi, experience joy! = farewell!; cf. also udagrī. The adj. also occurs in senses recorded in Skt.; intense, udagra-pratatavīrya-samanvāgataḥ.
(cf. udagra), joy, in ˚grī-bahula, preceded by prāmodya-, prasāda-, prīti-, utplāvanābahula, and foll. by uśī- (q.v.), utsāha-b˚. Is the fem. form due to attraction to the surrounding fem. stems?
= udaka-c˚ and daka-c˚, qq.v.: ˚drasamā imi kāmaguṇāḥ (vs), cited, reading dakacandranibhā.
(= Skt. ˚cayati), makes (voice) resound: perh. to be read in, see s.v. añja(s).
, aor. 3 sg., originated, was produced, for Skt. ud-apādi, etc. (only in; see for list of occurrences; sometimes written udupāsi in mss.).

(m., as in Skt.), (1) with vyaya (cf. Pali khandhānaṃ udayavyaya or udayabbaya, as cpd.; see also [Page128-b] samudayāstaṃgama), arising and passing away (of skandhas): (vs) (dharmacakram …) skandhānām udayaṃ vyayam, (the wheel of the law …) which is (consists of) the (doctrine of the) arising and passing away of the skandhas (wrongly, not quite rightly); (2) n. of a mleccha king:.
, n. of a former Buddha: n. sg. ˚miḥ, (so Index; text Udagra˚, apparently misprint).
, (1) n. of Śuddhodanaʼs purohita (father of Udāyin 1):; (2) n. of nāga:. (Also n. of the well-known king of Vatsa, as in Skt.,; cf. next.)
(in Pali Udāyibhadda), n. of a son of Ajātaśatru:. In the same line he is called Udāyin (n. sg. ˚yī); prob. read Udāyibhadra.
, read udaśvit (Skt., see), a mixture of buttermilk and water:;.]
, adj. or subst. m. (= Pali id.; Skt. uda-hāra; see s.v. hāraka), carrying (one who carries) water:.
(v.l. Udāragata) n. of a former Buddha:.
(v.l. Udānta˚), n. of a former Buddha:.
(by em.; mss. Udānta˚), n. of a former Buddha:.
(v.l. Udānta˚), n. of a former Buddha:.

, m. or nt. (= Pali id.; with acc. pron. usually imam, sometimes idam), a solemn but joyous utterance (acc. to sometimes a sorrowful one in Pali), usually but not always having religious bearings; almost always in modulation of phrase imam (less often idam, as;; or omitted) udānam udānayati (usually with sma after verb), very common:;;;;;; 3 pl. udānayanti;; aor. udānaye;;; udānesi; udān' udānayī (3 sg. aor.) (vs); perf. udānayām āsa; ˚āsuḥ; udānitavān; in non-religious connexions, udānam udānayati;; udānayetsu (3 pl. aor.); udānesi (3 sg. aor.); nt. udānam, as n. of a type or class of Buddh. literature, one of the 12 () or 9 () pravacanāni,;; Udāna-varga, n. of a specific work (abbreviated).

, denom., utters an udāna: used virtually always with object udānam, q.v. for forms and passages; used absolutely, without object, (vs) trikhuttam udānayati sulabdhā lābhā (so, but mss. lābhā sulabdhā; meter is bad in either case).

(or Udayin? below), (1) = Kālodāyin (also appears as ˚dayin), q.v. (in Pali he is also called Udāyī):, in text (also) printed Udayī, but Index Udāyin;;;; (son of the purohita Udayana); (2) one of the ṣaḍvārgika monks:. (Tho not named in Pali as one of the Chabbaggiya monks, 2. Udāyī in seems to have had a character deserving this reproach and is doubtless the same person as ours.) Named as type of a monk who might commit a sin; subjected to parivāsa and succeeding penances, (in and not identified with the ṣaḍvārgika); (3) n. of a son of Ajātaśatru and ancestor of Aśoka (= Pali Udāyibhadda):; in the same line called, acc. to text, Udayibhadra;

, adj. (= audāra, ˚rika; neither Skt. udāra nor Pali udāra, uḷāra, seems so used), coarse: (vs) yasya codāra saṃjñādi nāmarūpasmi vartate, visabhāgāya saṃjñāya udāraṃ citta jāyate, if in the nāma-rūpa of someone there works a coarse saṃjñā etc., then, since this saṃjñā is not homogeneous [with the pure mind], the mind becomes coarse too ().
, adj. (compv. of udāra plus ka), more exalted:.
, adj. = audārika 2 (if reading is correct), exalted, abundant: mahataś codārikasyāvabhāsasya (both edd., no v.l., but perhaps read caudār˚) loke prādurbhāvo 'bhūt.
, error or variant for Upālin, q.v.]

, m. (= Pali id.; Skt. Lex.), lifting up (of the voice); utterance; often in comp. with vacana or another word denoting voice or some form of utterance: ekavacanodāhāreṇa, with one voice (-utterance),; (śākyakumāraśatāny) ekavacanodāhāreṇāpūrvacaritaṃ samuddiśanti sma; (devāḥ …) evaṃ caikodāhārasvareṇa (with the sound of a single utterance) vāco bhāṣante sma; in read ekodāhāreṣu na sthātavyaṃ pṛthagudāhāreṣu (or ˚hāre) na sthātavyaṃ vyudāhāre na sthātavyaṃ, and in read ekodāhāro (text ˚haro) nimittaṃ vyudāhāro (text ˚haro) nimittaṃ pṛthagudāhāro (text ˚haro) nimittaṃ (see the several cpds.); ghoṣodāhāra- utterance of sound (in speech), buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ ghoṣodāhārasattvasaṃtoṣaṇam; ghoṣodāhāra-samatāṃ (… anuprāptaḥ); ayaṃ praśnodāhāraḥ, this utterance of a question; etena paraṃparodāhāreṇa by this successive expression (utterance; here substantially the same as word, name; of a succession of Tathāgatas all bearing the same name); an-udāhāra, adj., without utterance, not capable of being spoken, (a-ruto 'ghoṣo) 'nudāhāraḥ, said of the Buddhaʼs dharma; (yo 'syānta-dvayasyānugamo) 'nudāhāro 'pravyāhāra(ḥ).
(for udīkṣ˚,), looks (up): 3 pl. aor. udikṣiṣu twice, in bah(u) ud˚ (vs; Tib. sdod, wait); and sarva udikṣiṣu prāñjalibhūtāḥ (vs; wrongly; the Tib. he cites as lha zhiṅ must surely be read lta zhiṅ).
, n. of a country: ˚ne, loc. sg. See s.v. Kāviśa.

(= Aśokan id.), m. or nt., for Skt. uda˚, well, spring: so repeatedly mss. of, kept by, who suggests (note on) assimilation to initial u- (so, lxx): (here one ms. uda˚; in the rest no v.l.) =;;;;. It may be noted that the mss. often write udupāsi for udapāsi, q.v.
, n. of a city, home of Kaineya: Identified by with Pali Ātumā; but the corresponding story is located in Āpaṇa in Pali.
(= Pali id., n. of a village? cf. also), n. of a town: (˚re, loc.).
, adj. (ppp.; Skt. Lex. = sthūla, pīvara), coarse, or gross, swollen(?): udūḍha-śiraskaḥ śaṇaśāṭikā-nivāsitaḥ (mss. saṇa˚) sphaṭitapāṇipādo; same passage uddhūta˚, which seems not to fit.
, adj. (cf. uga, cited as Ap. from in, = udgata, udita), arising, arisen: (vs) tada saukhyam udgu (n. sg. nt.) mam' udāram abhūt.
, (1) (= Pali Uggata) n. of a king of Dantapura in Kaliṅga: (here ed. with one ms. Uggata, v.l. Udg˚);;;; (2) n. of a maharṣi:.
, f. ˚ikā () = udgata, high, elevated: [Page129-b] (vs) kaṭhinapīnapayodhara-udgatikām, of the daughters of Māra.

, with aruṇam, lit. makes the dawn arise: tatra (sc. in or on heresy) cāruṇam ˚yati; i.e., prob., either (1) and attaches great importance to it (cf. Eng. he thinks the sun rises and sets on …), or (2) spends all his nights (in meditating) on it; said of a tīrthikāvakrāntaka (see avakrāntaka) Tib. translates literally.
(cf. Skt. Lex. avaguṇṭhikā, and Pali oguṇṭheti, ˚ṭhita), veil, head-covering: nodguṇṭhikayā; -kṛta, (one) having the head covered (so Tib.), nodguṇṭhikākṛtāyāglānāya dharmaṃ deśayiṣyāmaḥ; similarly.

, nt. (ud plus gṛ [girati? or gurate?]; Skt. records udgoraṇa once), brandishing (of weapons): udguraṇam (udgūr˚, v.l. udgur˚) = Tib. gzas pa, brandishing (); (vs) daṇḍa-udgūraṇāni, by em., kept without note in; mss. udgīr˚ (except which is altered).

, (1) (= Pali uggaṇhāti), acquires (knowledge of truth), learns, comprehends: ger. often followed by paryavāpya, uddeśayogamanasikārān udgṛhya paryavāpya; udgṛhṇīta bhikṣavo nimittam antardhāsyati, antarhitaḥ; te (dharmāḥ) bhikṣubhir udgṛhya paryavāpya … dhārayitavyā(ḥ) etc.; sadodgṛhīta-dharmāvismaraṇa-; imaṃ samādhim udgṛhītavān, udgṛhya paryavāpya dhārayitvā …; samādhiṃ śroṣyati śrutvā codgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati …; na sukaraṃ … kāyasya pramāṇam udgrahītum; (sarvasattvarutapadavyañjanam) udgṛhṇīyād udgṛhya ca …; atha śuko … bhagavatā bhāṣitam udgṛhya paryavāpya …; na jātu rūpanimittam udgṛhītavān … na sparśanimittam udgṛhītavān;; udgṛhītum (so text each time); (2) holds fast to, keeps hold of, (so AMg. uggiṇhati, = dhār rakhnā,): so loko udgṛhīto sarvehi, all (the monks attendant on the Buddha Samitāvin) held fast to this world (i.e. imitated him in determining to remain until a new Buddha arose).
(m. or nt.; to prec.; cf. Pali uggaha, not in this mg.), taking hold (sc. of a womanʼs person), a samghāvaśeṣa sin (= kāyasaṃsarga):.

, nt. (= Pali uggahaṇa; to udgṛhṇāti; cf. ogrāhaka), grasping (intellectually), comprehension: = Tib. ḥdzin pa (id.);; sarvabuddhadharmodgrahaṇatayā; (na tv eva) mahābāhuśrutyaprāptaḥ śrāvakaḥ śrutodgrahaṇadhāraṇīpratilabdhaḥ kalpaśatasahasrodgrahaṇādhiṣṭhānena.

, m. (see also udghāṭaka, ghaṭaka; twice recorded udghaṭṭaka in mss.), lit. one who opens or reveals, i.e. explains (science or techniques; so, cited by); in cliché (aṣṭāsu parīkṣāsu, not in) udghaṭako vācakaḥ paṇḍitaḥ paṭupracāraḥ (…) saṃvṛttaḥ;;; (in the last two udghaṭṭakaḥ); same cliché reading ghaṭako for udgh˚;; and with udghāṭako;; he became an expounder, explainer, scholar, one of skillful performance (in the ‘eight testings’ of valuable things).

, adj. or subst. m. (= Pali ugghaṭitaññu; see : ‘das Geöffnete kennend’ = ‘sich auf das Offenliegende d.h. auf eine kurze Darstellung verstehend’), understanding (by) a condensed statement, opp. to vipañcitajña, vyanjitajña, qq.v., understanding (by) a full, detailed explanation: udghaṭitajñān (so with v.l., for text udghāṭ˚) vipañcitajñān (in a list of creatures, sattvān, of all kinds); same passage (read as in, or possibly ˚jñā for ˚jñān, but accs. pl.); ˚jñāḥ (udghaṭṭita˚), [Page130-a] vipañcitajñāḥ (Tib. on mgo smos pas go pa, understanding by mention of chief points); nodghaṭitajño (so two mss.; text ˚ghaṭṭ˚) vā na vā vipañcitajño 'nabhijño vā bhaviṣyati; vyañjitajñaḥ (q.v.) udghaṭitajñaḥ; implies high intellectual capacity, nipuṇo medhāvī udghaṭitajño (so read) tīkṣṇabuddhiko; other passages; (here most mss. udghā˚).

(note spelling udghaṭṭaka for udghaṭaka, q.v., and cf. sam plus ud plus ghaṭṭ-,), opens, loosens, undoes: pāśāv udghaṭṭayām āsa; phuṭṭakavastrāvārī udghaṭṭitā, mss. (ed. em. udghāṭitā with); for udghaṭita-jñāḥ (see this), udghaṭṭita˚. Cf. ghaṭṭita.
, m. (adj.?), = udghaṭaka, q.v., one who reveals or expounds: śāsanakoṭim udghāṭako, one who explains the height of the religious doctrine;;.

(v.l. ˚ṭikā; to ud plus han), in vāsodgh˚, lit. perh. interruption of, intervals between (or, postponement of) lodging, i.e. spending the nights (on a journey) in different places in succession: tvaṃ paścād vāsodghātikayā gaccha, ahaṃ tavārthe āhāraṃ sthāpayāmi; so 'pi vāsodghātikayā gantum ārabdhaḥ (the other person places caches of food for him at various points).
, the Pali form of Udraka, q.v., varies with the latter (and Udaka) in mss. and ed. of; in ed. prints Udaka (not in Index; by misprint for Udraka?) with v.l. Uddaka; the latter also v.l. in.
(= Pali uḍḍahati), burns up: ger. uddahitvā (vs); ppp. uddagdha daṇḍakavanaṃ (vs); pass. (saṃvartamāne … loke …) pṛthivīpradeśo uddahyati, is burnt up. See also.. Cf. uddāha, ˚hana.

, nt. (= Pali id.; see also antaroddāna, piṇḍodd˚), summary, brief statement, esp. of the contents of a longer literary work or passage: = Tib. sdom, summary;, cited, uddānabhūtaṃ sarvabodhisattvacaryāpraṇidhāna-saṃgrahaṇatayā, it is like a summary, because it comprises all …; uddānaṃ, applied to the following verse, which lists simply the titles of ten chapters of; asyoddānam, this is a summary of it (viz. of the results of a certain kind of good action; there follows in 5—6 lines the summary statement); (refers to the following verse summarizing seven points listed just before); similarly;;; etc.;; catvārīmāni dharmoddānāni, four summary statements of doctrine, which are then listed: (1) anityāḥ sarvasaṃskārāḥ, (2) duḥkhāḥ sarva˚, (3) anātmānaḥ sarva˚, (4) śāntaṃ nirvāṇam;, here by error for udāna, q.v., and see s.v. ityuktaka.
, adj., (one) who has no heir: = Tib. rabs chad pa, having lineage cut off;.

(m.; cf. uddahati and next; = AMg. id., also uḍḍāha; not noted in Pali; once in Skt.,), consumption by fire, particularly in kalpoddāha, the world-conflagration: kalpoddāhāgnibhūtaṃ (sc. bodhicittaṃ) sarvaduṣkṛtanirdahanatayā;; pṛthivī kalpoddāhe dahyamānā; kalpoddāhe (misprinted kulp˚) yathā vahniḥ.

(nt.? cf. prec.), in kalpodd˚, (world-)conflagration: kalpoddāhanabhūtaṃ (sc. bodhicittaṃ) sarvaduṣkṛtanirdahanatayā (cf., s.v. uddāha, cited from Maitreyavimokṣa; our passage is from the Maitreya chapter of, extracts from which, not including this one, are cited from by name in; the two seem not to be identical).

, poses, proposes (a mathematical problem; Tib. rtsis mgo phogs, set the beginning of a calculation): tatra bodhisattvaś coddiśati, ekaś ca śākyakumāro nikṣipati (figures, works out the problem) sma; na ca pariprāpayati sma bodhisattvasyaikadvau … yāvat pañcāpi śākyakumāraśatāni yugapatkāle nikṣipanti sma, na ca pariprāpayanti sma; tato bodhisattva āha: uddiśata yūyam, ahaṃ nikṣepsyāmīti … (19) pañcāpi śākyakumāraśatāni yugapad uddiśanti sma, na ca pariprāpayanti sma bodhisattvasya nikṣipataḥ;; in samuddiśanti, same mg. The Tib. renders nikṣipati by brtsis (brtsi, fut.), rtsis, calculate, figure. In same sense, uddiśati sma = Tib. sbaṅs (? sbyaṅs?) pa, or luṅ phog pa (?); Chin. uses the word used for BHS vyākaraṇa (3).
(nt.? to uddiśati), prescription, order: (vs) śayyāsanoddiśana (n. sg.) teṣāṃ naiva bhaviṣyate 'pi ca kadācit (no order for them is needed; they are provided without it).
(= uddiśati; not recorded in this sense), recognizes: (māṃ …) śāstāram uddiśyadbhir madyam apeyam, those who recognize me as teacher must not drink liquor.

(ppp. of uddiśati plus -ka, perhaps specifying,; cf. AMg. uddiṭṭha [food etc.] specially prepared for an ascetic,), (one who or that which has been) appointed, specified, prescribed; only in saṃghoddiṣṭaka, … by the brotherhood: ˚kāṃ bhikṣāṃ bhojayitvā, having fed them the food prescribed by the brotherhood; same, with bhikṣām understood,; in saṃghoddiṣṭaka-bhikṣavo (monks [as] directed by the assembly) bhojayitavyā(ḥ); prabhāte saṃghoddiṣṭakā bhikṣavo (n. pl.) bhojayitavyā(ḥ); ˚kān bhikṣūn.

, m. [= Pali uddesa; the Skt. use, see s.v. 2, is perhaps close enough to justify calling it the same mg.], exposition, explanation, setting forth (of a doctrine): ˚śaḥ svādhyāyo viniścayaḥ …; ˚śa-dānena; ˚śa-svādhyāya-saṃpratipattipāraṃparya-yogena;. See śramaṇoddeśa, ˚śikā.)
, m. (= Pali uddesaka), director, manager: vihāroddeś˚; bhaktoddeś˚ (= Pali bhattoddes˚).
, adj. (= Pali uddesika), intended for, in ātmodde˚ intended for oneself: ˚kaṃ (kuṭiṃ, hut), in parallel to Pali, where attuddesaṃ (sc. kuṭiṃ).

(m.? only in comp.; to Skt. ud with hṛ; also an-uddhara-tā below), neglect, ignoring: (vs) evaṃ hi teṣa bhavate guru-uddharāṇāṃ (so best mss. and ed.), for so it happens to those who ignore (the words of) the Master; na karmakriyoddhareṇa (bhavitavyam), one must not ignore, neglect …; an-ud˚ non-neglect, -ānuśāsany-anuddhara-, non-neglect of instruction; in (prose), for ed. anuddhuratayā, read anuddharatayā (anuddhara-tā, abstr.; grāhyavacanatām, sc. pratilapsyate), (he will attain a state of having his words accepted) because (they) will not be ignored, lit. by reason of non-ignored-ness. (Possibly read with some mss. anuddharaṇa-tayā, which would mean the same.)

(special mg. of Skt. id.; Pali has ppp. ubbhata, of kathina,, = BHS uddhṛta), suspends, stops, cancels (the kaṭhina ceremony); cf. Pali (kaṭhin)uddhāra: uddhṛte kaṭhine (Chin. as rendered by otherwise); (the kaṭhināstāraka speaks, in ending the ceremony) śva āyuṣmantaḥ kaṭhinam uddhariṣyāmi, yūyaṃ svakasvakāni cīvarāṇy adhitiṣṭhata (take possession of …); (corair muṣitakānāṃ) bhikṣūṇām arthāya kaṭhinam (which had been concluded) uddhartavyam (must be suspended); uddhrtam saṃghena coramuṣitakānām bhiksūṇām [Page131-a] arthāya; bhājite yasyābhipretaṃ tena svakāt pratyaṃśāt coramuṣitakānāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ saṃvibhāgaḥ kartavyaḥ.
, having lifted up, read prob. udvartya, cf. parallel udvartitaḥ; uddhṛtya would also be possible.]

(m.? cf. uddhava [comm. uddhavaa] = utkṣipta), perhaps pride, arrogance (so); or excitement (so; in some passages the context seems more favorable to this): in a verse found twice in (;) and repeatedly in (; etc.), vigatoddhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā buddhā(ḥ); otherwise recorded only in : avinaya-ślāghānuvṛtty-uddhavāt; yuddhoddhavābhimukhatāṃ; darpoddhavād apratisaṃkhyayā vā; amarṣadarpoddhava-karkaśāni; naṣṭa-harṣoddhava-dravaḥ; vyāvṛtta-pramododdhavena manasā; durjanaḥ paṭutarāvalepoddhavaḥ.
, nt., rude behavior: = Tib. rgod byed (which probably has this meaning, despite); so one Chin. interpretation. Cf. samuddhānana (˚dhanana).

(m.?), (1) some branch of mathematics, perhaps subtraction (or debits? accounting of debts, cf. 2), in a cliché, list of subjects studied by youths, mudrāyām uddhāre nyāse nikṣepe …;;;;;; seems to be replaced in by dhāraṇa, ˚ṇā, q.v.; (2) (= Pali id., and once in Skt.,, acc. to cited in) debt, in uddhārīkṛtam, kiṃcid ud˚ has anything been incurred as a debt?; (3) kaṭhinoddhāra (see uddharati; Pali uddhāra and ubbhāra), suspension, cancellation:
(m. or nt.), act of lifting, in pādoddhārakeṇa, instr., with lifting up of the feet: yadā teṣām ṛṣikopena pakṣāṇi śīrṇāni tatas te pādod˚ prasthitāḥ;.

(m.? so Skt. Lex., once in literature,), perhaps river, stream (suspected by of being only n. pr. of a river); in (prose) (mahatā) puṣpāḍhyena (pravarṣatā), should mean with a great stream of flowers raining down. Both edd. puṣpāḍhyena, which can only be understood if a noun for stream or rain is supplied; nearly all mss. puṣpodyena; udya is recorded as v.l. in a Hindu Lex. for uddhya, see; perhaps read puṣpoddhyena, or even puṣpodyena with mss.? Tib. me tog maṅ poḥi char chen po ni ḥbebs, a great rain of many flowers rained down.
(pass. to Skt. ud-dhvaṃs-), and caus. ˚syāpayati, is (causes to be) insulted or mocked; so read in, see s.v. udvaśyate.

, nt. (= audbilya, q.v.), joy, pleasurable excitement: prabhayā kāyacittodbilyasaṃjananyā (cf. under audbilya, also with prabhā); (prabhayā …) kāyacittaprahlādodbilyajananyā (so most mss., ˚daudbilya˚); (vāk …) kāyacittodbilyakaraṇī; kāyacittodbilyakaraṇatayā (of speech); udvilya-(mss. udvīla, ˚ra)-harṣā hāhākāraṃ udīretsuḥ; cittodbilya-karī (of Buddhaʼs voice; n. sg. f.); cittodvilyaṃ pratilabhante; cittodvilyasamanvāgatāḥ.
, f. ˚ikā, adj. (cf. next), manifesting, declaring, setting forth: dharmaparyāyodbhāvikā priyavāditā, and similarly in foll. lines.

, nt., and ˚nā, f. (= AMg. ˚ṇā; ˚na recorded in this mg. once in Skt.,), (laudatory) manifestation, making known, declaration: mahāyānodbhāvanārthaṃ; sarvabodhisattvānāṃ codbhāvanārtham; otherwise noted only in cpd. guṇodbhāvanā, [Page131-b] rarely ˚na, manifestation or making known, proclamation of virtues: Svāgatasya guṇodbhāvanāṃ kartukāmaḥ; ˚nāsya kartavyā; (śrutā …) āryāvalokiteśvarasya guṇ˚nā; same;;; āryāvalokiteśvarasya guṇ˚nāṃ kurute (in words then quoted); nt., vikurvitāni śrūyante guṇodbhāvanāni ca, but guṇodbhāvanāṃ śṛṇu; ˚nāṃ bhāṣitum ārabdhaḥ.
, m. (= Pali, in cpd. ubbhidodaka; Skt. udbhid, acc. to fem.), spring, fountain: = Tib. chu mig.
(m.c. for udbhūta), manifested, appeared: (vs); read gātrodbhutā (= gātrā ud˚) with mss. and Tib.

, adj., for which the site (vastu) is visible: (kalpika-śālā …) ˚tukā; glossed in 14 by prahīṇa-vastukā, the site for which has been abandoned (i.e. not in use otherwise); seems to correspond to Pali gahapati (˚tī?) (see comm.), one offered by a layman.
(m.?), n. of an ocean (samudra) in which the nāḍīkerī tree grows:.

(in Skt. nt., park, and so Pali uyyāna), (1) park, as m. (? with m. form of pron.): udyāna sarve (n. pl.) (vs); (2) advance (of an army), one of the arts mastered by the young Bodhisattva: udyāne (Tib. mdun du bsnur ba, moving forward) niryāṇe avayāne …; (3) in divide, probably, udyāna (for ˚naṃ) dhāraṇ' (for ˚ṇīnām!) ita (= itaḥ) pañcamim (sc. bhūmim) ākramanti, for this reason (so Chin.) they enter the fifth (stage), a garden of dhāraṇīs (so Chin.). Were it not for the Chin. translation, I should be tempted to understand udyāna-dhāraṇ(am) …, they proceed to maintenance of progress (in general; an extension of 2, above) from this point to the fifth (stage). It may, however, be noted that in the prose of,, the words udyāna (in mg. park) and dhāraṇī occur, not to be sure together, but in and respectively.

, m. (cf. Vedic id., the mg. of which in some places,, is not clear), in sūtrodyāmaḥ =, perhaps extension, drawing out (of thread), see s.v. tatkṣaṇa; but the precise meaning of the phrase {{excapes->escapes||20210831||https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/80|}} me. It may mean effort, exertion (Skt. udyama), as in (Kalsi). In this sense probably read nir-udyāmā, as suggested by, (prose).

, f. subst. (adj.?), (cf. Pali uyyodhika,, old comm. = yattha saṃpahāro dissati, the correspondent of our word, which seems to have been Sktized by association with yūtha, prob. unhistorically; root yudh is doubtless the true source; but mg. is rather obscure, see, who guesses sham fight), perhaps some sort of military exercise, such as sham battle; in ˚kā-gamanam = Tib. gyul bśams pa ḥkhrug tu (ḥgro ba), (going to) an army prepared for battle? or a battle-prepared combat (i.e. a military maneuver)?; in seemingly adj. with senā, udyūthikāṃ senāṃ darśanāya (Chin. regarder les manœuvres,); in accord with this possibly udyūthikā in may imply senā, meaning (an army) ready for military operations (?).

(see also s.v. udyoṭita), acc. to, = Pali uyyojeti, dismisses, sends away: yāvad dhārmaśravaṇikāś codyojayitavyāḥ parṣanmaṇḍalaṃ parisaṃsthāpayitavyam; but Tib. brtson par ḥgyur, = (to be) made zealous, the regular Skt. mg.; yāvad can be understood as up to the point (in the text where it is said—), thus fitting this mg., and ʼs interpretation seems implausible. [Page132-a] They assume the same mg. for (bhagavān … asuranayutāni … samyaksaṃbodhīye vyākaritvā bahūni ca prāṇisahasrāṇi āryadharmeṣu pratiṣṭhāpayitvā rājānaṃ śuddhodanaṃ ca) saparivāraṃ ca udyojaye; but here too this verb (mss. udyojeya or ˚yaṃ) may well mean aroused, inspired, as regularly in Skt.; this accords well with the preceding parts of the sentence, and seems more natural than dismissed (tho Śuddhodana and his followers did in fact depart, as the next sentence says).

, in eṣa bhikṣu(r) muhūrtam apy udyoṭitaḥ syād, acc. to Chin. () would seem to mean (may this monk be) annoyed (if only for a moment). But for this, I should assume a substitute for udyojitaḥ, dismissed, sent away (ppp. to udyojayati, q.v., in mg. of Pali uyyojeti). Cf. AMg. joḍiya (= yojita,), united; Hindi joṛnā; Skt. juṭ, juḍ, join.

(= Pali Uddaka, which also occurs in mss. of, see s.v., Rāmaputta; see also Rudraka), n. of a teacher with whom the Bodhisattva studied for a time:;;;; Udraka (alone), associated with Ārāḍa, q.v.,;; and with Devadatta (as persons of bad conduct),. Udraka also Tib. lhag spyod (superior conduct) for Udraka () and Rudraka ().

, (1) n. of a disciple of Śākyamuni (= Pali Udena?):; (2) another form of Rudrāyaṇa, q.v., a king of Roruka: (prose; mss.); (vs; here Rudr˚ would be metrically impossible; nevertheless the same pāda is repeated with the unmetrical reading Rudr˚!).
[= Pali ubbaṭṭeti; in Skt. rare and chiefly ppp. udvartita], rubs down, anoints, or the like: (kumāraṃ) … udvarteti supeti; so; ˚teti ca snāpeti ca.)
, ˚yamānas, and caus. udvaśyāpayitvā, for which Tib. mtho brtsams la is cited,, read uddhvasyate, pass. of Skt. ud-dhvaṃs-, is mocked, and caus. uddhvasyāp˚ ().]
(nt.; perhaps Sktization of Pali *ubbahana, to ubbahati pluck out, destroy, prob. from Skt. ud-vṛh-), removal, destruction: duḥkhodvahanacittāś ca; saṃsāre sarva-duḥkhodvahanāya bhavati.
, ger. (perhaps to otherwise unrecorded ud-vi-ci-, pluck, gather): (prose) puṣpāṇi udviciya, gathering flowers (v.l. uddhiricya).
, adj. (gdve., to ud-vi-īkṣ-), (worthy to be gazed at,) beautiful: bhavanāni (houses, palaces) … udvīkṣyāṇi.
(m. or nt.), a high number:; corresponds to upavarta, q.v.

(m.? = Pali ubbedha, defined as height; AMg. uvveha, defined by only as depth; Pkt. uvveha, acc. to height or depth, also zamīn-ka avagāha, penetration of the ground[?]), height (so surely in most cases): lokadhātuḥ saṃtiṣṭhate, caturaśītiryojanasahasrāṇy udvedhena;;; (yaṣṭi, or yaṣṭī …) dvādaśayojanāni udvedhena; (iṣikāni, so text …) dvādaśapauruṣā udvedhena; here preceded by figures relating to depth (extent of penetration of the ground), see naikhanya, and circumference (? see parigohya); in a close parallel,, (iṣīkāni …) dvādaśapuruṣa-udvedhena (mss. udvehena, uddehena) is preceded by the statement of depth (naikhanya) and by a form read by tripauruṣoccāni, which would refer to height and so be inconsistent with udvedhena (which, however, if it meant depth, would be inconsistent with the preceding form containing naikhanya); it seems that should have assumed -parigohya [Page132-b] (as in; or some form relating to circumference) instead of -ucca (mss. read -pauruṣaroccāni or -puruṣaroddhā, perhaps showing, in the syllable -ro-, a faint trace of that original). himself saw this in his note on, but overlooked it on. Cf. āvedha, pravedha.
, tears apart, destroys: (tadāsya gṛhād ekaikāṃ) śilām ˚yāma iti; = Tib. bkogs te gzhig go, pulling apart we will destroy.
, a posture with hands joined at the back of the neck:; so Tib. (gñaḥ goṅ du [mi = Skt. na] bsnol) and Chin.; = vyastikā (-kṛta); cf. also vinyastikā, atyastikā, one of which probably = this.
, adj. (= Pali unnaḷa; doubtless dial. form of next), haughty, arrogant: an-un˚, foll. by parallel anuddhata.

, (1) adj. (ppp.; cf. prec. and next; not recorded in this evil sense), arrogant: uddhatāṃ unnatāṃ dṛṣṭvā capalāṃ …; bodhisattvo 'n-unnatavīryo bhavati; (2) n. of a former Buddha:; (here of course in the good sense recorded in Skt. and Pali, lofty).
, f. (not recorded in this evil sense; cf. prec. and unnamana), pride, arrogance: ˚tiṃ varjayet sadā.
, n. of one of the 8 Uṣṇīṣa-rājānaḥ (see uṣnīṣa 3):.
(nt.), or ˚nā (= unnati, q.v.), pride, arrogance: (vigatamānaṃ) tena vīryārambheṇānunnamanāt (neg. an-un˚); (vs) tenonnamanā na cāsti śāstuḥ.
(not recorded in this sense), brings up = raises (a child); pass. unnīyate (˚ti): tahiṃ āśramapade so māṇavako unnīyati, in this hermitage-place the boy was brought up.
, (cf. Skt. unnaddha, haughty), (state of absence of) pride:.

(AMg. uṇṇāma, unnāma, elation, pride; in Skt. one doubtful occurrence where, if correct, it means [physical] elevation; not in Pali), elevation (of spirits), elation; usually in comp. with its opposite avanāma or ˚mana, once with nāma, also of opposite mg.: an-unnāmāvanāma-tāṃ, state of not being elated or depressed; lābhālābhatayā unnāmāvanāma-karo, causing elation or depression by getting or not getting; (vs) unnāma-nāmāni bahūni gacchatī, goes to many fits of elation and depression, see s.v. nāma = avanāma; nonnāmajāto bhavati;, text an-unnāmāvanāmana-tāyai, unto being not subject to elation or depression (mss. vary greatly).

(-tā, in comp.; nom. act. to ud-nud-, no form or deriv. of which is otherwise recorded), thrusting forth (from), driving out (of): sarvālayanilayonnodanatāyai, said of activities of a candidate for Bodhisattvahood.
, f. (= Skt. unmāda), madness: (prose) (yadi gacchen) maraṇonmattiṃ vā prayacchante.
, m., n. of a demon that causes madness: = Tib. smyo byed. Cf. Unmāda, in similar list of demons.
, disrespect, contemptuous treatment: ˚nāṃ kutsanāṃ sahate. No *un-man-seems recorded.
(m.), n. or epithet of some hostile (magic or supernatural) power: ˚nātaḥ, abl.; follows huvanātaḥ, see huvana; followed by bhūtātaḥ vetāḍātaḥ etc.
, n. of a class of demons (causing madness), = Unmada, which occurs in a similar list: etc.
, n. of a woman:. In Pali version of same story called Ummadantī; see.

(?), a turning sideways: in śīrṣonmijitakayā, [Page133-a] instr., (prose), with a turning of their heads to one side (they gazed at the Blessed One); of gods. So apparently Tib. mgo byol nas. Is the word somehow related to un-miñj- (see the foll. words)? The only v.l. is A śīrṣāmiñjitakāyā; I have thought of śīrsāniñjitakāyā(ḥ), with bodies unmoved as to the heads (see aniñjita). But Tib. clearly had no such reading (and no word for body).

, m. (to ud-miñj, cf. under miñj-; and next), apparently lit. opening, and so starting, initial development, initiation of something: sattveṣu mahākaruṇonmiñjaḥ saṃbhavati, and 19 mahāmaitryunmiñjaḥ, of Bodhisattvas; (udāraḥ khalu ta) unmiñjo bhadrikā mīmāṃsā kalyāṇaṃ pratibhānaṃ. (,) translates question, stating that ‘all the Chinese translators’ translate so.

, nt. and adj. (see s.v. miñj-, and cf. prec. two), (1) nt. opening, as of the mouth (so):; (in both Tib. phye ba); parapudgalānām unmiñjita-nimiñjitāni, lit. openings and closings of (or, things opened and closed by = beginnings and endings, starts and finishes, of) other individuals;, of an ascetic, tasya … śāntasya nirunmiñjitasya (without initiation of anything) nirālambasya; (2) adj. opened = initiated, begun: ˚tāni nimiñjitāni vicintitāni vitarkitāni … (see kelāyati) niketasthānāni tāni sarvāṇi vigatāni bhavanti sma; (3) nt. mouthful (lit. opening, sc. of the mouth, as in) (śvasv api …) ekaudanonmiñjitam ekālopaṃ vā parityajati, throws even to dogs … a single mouthful of porridge or a single bit of food.
, adj. (ppp. to ud-muh-; = Pkt. ummūḍha), infatuated: ˚ḍha-cittaṃ nigṛhṇāti.

, f. ˚ikā, adj. (= unmūrdhan, mit aufgerichtetem Kopfe,), with head thrown back: (rājā) kuśo … sudarśanāye devīye unmūrdhikāye (i.e. trying to escape from his {{vioient->violent||20210831||https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/80|}} embrace) āliṅgito (the king, whom the queen did not recognize, was hideously ugly).

, (1) at end of cpds. (= Pali -upaka, -ūpaka, ˚ikā f.; BHS also has equivalent -upaga, q.v.), pertaining, belonging to …; suitable, appropriate (to) …; fit (for) …; like: fragment in naivasaṃjñānopakā(ḥ), haplog. for naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanopakāḥ, which read, belonging to the … (= ˚yatanopagāḥ, see -upaga; ed. reads naivasaṃjñino nāsaṃjñino, a secondary recast); kulopaka (= Pali kulūpaka), lit. belonging to a family, = family associate, said of a monk who is regularly supported by a certain family, (tasya yo mātāpitṛṇāṃ, so mss., em. ˚tṝṇāṃ) bhikṣu kulopako āsi; (in replaced by kulopagata, q.v.; in wrongly read by em. in text, see s.v. kalopī;) also, by extension, said of the houses visited by such monks, kulopaka- (mss. kulopa-)gṛheṣu gatvā, and 3 te kulopakagṛhāṇy upasaṃkrāntāḥ; prob. by analogy with this word prajñopaka (em. for ājñop˚, ājñāp˚; context makes em. seem quite certain), dependent on prajñā, (śīlaṃ śiriṃ [so mss.] caiva kṛtajñatā ca) prajñopakā tu pravarā bhavanti, but (the virtues of) morality, majesty, and gratitude are excellent (but) subordinate to prajñā; akāryopaka, not fit for use, anarghaṃ vaiḍūryamahāmaṇiratnam uccāre patitam akāryopakaṃ bhavati; yathopakam, adv., according to what is fitting,; (after a seat of honor has been provided for the Buddha) ˚kaṃ ca bhikṣusaṃghasya, and (seats) for the assembly of monks according to propriety (i.e. relative rank); nirupaka, apparently adj., without a correspondent or match, peerless, unequalled, (vs) dharmaś ca me nirupakāyu (i.e. nirupaka = ˚kaḥ [Page133-b] plus ayu = ayaṃ) śrutaḥ; (2) (= Pali id.) n. of a Ājīvaka, with whom Buddha conversed while going to Benares to deliver his First Sermon: (note esp. tasmād ahaṃ upaka jino, a line which elsewhere contains the form Upaga, q.v.); (3) n. of a purohitaʼs son in the Upāli-Gaṅgapāla Jātaka:; corresponds to the character Aḍḍhamāsaka in the Pali, see.
, adj. (and subst. m.?; to Skt. upa-kṛ), beneficent: vāg upakarā; upakarāṃ (in 16 text ˚kārāṃ, erroneously) vācam;, upakaras tvaṃ tāta pañcaśikhāsmāka(m u)pakaraś ca yo hi nāma …;.

, = bhoga, food: upakaraṇavaikalya-jaṃ (duḥkham), one of 5 kinds of duḥkha, clearly = bhoga-vaikalya-duḥkha-, pain due to defects in food; prob. in this mg. upakaraṇavikalasya jīvikāpekṣāyaṃ caturtha upakleśaḥ;;. Cf. upakāraṇa.

, acc. to Tib. dishevelled state (of the hair of the head): (prose; of the harem women mourning the loss of the Bodhisattva) kāścic chīrṣopakarṣikayā … rudanti sma (Tib. mgo ḥbal lo, had their heads dishevelled).

(cf. AMg. uvagāraṇa = Skt. upakāra? or for Skt. and Pali upakaraṇa?), in evaṃ laḍḍukāgarbhoktārakaviśeṣān (? seems corrupt) pūpopakāraṇān sarvadevabhūtagaṇān sarvasattvāṃś ca mantropetān vidhinā niryātayet. We seem to need dat. instead of acc. forms for ˚gaṇān and ˚sattvāmś (as in the following parallel sentence); with that change, pūpopakāraṇān might mean benefactions consisting of cakes, or instruments (cf. upakaraṇa) of (making) cakes; or, with a mg. characteristic of upakaraṇa in Pali rather than Skt., commodities consisting of cakes; or finally, if = BHS upakaraṇa in (see s.v.), food consisting of cakes.
(= next; associated in both mgs. with Kāla, q.v.), (1) n. of a nāga king:; (2) n. of a yakṣa leader: (prose).
(= prec.), (1) n. of a nāga king: (prose); (2) n. of a yakṣa: (vs; cpd. Kālopakālakau).

(cf. Skt. upakīrṇa, covered, bestrewn), in Rājopakīrṇaka (sūtra), q.v.; mg. not clear, but the subject of the story suggests falling, reverting (to the king; of the property of one who dies without heirs), or that which has reverted etc.
, n. of a Buddhist deity or yakṣiṇī, always associated with Keśinī, q.v.:;;; (all prose). See next.
, once for Upakeśinī in vs (doubtless m.c.):.

, m. (= Pali upakkama; to upakramati; see also upasaṃkrama), violence, doing violence to …, attack (by violence): (vs) kāyopakrama-karaṇai(r) manyante bāliśāḥ śuddhiṃ; ˚meṇa ātmānaṃ māreyā; ātmānaṃ ca upakrameṇa māritukāmaḥ; similarly; sa evaṃvidha upakramaḥ kṛtaḥ; ātmopakrama-duḥkham, and 7 paropakrama-duḥkham, … thru violence by oneself and by others.
(nt.? = Pali upakkamana), = upakrama, violent attack: sarvasattvakāyotpīḍanopakramaṇādhivāsayamānān, enduring … violent attacks.

, also ˚meti (= Pali upakkamati; Skt. [Page134-a] upakrāmati in this sense once,; cf. upakrama, ˚maṇa, ˚mika, aupakramika), attacks, does violence to: upakramemi ātmānaṃ mārayiṣyaṃ; mātmānam (mss.) upakramāhi; ātmānaṃ upakramiṣyāmi, and 4 ˚nam upakramitukāmaḥ; upakrāntā, ppp., see s.v. upasaṃkrama.

, adj. (also aupa˚, q.v.; upakrama plus ika: = Pali opakkamika), due to, caused by violence, violent attack: (vyādhīn …) amanuṣyavaikārikān api viṣayaparopakramikān api (cf. s.v. aupakramika); (ābādho …) ātmopakramiko vā paropakramiko vā; otherwise recorded only in a cliché, ātmopakramikāṃ (due to self-inflicted violence) śarīropatāpikāṃ duḥkhāṃ tīvrāṃ kharāṃ kaṭukām amanāpāṃ (te added once) vedanāṃ vedayanti (vedayante);; (in amanāpāṃ omitted);;;. A shorter Pali form opakkamikā dukkhā tippā kaṭukā vedanā vediyanti (Pali has no *attopakkamika). In vedanā is usually recorded instead of ˚nāṃ.

(cf. Pali ppp. upakkiliṭṭha; and upakleśa), is stained: (caturbhir upakleśair …) upakliṣṭo bhavati; (prose) āgantukaiḥ kleśair upakliśyate, in passage cited from ‘Ratnakūṭa’ =, of which however text reads … upakleśe (read ˚śaiḥ) saṃkliśyate.
, m. (cf. Skt. upaklinna, rotten), putrefaction: nābhūt … upakledo (of the teeth, of the mahāpuruṣa).

, m. (also semi-MIndic ˚kileśa; cf. upakliśyate; = Pali upakkilesa, of which 5, 10, or 18 are enumerated; evidently there was no definitively fixed list), (minor, secondary) impurity, stain, depravity; in most texts no very clear distinction is made between them and the kleśa in principle, but (see esp. 89 of note 2) insists on the fundamental distinction, and comm. cites a list of 21 upa˚; they ‘proceed from’ kleśa, 91; a list of 24 in, whereas in the 6 kleśa have been listed; upak˚ listed (caturbhir upakleśair … upakliṣṭo bhavati) and (no relation to list);, following saṃyojana, bandhana, anuśaya, paryutthāna, and followed by paryavasthāna (so read); cf. saṃyojana-bandhanānuśayopakleśa-paryavasthānānām; ({{deflning->defining||20210831||https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/80|}} upāyāsa) (ye cānya evamādaya) upakleśās ta upāyāsāḥ; cf. sopadravaḥ sopakleśa(ḥ) sopāyāso;, see s.v. upakliśyate; vigatopakileśena; (sattvānām alpakuśalamūlānāṃ) bahūpakleśānām; (vs) upakleśair manādibhiḥ (see s.v. mana, app. m.c. for māna, which however is standardly one of the kleśa); ˚śair na lipyate. The word seems likely to have been originally a noun cpd., upa plus kleśa, the rare verb upakliśyate may be a back-formation from it; yet the ppp. upakkiliṭṭha occurs in canonical Pali.

, nt., subordinate (Buddha-)field:, stated to be four times the size of a (Buddha-)kṣetra; the implication seems to be that the environs of -the kṣetra constitute the upakṣetra. But no other reference has been noted.

, (1) at end of cpds. = -upaka (1); with MIndic g for k, partly induced by secondary association with upa-ga(m)-; cf. Aśokan chāyopagāni, concerned with (i.e. providing) shade; belonging to: ākāśānantyāyatanopagāḥ, and three others of the same group incl. naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanopagāḥ (q.v. for other occurrences; see -upaka; Pali has ˚yatanūpaga); hastopagaḥ, pādopagaḥ, lit. doubtless belonging to the hands or feet, of ornaments placed there (Tib. rgyan = ornament); Pali has hatthupaga and pādupaga,, as epithets of ornaments; (2) n. of an Ājīvaka, = Upaka (2), q.v.: (so mss., wrongly em. [Page134-b] in ed. to Upagaṇa); (vs), same as, in both Upaga for Upaka of Pali correspondent and (tenopaga jino hy ahaṃ; tato 'ham upaga jino; alone corrects the meter by transposing Upaga; Pali tasmāham upaka jino).
, also an-upa˚ (to Skt. ˚ta with specifying ka), pl., those that have (or, have not) entered (here, to residence for rains):, see āvāsin; in Tib. cited as dam bcas pa, entered upon a vow.
, m.,, or nt., id., cited from, a high number (in text upāgama-, q.v.)
, ppp. (of upa-guṇṭh-, not noted elsewhere), entwined, encircled: (prose) hārārdhahāropaguṇṭhitadehaṃ.
, n. of an alakṣaṇaka (q.v.) Buddha:; converts Māra,;;; (here called Sthavira-Upa˚) ff.;; see next.
= prec.: (prose; neither dim. nor pejorative force perceptible).

, adj. (Skt. ˚ḍha plus -ka, pejor.?), embraced (wrongly): pāpamitropa˚ (so the {{repentent->repentant||20210831||https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/80|}} Ajātaśatru, of himself; Buddha, repeating his words, uses upagūḍha,).
, approves, recommends: (dayānuvṛttyā ca nāma te kṛtya-pakṣam) āśvāsanavidhinopagṛṇīte. So ed., but mss. (u)pagṛhṇīte, wins over, which seems better.]
, wrong em. in ed.; see aruṇodghāṭa.]

, adj. (cf. Skt. ˚tin, ˚taka; Pali ˚tika but as noun, injury,, contrary to), injuring … (end of cpd.): atikrūras tvaṃ vajrapāṇeḥ (read ˚ṇe) yas tvaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ sattvopaghātikaṃ kāmopasaṃhitaṃ ca mantratantrāṃ (= ˚trān) bhāṣayase.
, nt., in piṇḍopacaraṇam, begging-round (= Pali piṇḍa-cāra; upacaraṇa not in Pali, in Skt. only in sūpa˚, see).
, adj. (cf. Skt. upacāyin; to root cāy), revering: kulajyeṣṭhopacāyakaḥ (Tib. ri mor byed pa, revering).

, m. (= Pali id.; see also s.v. tāḍāvacara), (1) environs, neighborhood: deśapradeśopacāreṣu nimnonnata-samaviṣameṣv; (mahābrahmā …) lokadhātau gahananimnopacārān avabhāsayati; (2) access (for Pali cf. s.v. 7, with references): (see prajñapti 4).
, n. of a cakravartin king:. Seems to correspond to Pali Upacara,. Cf. Cāru.

, adj.-ppp. (Skt., heaped up), (1) technically applied to karman, piled up; aggravé ():; (as explained here, acts may be kṛta, done, or not done, and both kinds may be upacita or not; see); (2) honored (perhaps error for apacita): tasya (sc. Buddhasya) devamanujopacitasya (read ˚jāpacitasya?) añjaliṃ kurutha.
, adj. (in Skt. ˚tra only as n. of a meter), (somewhat) variegated: citropacitro (of the deer-king); citropacitrāṇi pratyāstaraṇāni. The cpd. seems to be intensive. Also, citropacitrako vatso.
, n. of a daughter of Siṃha (8): (cf. Celā).
(= Pali upacchindati; Skt. has no cpd. of upa and chid; cf. upaccheda(-na) etc., anupacchinna), cuts off, interrupts: kathāṃ nopacchinatti.

, m. (= Pali id.; see upacchinatti, anupaccheda, etc.), cutting off, severance, destroying: dharmopa˚ the cutting off of the states of existence, of conditioned existence, in a formulaic list, followed usually by tṛṣṇākṣayo virāgo nirodho nirvāṇam:;;; (separate from prec., for which mss. samartho); in text sarvatamopacchedaḥ, no v.l., read perh. (sarva-?)dharmopa˚; āhāropa˚; -dāridryopa˚; yamalokopa˚; vṛttyupa˚; vaiśāradyopa˚.
(nt.), cutting off: vaṭṭopacchedana-, see vaṭṭa. See also upacchinatti, and an-upacchedana(-tā).

, also ˚jān˚ (see under janayati, and on), conceives (lit. produces) a thought or feeling, in oneself: dullabhasaṃjñām upajanetvā, conceiving the thought that it is hard to get; (vs) upajānaya tvaṃ sukhāni, rejoice!; in (vs) gauravam upajenitvā (best mss. ˚janitvā; read ˚jānitvā, as meter requires long initial syllable?), conceiving veneration.

, nt. (to Skt. and Pali upajīvati; cf. Skt. upajīvana), dependence, living a subject life: (vs) varaṃ mṛtyu (most mss. ˚yuḥ) prāṇaharo dhig grāmyaṃ nopajīvitam, better death that takes away life; fie! is not dependence vulgar?

, ger. ˚tīrya, having crossed over (the saṃsāra), become saved: (vs) svām' (see svāmam) upatīrya tāraya jagad, yourself having crossed (being saved), make to cross (i.e. save) the world; Tib. ñid rgal nas …

(= Pali Upatissa; cf. Tiṣya 6—9), the given name of Śāriputra: (story of his conversion);;; in mentioned in a list of śrāvakas, following Tiṣya, but not juxtaposed with Śāriputra (who occurs in in the same list).

, (1) exhibits (in words) as a future prospect; promises, predicts (for someone): trīṇi yānāny upadarśayitvā; (˚darśayati);, having held out a prospect of (promised) three vehicles; kusumāyāṃ (loc., so read with mss.) mahāvīcim upadarśeti nāyakaḥ (vs), the Leader holds out for Kusumā the prospect of (predicts, prophesies) the (hell called) Great Avīci (as recompense for sin); (2) as in normal Skt., exhibits, displays (e.g. an art or skill: śakyasi … śilpam upadarśayitum, can you exhibit an art?); in mayā sārdhaṃ samarthaḥ śilpena śilpam upadarśayitum, lit. able to display art for art with me, i.e. to vie with me in such displays.
(semi-MIndic for Skt. ˚dṛś˚), appears, perh. to be read in and, see s.v. pad.
, m., n. of a type of Buddhist literature, one of the pravacana (last in both lists, ninth in, twelfth in), lit. instruction:;. Apparently not so used in Pali. See

, exhibits, displays: jarāṃ ca upadeśenti, na caiṣāṃ vidyate jarā; and 19, ārabdham (? mss. alabdhi) upadeśenti eṣā lokānuvartanā (see anuvartanā). Similarly (they are not born or begotten, yet) mātāpitṛñ ca deśenti eṣā lokānuvartanā; alpotsukatvaṃ pradeśenti eṣā˚. The mg. is regular for Skt. deśayati and for upadiśati, pradiśati, but not recorded for the causatives of the two latter. Nevertheless it seems necessary to keep the mss. readings, rather than read (upa-, pra-)darśenti, as in his note was tempted to do (and that altho forms of darśayati are similarly used in the context, e.g.).
(to Skt. upa-dru-), oppressor, aggressor: [Page135-b] ˚tāraḥ (n. pl.? or intended as n. sg.? cf.; all other nouns in the section are sg.).
, n. of one of the brothers of Śāriputra:.

, (1) nt. (= Pali id., paradukkhūpadhānena yo attano sukham icchati, on the basis of, by means of, pain to others …, cf.,), basis, what causes or is needful for …, usually in comp. with sukha-: (vs), read, evaṃ (or, etan) mamo sarvasukhopadhānaṃ saddharma …, the Good Law which is the basis of all happiness for me; sarvasukhopadhāna-pratimaṇḍitāḥ; sattvānāṃ sarvasukhopadhānaṃ dadyāt; dānaṃ naikasukhopadhānasumukhaṃ; sukhopadhānam = Tib. bde baḥi yo byad, what is needful for happiness; sarvasukhopadhānena; (sukhitān kuryāt);;; ˚dhānair; sukhopadhānaiḥ (preceding word missing); manuṣyasukhopadhānena; upadhānasaṃpanno, ep. of Buddha, possessed of the basis (sc. of happiness, presumably short for sukhopa˚); also cpd. with hita-, (vs) sarvaṃ hitopadhānaṃ, all the basis of welfare; with duḥkha- (as in Pali, above), yat teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ duḥkhopadhānaṃ tad utsṛjya;, see s.v. śatana; (2) ifc. Bhvr., base, rest, support (lit. and physical): and aśmantakopadhānāyāṃ (resting on a stove) kāṃsyapātryāṃ (in ˚kopādh˚, misprint); (3) piṇḍopadhāna, see this; (4) m., n. pr., in, a cousin of the Buddha, son of Śuklodana and brother of Ānanda and Devadatta; perh. distortion of some other name (Upananda?).

, some part of a lute, perhaps bridge (as the support on which the strings rest)?: droṇīṃ ca pratītya carma ca pratītya tantrīś ca pra˚ daṇḍaṃ ca pra˚ upadhānīś ca pra˚ koṇaṃ ca pra˚ … vīṇāyāḥ śabdo niścarati.

(m.; = Pali upadhi, and also Pali upādi), (1) substratum of continued existence; attachment, bond uniting one to existence. Acc. to upādi means the khandhas alone, while upadhi includes also kilesa (with which makes it ‘almost synonymous’), kāma, and kamma; but acc. to upadhi is sometimes equated with the pañca-kkhandhā. In Pali, upādi is, acc. to, used only in comp. with -sesa, in cpds. usually beginning sa- or an- and regularly epithets of nibbāna (-dhātu); these are represented in BHS by anupadhiśeṣa, nirupa˚, sopa˚, qq.v. But BHS also has upadhi and nir-up˚ (m.c. niropadhi) = Pali (nir-)upadhi. The passages here listed belong exclusively to this latter class, = Pali upadhi. (But it seems that even in Pali, upadhi and upādi are not always clearly distinguished.) upadhī-kṣīṇā (vs); sarvopadhi-pratiniḥsarga the getting rid of all up˚;;; sarvopadhi-niḥsarga (Bhvr., with dharma);; sarvopadhikṣaya-; cf. upadhi (mss., em. ˚dhiṃ) pratītya duḥkhasya saṃbhavo sarvaśopadhikṣayato (mss., em. sarvopa˚) … nāsti duḥkhasya saṃbhavo; upadhi-saṃkṣaye; śalyam upadhiṃ viditvā; upadhiṃ hi loke śalyam iti matvā, lʼattachement … cʼest la misère … Others s.v. niropadhi. In upadhi has three Tib. definitions; the first, phuṅ po, regularly = skandha (as Pali upādi = khandha); the third, ñon moṅs pa, regularly = kleśa (as Pali upadhi, ‘almost syn. with kilesa,’); while the second, rdzas, thing, substance, matter, belongs to a meaning of the word app. unknown to Pali, viz. (2) material thing, ‘chose matérielle’ (, = Tib. dṅos, which also = Skt. vastu), ( in); see also : ‘Par upadhi, il faut entendre la chose (ārāma, vihāra, etc.) donnée à un moine ou au Saṃgha: le mérite qui procède (tadbhava) de cet upadhi sʼappelle [Page136-a] aupadhika’ (q.v.). Hence, (3) in bhagavān upadhau vartate, the Lord was acting in regard to material things (of the assembly of monks), i.e. in the function of an upadhi-vārika, q.v. (= aupadhike). (See also s.v. plotikā.)

, adj. = aupadhika, q.v.: (prose) sarvopadhika-puṇyakriyāvastv-abhibhāvanatāyai (no v.l.). assumes sarv' opadhika-, MIndic for aup˚, which seems less plausible than assumption of the form lacking vṛddhi.
, m., guardianship of material objects, the office of an upadhi-vārika, q.v.: anyatamasyārhata upadhivāraḥ prāptaḥ; kasya dāsīputrasyopadhivāra iti.( wrongly treats this as equivalent to ˚vārika.)

(only), regularly ˚vārika, m. (from prec.; see upadhi 3), lit. guardian of material objects; beadle or provost of a monastery, in charge of physical properties: = Tib. dge skos (dge bskos, dge skyos or bskyos), lit. virtue (or welfare, or alms) commissioner; see; upadhivārikasya; (=) ˚kaḥ pṛṣṭaḥ; (Dharmarucir) vihāre ˚ko vyavasthāpitaḥ;; ˚vārakasya, but, repeating the substance of, ˚vārikasya; tata upadhivārikeṇa gaṇḍīr ākoṭitā; he announced the day of the half-month to the monks,. Acc. to, this officer was ‘a supervisor or director of monks … a sort of provost-sergeant … who keeps strict order and punishes transgressors.’ This fits well the usual mg. of Tib. dge ba (virtue).
, blames, finds fault with, thinks (or speaks) ill of: (prose) te tām upadhyāyanti.

, (1) n. of a monk, disciple of the Buddha:; one of the ṣaḍvārgika or ṣaḍvargīya group, (with Nanda,; cf. Nandopananda);;;; (2) n. of a nāga king, always associated and almost always compounded with Nanda, 2, q.v. for references.
(= prec., 2), n. of a nāga king:; (both vss, prob. m.c.; in cpd. Nandopa˚).
, n. of a nāga king:. Cf. next (doubtless the same).
, n. of a nāga king:. Cf. prec.

= Skt. id., Pali upanayhati; in defines (ye taṃ) upanayhanti by bear enmity towards; but most interpreters take it in the usual sense, ye taṃ upanayhanti, who are attached to this (thought). The same vss; read atra ye copanahyanti (, nopa˚; ye upa˚); here atra, loc., depends on the verb: who are (not) attached to this (thought). However, note the BHS and Pali upanāha, q.v.)

(= Pali upanāmeti, brings, presents; once in Skt., (piṇḍān) kumāryā upanāmayet, he shall offer [tender, hold out] to the girl); most mgs. classifiable under the two headings brings (to a person or place), and presents, offers; but the two shade into each other, and there are aberrant cases; in practically all, the thing (or person) brought or presented is acc., or nom. in passive expressions; the goal or recipient is sometimes acc., rarely loc., but much more commonly gen., rarely dat., with both act. and pass. expressions; very rarely nom., subject of a pass., the thing presented being then acc., (vs), read with best mss. āhāram upanāmye 'yaṃ (for ˚yet-ayaṃ; ˚yeta), let him be tendered food; (1) brings, physically (to): and upanāmehi me (chandaka aśvaṃ) kaṇṭhakaṃ, bring me …; (vs); [Page136-b] (prose) pañca haṃsaśatāny upanāmitāni, were brought (physically; here not ‘presented’) to the king; (prose) (yasmiṃś ca kūṭāgāre bodhisattvo mātuḥ kukṣigato 'sthāt, taṃ brahmā … brahmakāyikāś ca devaputrā abhyutkṣipya brahmalokaṃ …) pūjārthaṃ copanāmayām āsuḥ, transported (the apartment) to the brahma-heaven; (kumāram … asitasya maharṣer) antikam upanāmayati sma, brought into the presence of …; upanāmyantāṃ maṅgalāni, let auspicious objects be brought; (text upā˚); also brings to enlightenment, (vs) kathaṃ nu bodhāv upanāmayeyaṃ (sc. sattvān); in (vs) supply tān, (ye cāpi saṃśrāvitakā tadāsī te śrāvakā teṣa jināna sarve,) imam (most mss. idam) eva bodhiṃ upanāmayanti, they bring (them) to enlightenment (subject the Jinas, not the disciples as and assume); (2) delivers, as a letter, or the like: sa tasyās taṃ lekham upanāmayati sma; (prose) tena taṃ lekhaṃ tasya sārthavāhasya upanāmitaṃ; (prose) (sā ratnapeṭā rājño Bimbi)sārasyopanāmitā lekhaś ca; (prose) tāny asthīny ādāya bhagavate Buddhāyopanāmayām āsa; (3) presents (introduces, shows, makes known) a person to another (usually gen. but may be acc., as in) (vs) (kumāram …) upanāmayan suravarāṃ (for ˚rān), cf. = (vs) vādicandraṃ upanāmayati suravarāṇāṃ (and cf. upanayati in similar context); upanāmetha kumāraṃ ṛṣisya, and 3 (kumāro) ṛṣisya upanāmito; (prose) taṃ daridrapuruṣam ānāyya (or ānayitvā) mahato jñātisaṃghasyopanāmayitvā, … to a great crowd of his kinsfolk; upanāmayi (aor.); (kumāro rājño) 'śokasyopanāmitaḥ; (4) hands over an arrested person (criminal, etc.) to the king: (prose) (sa …) rājño upanāmayito (!ppp.; v.l. ˚nāmito); so … rājño … upanāmito; kāśirājño upanāmehi; and similarly, of a snake subdued and confined, (bhagavāṃ taṃ nāgaṃ …) uruvilvākāśyapasyopanāmayati; (5) presents, offers, tenders, gives (e.g. food and drink, medicine, etc.): (above); (vs) (odanavidhim …) svahastam upanāmayate, offered them (food) with her own hand; (vs) phalāni upanāmaye (aor.); (prose) (tasya lubdhakasya) phalodakam upanāmitaṃ; (prose) tena so bhojano tasya vadhyasya upanāmito; (prose) mātāpitṝṇāṃ upanāmeti; (vs) upanāmaye (aor.) piṇḍapātraṃ jinasya; asmākaṃ lūhāny (sc. praheṇakāni, q.v.) upanāmayasi; (teṣāṃ … mūlaphalāni) copanāmayati; (prose) (bahu cāsya …) pānabhojanaṃ tatropanāmyeta (pass., would be provided there for him); (prose) bodhisattvāya … tā yūṣavidhāḥ kṛtvopanāmitā abhūvan; (vs) yatropanāmyanti (pass., sc. bheṣajā), and wherever (the medicines) are given; in prose, (yatra ca punar vyādhyā) vyupanāmyante (q.v.); Tib. (both times) btaṅ, give (medicine; in line 3 nad gaṅ la, for whatever disease); (prose) tac ca bhaiṣajyam upanāmitaṃ na pibeyuḥ, and 12 upanāmitam; (jewels, ornaments, etc.) (prose) ratnarāśayas tasya dharmabhāṇakasyopanāmayitavyāḥ; sarvaṃ devīye upanāmeti, 10 tāni devīya upanāmayati; sudarśanāye upanāmiyanti (pass.); (bowls) tathāgatasyopanāmayanti;;; (a seat); (garments) (bodhi)sattvāyopanāmayati sma; (a car) yāne rāvaṇenopanāmite; (a celestial palace; for residence) (vs) upanāmayiṣye (sc. madvimānaṃ; a god speaks); (water for bathing) upanāmemi (could also be rendered bring); (flowers) bhagavatas tāni padmāny upanāmayati sma; (a putative son) sārthavāhasya upanāmeti (dārakaṃ); (taxes) tasya … karapratyayā upanāmitāḥ (also 16); (a bow) (prose) (bodhisattvasya) yad-yad eva dhanur upanāmyate (could also [Page137-a] be rendered was handed to, provided for) sma, tat-tad eva vichidyate sma; (6) presents = proclaims, makes known (a religious text or ‘door to salvation’): (where monks shall preach this sūtra) sūtrendrarājaḥ teṣu viṣayeṣu upanāmito bhaviṣyati; (vs) mokṣadvāram upanāmayāhi me (addressed to Mañjuśrī); (7) (orig. brings, and so) places, locates: (prose) tad bhojanaṃ hastipṛṣṭham (acc. of goal) upanāmya, having placed that food on the elephantʼs back.

, f. ˚ikā, (1) adj. (= Pali id., see below), only in cpds., introducing to, functioning as introduction to, having reference to, relating to: ātmopanāyika (= Pali attūpa˚, often ep. of dhamma or the like, as spoken) introducing oneself, relating to oneself, (Lalitavistaro nāma dharmaparyāyasūtrānto …) ātmopanāyikas tathāgatena bhāṣitas …; ˚kaṃ dharmaṃ deśayām āsa; -jñānopanāyika-, constituting an introduction to knowledge, sarvajagaj-jñānopanāyika-dharmacakrapravartanā-; other cpds., -jagadupasaṃkramaṇopanāyika-sarvajñatā-; yathāvaināyikopanāyika-varṇā (n. sg. f.), having a color (aspect) that acts as introduction to that which is in accord with Buddhism (see vaināyika); (2) f., in varṣopanāyikā, subst. (= Pali vassūpa˚), the first day of (i.e. serving as introduction to) the rainy season: ˚kā; ˚kāyāṃ, loc. sg.,;;.

, m. (= Pali id.), hatred, malice; follows krodha: = Tib. (ḥ)khon du ḥdzin pa (after krodha, before mrakṣa); (one of 40 cittasaṃprayuktasaṃskārāḥ);, list of 24 upakleśa begins krodha, upanāha, mrakṣa; these three also listed; kleśopakleśāṃ (for ˚śān) krodhopanāhādīn; krodhopanāha as cpd. also;;; neg. anupanāho (= Pali id.; non-hatred) dharmālokamukhaṃ.
, adj. (or subst.; = Pali id.; to prec.), malicious (person): (na krodha)nasyopanāhinaḥ akṣāntibahulasya …

(not recorded in either mg., cf. next), (1) lays down, establishes (dharma): yaṃ ca kāśyapa tathāgato dharmaṃ yatropanikṣipati sa tathaiva bhavati; sarvadharmāṃś ca kāsyapa tathāgato yuktyopadiśaty (om. upadiśaty with v.l.) upanikṣipati; tathāgatajñānenopanikṣipati …; (2) includes: … praṇidhānāni, tāny ekasmin mahāpraṇidhāne upanikṣiptāny antargatāny anupratiṣṭhāni.
(nt.; cf. Pali upanikkhepana, not noted in this mg.), laying aside, putting down, leaving off: saṃghāṭyā pañcopanikṣepaṇakalpā(ḥ) (cf. Pali).

(in Pali only ger., see 2 below; in Skt. used of secretly depositing, caching treasures, not in mg. 2), (1) hides, secretes: (yaḥ punar bhikṣur bhikṣoḥ …) jīvitapariṣkāram upanida [-dhyād upanidhāpayed vā …], confirmed by Chin. as to mg.; but Pali equivalent,, has apa-ni-dheyya vā ˚dhāpeyya vā, and this cpd. is regular in Skt. and Pali in this mg.; perhaps read apa-for upa- in; (2) ger. upanidhāya (= Pali id.), comparing, making comparison with (acc.):; (18—22) tatra parataḥ śīlasamādānād bodhisattvasya param upanidhāya śikṣāvyatikrame vyapatrāpyam utpadyate. suviśuddhāśayatayā śīleṣu bodhisattvasyātmānam upanidhāya śikṣāvyatikrame hrīr utpadyate.

(and ˚dhyāyana?), nt. (to next; = Pali ˚nijjhāna and ˚nijjhāyana), reflection (upon): dharmārthopanidhyāne; paṇḍito bhavati samyagupanidhyāna-śīlaḥ; sva-parārtha-samyag-upanidhyānāya dhyānam; in text corruptly, uparidhyāyatanatā [Page137-b] (the complement is teṣāṃ manasikārāṇāṃ, line 1), for which read either upanidhyāna-tā or (rather more likely) upanidhyāyana-tā, cf. the second Pali form above.

(Skt. has both presents to dhyā but does not use this cpd.; = Pali upanijjhāyati; cf. prec.), thinks, reflects upon (acc.): te bodhisattvam upanidhyāya (ger.) gāthābhir abhituṣṭuvuḥ; … bhūtaśāntatāṃ ca kāyasyopanidhyāyati; (tathāgatavikurvitaṃ …) na nidhyāyanti nopanidhyāyanti; -dharmaparyāyam … upanidhyāyāmi (so read for text ˚dhāyāmi); similar context upanidhyāyati; upanidhyātavyaḥ (follows vyavacārayitavyaḥ); tvam (read tvayā, with note) … saṃraktacittayā puruṣaś cakṣuṣā cakṣur upanidhyāyatyā (pr. pple., instr. sg. fem.) na vyavalokayitavyaḥ; raktacittā anyonyaṃ upanidhyāyetsu (of the two sexes), repeated in 11 in dubious form ˚dhyāyeta or ˚dhyāyet, mss., em. ˚dhyāya (ger.) te … (the forms of mss. could be used as aor. but seem repetitious in that sense); upanidhyāti only noted in and evam (as described in preceding) upanidhyāti; but in followed in same line by evam upanidhyāyataś, gen. sg. pres. pple.
, ppp. to ˚pātayati (caus. to Skt. upa-nipat, or denom. to upanipāta?), in ˚ta-tva, state of being made to appear, or the like: (cittaśarīrapra)-pīḍanopanipātitatvād vastusatyaṃ prajānāti.

(in Skt. ppp. ˚pīḍita, only in fig. sense, afflicted, heimgesucht), presses down upon (lit. and physically): (vs) (caraṇau mahāmune) mūrdhinā upanipīḍya (v.l. upari pīḍya) vandituṃ, to revere the feet of the Great Seer, pressing with his head upon them.

(cf. next; Pali ˚bandhati, binds to, attaches; Skt. writes, composes, except once ppp. haftend an,), fastens, attaches: sarvasattvakāyāṃs tatra svakāya upanibadhnāti, connects the bodies of all creatures with his own body; (guṇān … na vijahan, manasā āgamayann,) upanibadhnan, making fast, attaching (to oneself); yeṣu kuleṣu piṇḍakā upanibaddhās (attached to, fixed for, himself) teṣu bhoktuṃ preṣayati (sc. his guest-monks); maṇiratnaṃ vastrānta upanibaddham, fastened on (lit. and physically); balīvardā nopanibaddhāḥ, not tied up.
, m. (= Pali id.; Skt. not in this mg.; cf. prec.), connexion, dependence (of effect on cause): pratītyasamutpādasya hetūpanibandhaḥ katamah (and repeatedly in the sequel), cited.
, ppp., written, recorded; surely error for Skt. upanibaddha: sthavirair api sūtrānta ˚ddham.]

, m. (cf. Pali upanissaya, but the usual Pali mg. does not seem to be quite paralleled here), (1) dependence, reliance: sarvasattvā buddhopaniśrayavihāriṇo (dwelling in reliance on the Buddha) bhavantu; kalyāṇamitropaniśraye vihāriṇo bodhisattvā(ḥ); ye te sarvakalyāṇamitropaniśraya-vihāra-vihāriṇaś ca; (2) in ˚yaḥ, residence for a little while, temporary residence, acc. to Tib. re zhig gnas bcaḥ ba, and Chin.

, ger., postposition (= Pali upanissāya;; also Sktized as upaniśritya, q.v.), near, with acc.: (prose) naite … devamanuṣyān upaniśrāya viharanti, they do not dwell near (in the company of) gods or men; (yaṃ …) grāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā upaniśrāya viharati.

, ppp. (= Pali upanissita; cf. prec. two and next), dependent on, reliant or based upon, once with instr.: satkāyenopaniśritāḥ (text erroneously [Page138-a] ˚niḥśritā; see s.v. satkāya); (vs), reads (with several em.) mahyam mālā citrā upaniśritā, which (if correct) I would interpret bright garland that depends on me (for which I am responsible; otherwise).

, ger., postposition (to Skt. upa-ni-śri-, but actually a Sktization of upaniśrāya, q.v.; in mss. often written upanisṛtya, sometimes ˚śṛtya, which is undoubtedly an error,,), near, with acc.: śrāvastīṃ mahānagarīm upaśritya viharati sma; so regularly foll. by viharati, nagarīm upa˚ vi˚;; etc.; caityam upa˚ viharanti; pūrvāṃ diśam upaniśrityāsthāt, took a stand near the eastern quarter, and so; examples of spelling ˚sṛtya in mss. (and ʼs text of), vaiśālīm upanisṛtya prativasati sma; mahānagaram upanisṛtya viharati sma (one ms. ˚śṛtya); rājadhānīm upanisṛtya (em. ˚śritya) viharati etc.
, ppp. (to upa-ni-ṣīdati, only Vedic and not in this sense; cf. Pali upanisīdati), seated: sukhopaniṣaṇṇa-, comfortably seated. Cf. next.
, m. (= prec. plus ‘specifying ka’), the one that is seated: kuśadrumaṃ kumāraṃ rājāsane upaniṣaṇṇakaṃ upadarśayati, showed Kumāra the prince, who was seated on the throne (not the real king).

, f., upaniṣā, also written ˚śā, ˚sā, ˚sad (= Pali upanisā, in mgs. 1 and 2; on relation to Skt. upaniṣad see (1926), magic correspondence;, orig. connexion, from upa-ni-sad- approcher … être ou mettre en regard, confronter), (1) cause, basis: duḥkhopaniṣac chraddhā, la foi nait de la souffrance (); hetu, pratyaya, nidāna, kāraṇa, nimitta, liṅga, upaniṣad are synonyms (Vyākhyā); ib. Index, referring to, mokṣadharmopaniṣad ucchedaḥ; (base causale,); (ādhāra ity ucyate,) upastambho hetur niśraya upaniṣat pūrvaṃgamo nilaya (cf. the synonym-list above,) ity ucyate; anyā hi lābhopaniṣad anyā nirvāṇagāminī, for the cause (basis) of gain is one thing, that which leads to nirvāṇa is another (same vs in, with lābhūpanisā); see also under (3) below, and s.v. candropaniṣad; (2) likeness, comparison (so), chiefly in a frequent cliché, found;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;; usually a long formula, ending kalām api gaṇanām apy upamām apy upaniṣadam (or ˚ṣām, etc.) api na kṣamate (or, nopaiti); sometimes abbreviated by yāvad (e.g.;, all 3 times) or vistareṇa yāvad () or without any such phrase indicating abbreviation (e.g.); on the other hand, additional terms may be added, esp. at the end (before na …), as dhṛtipadam (q.v.) api, aupamyam api; (both times but before upani˚);. The forms of our word, besides the regular upaniṣadam, are: upaniṣām (ed., but most mss. ˚ṣadam; one ˚sām api ˚ṣadam api);;; ˚sām both times, and see above; ˚śām;;; in (both times), as in one ms. of (above), the item is duplicated, reading upaniśām apy upaniṣadam ( ˚sadam) api; for the verb, na kṣamate (or pl. ˚nte) and nopaiti are equally common, while has the isolated na gaṇito bhavet. Tib. (on, and acc. to on) renders upaniṣad in this passage by rgyu, cause, but this clearly makes no sense. A sort of modulation of this cliché, with nom. sg. forms, in na teṣāṃ saṃkhyā vā gaṇanā vopamā vopaniṣad vopalabhyate; also (yeṣāṃ saṃkhyā nāsti) gaṇanā pramāṇam upaniṣad aupamyaṃ nāsti. [(3) acc. to, and s.v., where [Page138-b] Dharmarakṣa is cited as authority, the word also means step, degree (Grad, Stufe), and Wogihāra finds this mg. in This passage reads (18—23) tasyaibhir daśabhir ākāraiḥ kuśaladharmasaṃgrāhakaśīlavyavasthitasya kṣipram eva kuśalasaṃgraho bhavati, sarvākārasaṃgrahaś ca: yad uta, dānopaniṣadā śīlopaniṣadā kṣāntyupaniṣadā vīryopaniṣadā dhyānopaniṣadā pañcākārayā ca prajñayā. Clearly the 10 ākāra = the 10 pāramitā (), the last five being ‘forms’ of prajñā. But I doubt that upaniṣad here means degree, step, or stage; rather as in 1 above, by the cause of dāna etc., on the basis of …, by means of … (4) In for (tayā) svopanisad (uktā) read prob. svā pariṣad, her retinue, with note.]

, adj., f. ˚nī (= Pali id.; to Skt. upaniṣevate, Pali ˚sevati), serving, waiting upon: read akṣudrasattvop arisevinī sadā, in;, with Pali (same vs) apāpasattūpanisev˚. , ppp. (= Pali id., upanītasmiṃ jīvite; also upanīyati is brought to an end,), ended, finished: (vs) māya (= māyāṃ) … mānadarpopanītāṃ, done with (= free from; lit. finished as to) arrogance and pride.
