, f. (= Pali id.; cf. next three, and upapāda; specialization of Skt. id., cf. s.v.,), (re-)birth, state of existence (past or future or present): (vs) ˚tiṃ śubhāṃ tyaktvā, giving up a glorious state of existence (in a heavenly world, to be reborn on earth); upapattiyā (loc. sg.) … vaśitāṃ gato (see ˚tti-vaśitā); kā upapattiḥ (future state) ko 'bhisaṃparāya (q.v.) iti; (tiryagyony-)upapattibhayabhīto; ˚tti-nānātva-tāṃ; na cyutir nopapattiḥ; bodhisattvānāṃ pancavidhā upapattiḥ; upapatty-ānantarya-citte pratyupasthite, said of a man at the point of death, when the mental state which immediately precedes rebirth has arrived (he becomes aware, by sight, hearing, etc., of the state in which he is about to be reborn by the power of karma); upapatti-pratilambhika, or ˚prātilambhika, qq.v.
(cf. Skt. aupapattika, and see s.v. aupapatti; from upapatti plus (i)ka), spontaneously produced, or perhaps merely of (various) origins (nānopa˚): nānopapattika-sarvakāyanirmāṇameghān niścarya.

, supernatural power of choosing rebirth ( conjectures, of choosing the family he is to be born in; perhaps too limited), one of the vaśitā, q.v.:;, defined sarvalokadhātūpapattisaṃdarśana(-tayā); cf., s.v. aupapāduka; in (vs) read upapatti-vaśītāsya [Page139-a] = ˚vaśitā (ī m.c.) asya, which mss. clearly intend; ed. has false em. See also under upapatti,.

apparently error (misprint?) for upapanna, in tiryagyoni-yamalokopapaddhānāṃ sattvānāṃ and 3 ˚paddhāṃ (! read ˚āḥ) sattvās (n. pl.). Certainly means reborn in (states of animals or of Yamaʼs world), and is associated with upa-pad-, cf. 7 upapadyante.]

[= Pali upapajjati, also Skt. ˚yate but rarely, see s.v. upa-pad- 8], is (re-)born [cf. upapatti; one or two cases are here cited]: upapatsyate, see s.v. aupapāduka; saptame divase … sūkaryāḥ kukṣāv upapatsyāmi; (Tuṣite) devanikāye upapannaḥ. For upapadiṣyati,,;, read upadṛśyati or ˚diśyati, see.)
, m. (cf. next two), investigator, advisor (of a king): rājño … amātyāś cintakās tulakā upaparīkṣakāś cintayitvā tulayitvopaparīkṣya … ime tulakā upaparīkṣakā iti.
, nt., and ˚ṇā (= Pali ˚rikkhaṇa; cf. prec. and next), investigation, examination: ˚ṇam; (dharmāṇām … samyak-cintanā) tulanā upaparīkṣaṇā.

, rarely ˚kṣyate and ˚kṣyati (ya- present? or possibly phonetic corruption? cf. parīkṣy˚, nirīkṣy˚; = Pali upaparikkhati; not in Skt., but has noun upaparīkṣā, s.v.; cf. prec. two), investigates, gives consideration to (acc.): saṃsāram upaparīkṣate sma; (yoniśa, ˚śo; evam) upaparīkṣitavyam, must be carefully considered, (so v.l., Index, and; Kyoto text upalakṣitavyam);;; ˚kṣya, ger., (see s.v. upaparīkṣaka); (kācamaṇayo ratnasadṛśās te) bhavadbhir upaparīkṣyopaparīkṣya (in ˚kṣya-m-upa˚, with ‘hiatus-bridging’ m);; ˚kṣyopaparīkṣya also (jewels); (vastu …) cintayitvā tulayitvā upaparīkṣya; (mantrapadānām artham cintayati) tulayaty upaparīkṣate; dharmānām artham upaparīkṣate; tad evaṃ … samyag upaparīkṣamāṇena; present forms in ya, upaparīkṣyeta (prose); arthaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca cintayanti tulayanty upaparīkṣyanti.

(m.; in this sense not in Skt.; cf. upapāduka, aupa˚; corresp. to Pali upapāta, in cutūpapāta or cutup˚;; and AMg. uvavāa, ˚vāya, birth, derived by from upapāta, but could as well represent upapāda; cf. also upapatti, same mg., from upa-pad-yate), birth, incarnation: (vs) darśeti sattvāna cyutopapādam (= cyuty-upa˚, Pali cutūpapāta, above; dvandva, fall from one existence and rebirth in another); (vs) cyutopapādaṃ jānāti sarvasattvāna nāyako. Knowledge of this constitutes one of the three vidyā (see traividya) and is a product of divyacakṣus as one of the abhijñā,.

= aupapāduka, q.v.; used in exactly the same ways, often in the same texts which elsewhere use aup˚, and by me grouped under the occurrences of that form; note esp. aupapādukaḥ as title of the story, but in the text itself always upa˚,; other occurrences of upa˚ are;;;;;;;;;;;. , adj., quasi-ppp. (= AMg. uvavea, upaveya; correctly explained by as = upeta blended with upapanna, which replaces it in Pali, below), provided (with), possessed (of), at end of cpds., and only in vss, apparently used m.c.: āryaguṇopapetā; patrapuṣpopapetāḥ; vīryabalopapetā (same vs in Pali,, thāmabalūpapanno); [Page139-b] śīlopapeto; kuśalopapetaṃ; balopapeto; puṇyopapete (mss. ˚pamete); varṇopapetaṃ (v.l. varṇopetaṃ, metr. inferior); lakṣaṇopapeto (mss., em. ˚ṇupa˚); sumatopapeta-; vīryopapeta; jñānabalopapetāḥ; jñānapathopapetā(ḥ); kuśalopapetā(ḥ); dhyānabalopapetaḥ.

(m.; Skt. upamā plus Skt. upanyāsa), use of comparisons (in disquisitions): sūkṣmaṃ (text śū˚) tac cakram an-upamopanyāsa-vigatatvāt, … because it is not (to be) separated from the use of comparisons; upamopanyāsa-nirdeśās (read ˚śāms?) te … nirdekṣyāmi.

, adj. (to Pali upaya, cf. Skt. and BHS upāya, plus -ika), serving as an approach or means: only in cpd. sādhanopayika (-karma-, or -visaraḥ), in colophons: (here sādhanaup˚);;;.

(= Skt. upari; 3 times in prose of, otherwise in vss), (1) adv. on high, above: upariṃ ca khe dundubhayo vineduḥ; u˚ ca devā 'bhihananti tūryān;;; (vs) heṣṭā … upariṃ ca; (2) adv., further: (prose) noparim itthatvam (q.v.); (3) postp. with gen., above, on top of: (prose) mīḍhaparvatasya uparim anupalipyamāno caṃkramaṃ cakrame (mss., em. caṃkrame); (prose) bodhisattvamātur na kvacid upariṃ (so mss.!) uparimena gacchati, does not pass aloft anywhere above the bodhisattvaʼs mother. (prob. represents, m.c., MIndic Uppala = Skt. Utpala;; cf. Utpala 4, Utpalaka 3, and Padma 4, id.), n. of a mythical kalpa, in which lived successively 300 former Buddhas termed Kauṇḍinya-gotra: (vs) ekatra kalpe upalāhvayasmiṃ.

(in mg. 1 = Pali upalabbhati, pass. of upa-labh, much commoner than the act.): (1) is found, occurs, like Skt. vidyate. This mg. seems probable in, where for corrupt text read prob. nobhayayor antarāle upalabhyate, or perh. with the quotation nobhayam antareṇopa˚; and yan na labhyate tan nopalabhyate, what is not found, does not occur (exist?); it must however be noted that Tib. renders mi dmigs pa, is not conceived mentally, fancied (see under upalambha); (2) is upbraided, reproached: ˚yati; ˚yamāno; no v.l., but as notes, this is the regular mg. of Skt. upālabhyate; perhaps read upā˚, but note the curious fact that cites a Tib. dmigs paḥi (regularly = upa-labh and derivatives!) smra (speech), defined by execration, {{revilling->reviling||20210831||https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/80|}} (apavāda)!

(cf. Skt. id.; not recorded in Pali; cf. prec., an-upa˚, an-upalabdhi, the next items, and aupalambhika), acc. to standard interpretation, mental perception or apperception, realization by the intellect; comm. buddhyā pratipattiḥ; Tib. dmigs (-pa) thought, fancy, imagination; to construe in oneʼs mind, etc.; see also s.v. upalabdhi. Were it not for this persistent tradition, some occurrences, esp. of the neg. forms (an-upalambha, ˚labdhi), could easily be interpreted as related to upalabhyate (1) and mg. (non-)occurrence, (non-)existence. These mgs. are attributed by to an-upaladdhi, ˚labbhana; and tho not recognized in, occurrence, existence seems to me the probable mg. of upaladdhi in the two passages cited for it, and. In many BHS places inconceivability or non-occurrence, non-reality would make equally good sense for an-upa˚. I do not, however, venture to abandon what [Page140-b] seems to have been the standard tradition. Reliance on upalambha, mental perception, fancy, is an error, stigmatized as upalambha-dṛṣṭi, the heresy that relies on upalambha, (or as Bhvr., one who adheres to that heresy,); see also ˚dṛṣṭika. Similarly upalambha-saṃjñin, having the (false) notion of upalambha; upalambha-yogena, by the (erroneous) method of upalambha,, repeated formulaically (cf. anupalambha-yogena s.v. anupalambha).
(see prec.) one who holds the heretical view of reliance on mental perception or imagination (see upalambha): ˚ko … bodhisattvena na sevitavyaḥ;;.
(nt., = Skt. upalālana; to next), coddling, amusing, spoiling: ātmopalāḍana-parāḥ, bent on amusing themselves (with shows and other amusements).
(= Skt. upalālayati), caresses, coddles, treats affectionately: upasthāpayed vā upalāḍayed vā; tās tvām atyartham upalāḍayanti; (see);. Cf. prec.
, nt. (= Pali id.; to next), wheedling, cajoling, humbugging: bālopalāpanaṃ (… of fools, or children) mūrkhasaṃmohanam. The more usual term is bālollāpana, see ullāpana.
(cf. Pali upalāpeti, and prec.), flatters, cheers up: pass. pres. pple., strīnṛttagītair upalāpyamānaḥ.

(denom. to vatsa; as to preverb, cf. upalāḍayati), treats affectionately: kālena ca kālaṃ vaiśeṣikeṇa lābhena priyavāditayā copavatsati (v.l. ˚tsayati), na caiṣu dāsīdāsa-saṃjñāṃ karoti (sc. a bodhisattva, in dealing with servants and dependents).

(= Pali id.; also Vedic, but not Cl. Skt. in this mg.; cf. Anupavadya, nirupavadya), blames, reproaches: (vs) te hi no upavadeyur (so 4 mss.; with v.l. upapadeyur, but this form is bad, it should be ˚padyeyur) anudagrā (mss.), they would blame us as ignoble (or, if anudagrā is nom., being displeased, distressed; this is perhaps more likely).
(m. or nt.; cf. JM. uvavajjana = Skt. *upavarjana, abandonment), abandonment: (vs) svargopavargair viniveśya sattvān sarvajñabhūmim pravidarśayanti.
, m., or nt. id.; : a high number. In cited from, which in the source of the quotation,, has the same, but in a corresponding list udvetana, q.v.

(nt.; Pali Upavattana, see below; Skt. upavartana, nt., country, Lex., and once (24), line 32, virāṭopavartane), land, country (? in Pali, at least later, n. of a locality in the Malla country or of the śāl-grove there where Buddha entered nirvāṇa): (tathāgato … pari)nirvāṇāya gamiṣyati Mallānām upavartanaṃ Yamakaśālavanaṃ; (viharati sma Mallānām) upavartane (ms. ˚tate) Yamakaśālavane; virtually the same; (vss) Mallānām upavartane (text ˚te), Yamakaśālakavane madhye nirvāṇaṃ me bhaviṣyati; (vs) Yamakaśālakavane tatra Mallānām upavartane (so read for text upadartate!); (vss) Yamakaśālavane vane caitye makuṭabandhe tu (cf. caitye makuṭavardhane) Mallānām upavartane, parinirvṛte (? read ˚to or ˚taś) ca tatrāhaṃ … Occurs in Pali and BHS only in reference to the place of the Buddhaʼs parinirvāṇa. In the canonical Pali texts, e.g. (cf. comm.) yena Kusinārā upavattanaṃ Mallānaṃ sālavanaṃ ten(a) …, and cf. esp. Kusinārāyaṃ bhagavā Mallānaṃ upavattane, it could be understood [Page141-a] as the country (of the Mallas); but the comms. seem to have taken it as a place-name, specifically the name of the śāl-grove where the Buddha died. And this is perhaps confirmed by one passage, yadā ca parinibbāyi saṃbuddho Upavattane, where the gen. Mallānaṃ is not found, and Upa˚ most naturally would be a n. of a place (but see below). In Akanumaʼs Dictionary of the Proper Names of Indian Buddhism the word is misquoted as Upavattava = Skt. ˚vartava (but the Chinese transcriptions quoted end consistently in -tan, supporting ˚vartana); the Chin. translations seem regularly to interpret it as a common noun, uncultivated land (the word for land usually rendering bhūmi, land country). This may be interpreted as support for use as a common noun, as it is used (rarely) in Skt. Note that in BHS the name of the grove is clearly Yamakaśāla(ka)vana, q.v.; not so in Pali. Modern editors and interpreters seem unanimously to take Pali Upavattana as n. of the grove (see s.v. for some other references; but the important is not cited there). On the other hand, ed. prints upavartanaṃ with a small initial letter; it fails to record the word in Index or Notes. I am inclined, with some dubiety, to understand the BHS word as a common noun, country. Even the Pali word may have had that meaning originally, and in the canonical passages still. Later, the Pali comms. seem clearly to have understood it as the n. of the śāl-grove; and in it looks like a place name. Yet, if the Chin. translation uncultivated (waste, barren) land be accepted, perhaps upavattane might be understood in this sense in that passage.
, ppp., rained down (upon): (prose) muktāhāram ca varṣopavarṣitam, … rained down in a shower.
(= Pali id.; also Vedic, not recorded for Cl. Skt.), blows near (intrans.): (prose) vātāni upavāyanti yais tāni asipattrāṇi patanti; (ṛṣīṇāṃ gandho …) upavāyati erito mārutena.
, adj., ppp. (= Pali id.; to *upa-vāsayati, unrecorded otherwise), perfumed: (vs) divyagandhopavāsitaṃ; (vs) divya˚tāḥ; (prose) nānāprakārehi ca mālyehi upavāsitaṃ.

(= Pali id., not in or, but occurs; cf. next two), ranges over, occupies oneself with: (see s.v. upavicāra); (atra hi manaś) carati, upavicarati, tasmān manogocarāity ucyante; (sarva)lokagatiṣu copavicaranti.

, m. (to prec.; in mg. 2 = Pali id., badly defined in), (1) environs: (Tib. ñe ḥkhor) grāmopavicāraḥ; (yena suprabhasya) mahānagarasyopavicāras tenopasaṃkramya; kṣetrāṇi samāni samopavicārāṇi; (2) range, scope; substantially = Skt. gocara, see s.v. upavicarati: udakastabdhikā manuṣyāḥ snānopavicārāḥ (text snāto˚), … devoted to bathing (lit. having bathing as their range of interest; cf., where this word is wrongly interpreted); tataḥ paścāc (not cpd. with the following as note suggests!) chravaṇopavicāraṃ vijahayya darśanopavicāre kāyam avanāmya …, after that, causing her to leave the range of hearing (of the assembly of nuns, but still) in the range of (their) sight, having made her bow down her body, etc. (what follows is a private examination of the initiate by a specially designated nun; it is to be held in sight of the assembly but out of their hearing); (pāne yāne) vastre alaṃkāropavicāre bhāṇḍopaskare …, in regard to the sphere of ornaments (i.e. things that fall under the head of ornaments); aṣṭādaśamana-upavicāraḥ (Bhvr.), having 18 spheres of mental activity (said of man; cf. Pali aṭṭhādasamanopa˚), listed in aṣṭādaśeme … mana-upavicārāḥ … cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā saumanasyadaurmanasyopekṣāsthānīyāny [Page141-b] upavicarati, on seeing forms with the eye he ranges over (experiences) such (forms) as give rise to pleasure, pain, or indifference; (20) evaṃ śrotrādiṣu vācyam (with the other five senses, incl. manas), so that there are 6 times 3 = 18 in all.

(otherwise unrecorded; formally caus. to upavicarati, q.v., but seems to be used in same mg.; possibly denom. to upavicāra, q.v.), occupies oneself with, dwells on (mentally): muktakasya … guṇān udānayann upavicārayann abhilaṣan …
, accumulates, heaps up: (prose) avidyāndhāś ca saṃskārān upavicinvanti.

(m.?), in ˚keṣu vā, at the end of a list of arts and exercises (in almost wholly martial; in corresponding passage includes many non-martial) in which the Bodhisattva challenges the other Śākya youths; preceded by rathasmiṃ vā dhanusmiṃ vā tharusmiṃ vā, which does not fit well with any intellectual exercise (reasoning or the like) such as the apparent etymology suggests.

, adj., at end of cpds., lit. forming a subordinate variety (of …), a kind or sort, variety (of …): (vs) devy-upaviśeṣa marutsnuṣeva, a kind of goddess … (said of Māyā); (bodhisattvānām upāyakauśalyatā … nirvāṇoparigāminī) vartmopaviśeṣā, a particular kind of way …
, adj., ppp. of *upa-vi-stṛ-, or cpd. of upa- plus vistīrṇa (?), extended, or rather extended:, in explaining siṃhapūrvārdhakāyaḥ (one of the 32 lakṣaṇa), (anupūrvodgataśarīra) upavistīrṇavṛtorasko.

, adj. (= Pali upavuttha, MIndic ppp. = Skt. upoṣita, to upa-vas), having fasted: (vs) sarvato yaṣṭukāmasya upavustasya (mss. opa˚; no metr. reason for o- instead of u-; em.) me sataḥ; the same vs in Pali,, has upavutthassa.
, adj. (= AMg. uvasamiya), peaceful, characterized by tranquillity: (prose) ˚kaṃ (with all mss. upasamikaṃ) … dharmaṃ saṃprakāśayeyam. See aupaśamika.
(m. or nt.), perhaps a small bed, cot; or, surface of a bed: (prose) tena … samayena Jalavāhanaḥ śreṣṭhidāraka upaśayane (but reading uncertain; 3 mss. om. upa; one ms. upasamane) śayitaḥ.

, ppp. of *upa-śiṣ-, taught: ʼs em., yāni ca bhaiṣajyāni loke pracaranti sattvānāṃ hitasukhārthaṃ sarvāṇi tāni bodhisattvebhyaḥ upaśiṣṭāni (mss. upariṣṭāni or ˚sthāni; like I find it hard to interpret either form; but the absence of record of any upa-śiṣ- or equivalent in Skt. or MIndic makes the em. dubious; cf. however Skt. upa-śikṣ-).
(m. or nt.; = Skt. upaśruti, Pali upassuti; cf. next), listening secretly, eavesdropping: ˚vagatam.

, adj. or subst. m. (= Pali upassutika; from Skt. upaśruti, see prec.), an eavesdropper, or (adj.) engaging in eavesdropping: tūṣṇīm upaśrutikas tiṣṭhed, yad ete bhikṣavo vakṣyanti tad ahaṃ (śrut)yāvāpya dhārayiṣyāmīti. Cf. Pali upassutiṃ tiṭṭheyya.

, causes (a man) to choose, take to himself (a woman, as wife): tad arhasi taṃ mamopasaṃvarayitum, so please make him take me as wife (said to a merchant by an ogress pretending to be the deserted bride of another merchant).
, ppp. of *upa-sam-han-, struck, played (of mus. instruments): daivatyopasaṃhatena vāditraviśeṣeṇa.

(nt.; = Pali id.; to next), provision, production: pitṛbhūtāni kalyāṇamitrāṇi vipulahitopasaṃharaṇa-tayā, good friends are like fathers, because they provide many salutary things; sattvānāṃ kliṣṭavarjitānugrāhakavastūpasaṃharaṇa-kāmatā.

, rarely ˚te (cf. prec. and ˚hāra; use in Pali needs more careful definition than Dictt. have given; the only Skt. use pertinent to BHS uses here cited seems to be collect, as in Cr. ed. dravyāṇy anekāny upasaṃjahāra, collected many things of value; we begin with passages closest to this), (1) collects (as in Skt., above), annajātam upasaṃhṛtya; (2) brings together, provides for someone: (pañca cāsya kāmaguṇān asadṛśān) upasaṃharati sma, and he (Śuddhodana) provided for him (the Bodhisattva;, strangely, als Beispiel herbeiholen) incomparable (specimens of the) five objects of sense; sarvaratikrīḍāś copasaṃhartavyā(ḥ) (same situation); (glānopasthāna …)-kriyayā premagauravaprasādopasaṃhṛtayā, provided (tendered) with affection etc.; kiṃcid eva mātram upasaṃhariṣyāmaḥ (and upasaṃharet 4), we will provide a little something (recompense, present) for you; dṛṣṭibandhanabaddhānāṃ prajñāśastram upasaṃhartukāmaḥ, wishing to furnish the knife of knowledge for those bound in the bonds of heresy; this shades over into (3) produces, effects, brings about, often as in prec. with gen., for …: (tatra bodhisattvo yad eva hitapakṣyaṃ sukhaṃ, tad eva) sattvānām upasaṃharet, na tv ahitapakṣyam; apramāṇāni sattvasukhāny upasaṃhartavyāni, must be effected (here, instead of gen., sattva- as prior member of cpd.); na pramādasthānam asyopasaṃharati, and he does not produce (cause, make) for him any occasion for heedlessness; (na madgubhāvam, so read with ms.) asyopasaṃharati, and he does not cause any annoyance to him (a petitioner, beggar); and 11 (na …) kaukṛtyam upasaṃharati, (a Bodhisattva) does not produce (cause) regret (remorse, troubled feelings, see kaukṛtya; sc. in others); similarly (vs) pareṣu kaukṛty' upasaṃharanti; Tib. renders verb by ñer (= near, rendering preverb upa) sgrub (produce); (ahaṃ … Sarasvatī … dharmabhāṇakabhikṣor) … pratibhāṇam upasaṃhariṣyāmi; (pūjayati sarvākāra-)pūjābhinirhāraṃ copasaṃharati, … and makes an accomplishment of homage of all forms (to Buddhas); (4) esp. with the object something said, produces (stories, sacred utterances, etc.), tells: (tathāgato … tāṃs-)tān dharmaparyāyān upasaṃharati, tāṃ-tāṃ dharmakathāṃ kathayati …; (subj. a preacher) upasaṃharec citrakathāṃ (so, or kathān, mss.); in vividhasaṃmodanakathām upasaṃhṛtya, so prob. read with v.l. in both edd., text of both upasaṃskṛtya; Tib. byas nas, having made; produces or presents (orally), recites (as, a sacred stanza), te upasaṃharanti (sc. the verse cited above, 2—5); (dharmaṃ deśayamānān … vijñāpayamānān) upasaṃharamāṇān (mid. = act., proclaiming) apaśyat; (5) adduces (verbally), mentions, describes, brings up, refers to: (tathāgateṣu …) jñānadarśanam upasaṃharet, one might adduce (describe; but, pile up); (katham …) tathāgatamāhātmyeṣu śrāvakam upasaṃharasi, how can you speak of (adduce) a disciple?; (after contemplation of decomposed corpses; sa imam eva kāyaṃ) tatropasaṃharati, ayam api kāya evaṃdharmā evaṃsvabhāvaḥ, he speaks of (adduces) this very (living) body in this connection, saying, this body too is of the same nature.
, f. (to *upa-saṃ-harṣayati, unrecorded), one who causes joy or exhilaration, augmentation [Page142-b] (to, gen.): (jīvitasya dhanasya ca) prajñayā ˚ṣī.

, m. (to ˚harati; Pali cited only, where devatūpasaṃhārato (supinaṃ passati) prob. means not ‘being seized or possessed by a god’ but thru providing, procurement, causation of, i.e. by, a god), (1) (cf. upasaṃharati 1 and 2) collection or provision, esp. of food and drink: (also 9) bhikṣubhir upasaṃhāra ārabdhaḥ kartum; (kriyatām asya gṛhapater) upasaṃhāra iti; and āmiṣopasaṃhāra, defined as bhojanapānādivikalānāṃ bhojanapānādyupasaṃhāraḥ;; also furnishing, providing of other things, and dharmopasaṃhāra, defined as dharmāṇām anupradānam, q.v.; upakaraṇavikalānām upakaraṇopasaṃhāraṃ karoti; hitasukhopasaṃhāra-prayogaḥ; (dharma, as above); (hita); (naṣṭapratibhānānāṃ) sattvānāṃ pratibhānopasaṃhārāya, cf., s.v. upasaṃharati 3; (tasya … bodhisattvasya … buddhā) bhagavantas … tathāgatajñānopasaṃhāraṃ kurvanti, the Blessed Buddhas make (for this Bodhisattva) a providing of Tathāgata-knowledge; mayaite poṣitāḥ pāramitopasaṃhārair, … by providing for them the perfections; (sarvasattvānāṃ) sarvahitopasaṃhārābhiyuktāḥ; mayātīva evaṃvidho dveṣapratyayopasaṃhāraḥ kṛto, by me such an excessive collection of causes of hatred was made; so the ms., em. to ˚opasaṃbhāraḥ, and in fact in the next line (15) the ms. reads dveṣopasaṃbhāro, but upasaṃbhāra seems otherwise unknown and should prob. be emended to upasaṃhāra, rather than vice versa; one alternative Tib. rendering of upasaṃhāraḥ at is ñe bar (near, a lit. rendering of upa) bsgrub pa (make, provide, supply), cf. s.v. upasaṃharati 3; (2) production, the act or process of producing or causing: in Tib. the usual rendering seems to be ñe bar (= upa) sbyor (or sbyar) ba (produce, compose), as in and (see below), and in one alternative at (see just above), while at it is lti bar sbyor ba (I cannot find what lti means); another word meaning produce, bskyed pa, is used in for kaukṛtyopasaṃhāraḥ, the causing of disturbance of mind or conscience, remorse (see kaukṛtya and upasaṃharati 3; the corresp. Pali passage,, has kukkuccaṃ upadaheyya); on see below; dharmālokopasaṃhāraṃ pratīcchati (here the mg. production, viz. of the light of the law, is guaranteed by the verb upasaṃharati just before, see that word, 3); (3) (cf. upasaṃharati 4, 5) specialized as production in words, presentation (orally), statement, declaration, proclamation, esp. of something of religious nature: śikṣopasaṃhārapratikṣepaḥ, rejection of a statement of instruction (prob. refers to the case of Pali.,); here Tib. ñe bar (= upa) ḥjog pa (put, place, arrange); -dṛṣṭāntopasaṃhāra-, presentation or statement of a comparison; durlabho bhūtanayānuśāsany-upasaṃhāraḥ; dānakāle śīlopasaṃhārasyāpekṣā (acc. to note in, read ˚syopekṣā).

(nt.; = prec.), provision, furnishing: priyāpriya-saṃyogaviyogopasaṃhāraṇatayā, by the fact of provision (for creatures in need) of association or dissociation with pleasant or unpleasant things (respectively), i.e. by the fact that he (the Bodhisattva) sees to it that creatures are thus looked out for.

(m.; to upasaṃkramati), violent attack, = upakrama; ātmānaṃ upasaṃkrameṇa māritukāmo (in prec. line same phrase with upakrameṇa); na śakyam asyā atropasaṃkramaṃ kartum araṇyaṃ nayāmīti; sā tenāraṇyaṃ nītvā tathopakrāntā yathā kālagatā (otherwise Index and).

(nt.; = Pali ˚kamaṇa; in Skt. only Gr.; to ˚kramati), (1) act of approaching, approach: (bhagavantaṃ) darśanāya upasaṃkramaṇāya paryupāsanāya (quasi-infinitives); -bodhimaṇḍopasaṃkramaṇa-; paṇḍitopasaṃkramaṇa-; sarvatathāgatopasaṃkramaṇa-, 22 -jagadupasaṃkramaṇa-; -kalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇam adhyatiṣṭhat; sarvasattva-sarvakālopasaṃkramaṇa-saṃbhāṣaṇa-saṃvāsa- (etc.); upasaṃkramaṇa-paryupāsana- (etc.); (2) approaching (a man, sexually): (girls) nṛttakuśalāḥ hasitakuśalāḥ puruṣopasamkramaṇa-kuśalā(ḥ).

(cf. upasaṃkrama, ˚maṇa; in Skt. approaches, and so also BHS, e.g.;), violently attacks: and 4 ātmānam (aham) upasaṃkrameyaṃ, I would do violence to (= kill) myself; ātmānam upasaṃkramitukāmaḥ; ātmānam eva upasaṃkramitukāmo;.
(for ˚nayati; Skt. upa-saṃ-jan-, mid. intrans., appears, presents oneself), produces, establishes: karaṇaṃ upasaṃjanetvā (so with mss.) imāṃ girām abhyudīremi (mss. ˚retsuḥ, ˚ransuḥ).
, manifests: (prose) tathārūpam upāyam upasamdarśayeyaṃ, yenaite ca pratyakṣā bhaveyuḥ.

, ppp. (to *upa-sam-anv-ā-har-; note that samanvāhṛta (see samanvāharati 3) is used in this same sense, but only once, in the near vicinity of this word,), collected (of food): trailokyaguror anurūpa āhāra upasamanvāhṛtaḥ.

, and ˚padā, f. (cf. the next items; = Pali upasaṃpadā, in both mgs.; the form ˚padā is regular, perhaps universal, in, but has been noted elsewhere only in, other texts having ˚pad), (1) attainment: (vs, = Pali) kuśalasyopasaṃpadā (kusalassa upasaṃpadā); (2) ordination (as monk or nun): four kinds, svāma-up˚, ehibhikṣukāya (instr.) up˚, daśavargena (so!) gaṇena up˚, pañcavargena gaṇena up˚ (see the several terms); ˚padābhāvam icchanti; usually in standing formula preceded by pravrajyā, and followed by bhikṣubhāvaḥ (or bhikṣuṇi-bh˚); so (˚padā);;;;;;; only pravrajyā and upasaṃpadā;; pravrajyā upasaṃpad bhikṣubhāvaḥ; similarly; and (bhikṣuṇībhāvaḥ); pravrajyām upasaṃpadam (acc.) bhikṣubhāvam;;;; (bhikṣuṇībhāvam);.
, adj. (ppp.; = Pali id.; cf. an-upa˚, and the prec. and foll. items), ordained (as a monk):; sūpasaṃpannaḥ (of śrāvakas); varṣaśatopasaṃpannasya bhikṣusya; ˚nnānāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ;; ˚nnasya bhikṣor.
, m. (prec. plus specifying -ka) one that has been ordained (with gen. of ordainer): sarvasyopasaṃpannako, … by anybody.
, nt. (to next; not in), ordination, act of ordaining (a monk): unavimśavarṣopasaṃpādanam.

(= Pali ˚deti; cf. prec. items), ordains, receives into the order of monks: duḥśīlena bhikṣuṇā nopasaṃpādayitavyaṃ; regularly preceded by a parallel form of pravrājayati, ˚jeti: pravrājetu upasaṃpādetu, similarly;; ˚pādetha; (pravrājehi …) upasaṃpādehi; ppp. upasaṃpādita, regularly used when the actual ordination ceremony is in mind, thus slightly differing from upasaṃpanna, q.v., which means (one that has been) ordained; regularly preceded by pravrājita (in text pravrajita); nom. of various numbers, [Page143-b];;;;; (dual);.
(to Skt. upasarga), having … as an affliction, afflicted by …: (vs), read prob. mahāmāry-upasargiṇaḥ (text -opusargiṇaḥ!), gen., of one afflicted by a great pestilence.
, n. of a nāga king: (follows Sāgara, q.v.).

, in sopasṛṣṭāmbaravasanā, would seem to mean she (a wife whose husband had gone away), abandoning the wearing of (fine) garments (kleśair bādhitum ārabdhā). But Tib. seems to have been different; it is cited as de yaṅ (should = sāpi) kha zas zhim po daṅ (= with well-tasting food).

(identity of 1, 2, and 3, and of any of them with one of the Pali personages of this name, not certain), (1) n. of a monk who converted Śāriputra:; (2, possibly = 1) n. of a nephew of the three Kāśyapas, who became a follower of Buddha:; doubtless the same (named after Nadī-Kāśyapa and GayāKāśyapa) and (named shortly after UruvilvāKāśyapa and Nadī-K˚); (3) Upasena Balāntīputra (perh. = Pali Upasena Vaṅgantaputta? Instead of Balāntī- Tib., gar mkhan ma, points to Nartakī-), n. of an evidently important Buddhist elder, who had a retinue of 500 monks:; (4) n. of a former Buddha:.

, ppp. (cf. Skt. an-upaskṛta, nir-upa˚; apparently Skt. literature knows no other forms of upa-(s)karin this sense), corrupted: deśikena sārthacaurair upaskṛtena, by a guide who had been corrupted (bribed) by caravan-thieves.

, ppp. (to Skt. upa-stambh-; in BHS, = Pali upatthaddha, used in ways apparently not closely paralleled in Skt.), based upon, supported by, resting or relying on, with instr., or in comp.:, repeated 12 and, karmopastabdhatvāt, because of the fact that it (the body, or bodily existence) is based on karma (kept going by it); paṇḍito buddhimanto sukuśalamūlapuṇya-upastabdho; pañcavidhaṃ āryasmitaṃ prādur-akare, sayyathīdaṃ: chandopastabdhaṃ, vīryopastabdhaṃ, smṛtyupa˚, samādhyupa˚, prajñopa˚ (based on …); paramapuṇyopastabdhā (as a consequence of supreme merit) vayam īdṛśe pravacana upapannāḥ; (vs) upastabdha (= ˚dhāḥ, n. pl.) ye (text ˚bdhaye) guṇamahodadhibhiḥ sumedhāḥ; tvaṃ … sūpastabdhaś ca śukladharmaiḥ (well supported by, firmly based on …).
, m. (= Pali upaṭṭhāka; for the usual BHS upasthāyaka, q.v.), servant: (vs) ˚ko (v.l. upasthāyako, which is metr. impossible).

(f.), -kārikā, (a woman) serving, doing service to (a man, sexually; said of a courtesan): and 8 (˚kāri), 12 (˚kārikā). Both mss. in 5, and one in 12, read upasthāna; upasthāpana- with v.l. in 8 and 12 (one ms. in 8 ˚sthapana-); see upasthāpana. See also smṛty-upasthāna.
(= Skt. ˚na-gṛha, Pali upaṭṭhānasālā), hall of meeting (for monks):
,, read apāstāni, cast away, with Pali apatthāni.]

, m., read ˚yaka, q.v., servant: (bodhisattvena …) chandako … upasthāpako (so text, no v.l. cited) upasthāpito upanāmehi me chandaka aśvaṃ kaṇṭhakaṃ. In view of the following upasthāpito p for y in the preceding noun is a particularly easy error, possibly made by.]

, see upasthāna-kāri; read upasthāna-. [Page144-a] To be sure defines Pali upaṭṭhāpana by attendance, service; but in the only passage cited,, cf. the comm. 27, it certainly is causative: causing (someone else) to attend, wait upon. That meaning is impossible in.]

(cf. Skt. caus. of upa-sthā-; Pali upaṭṭhapeti, ˚ṭṭhāpeti, only partly corresponding in mg.), (1) (substantially as in Skt.) provides, furnishes: ye kecij jalacarā prāṇāḥ, te na (i.e. te = tān, naḥ? or read tāni? tena, which I cannot interpret) upasthapetha (provide them for us?), sarvabhūtehi yajñaṃ yajiṣyāmi; in (vs) reading doubtful, Nep. mss. upasthāna anekavidhānayānān (or ˚yānaṃ), which is metr. and otherwise impossible; upasthape sya neka˚, metr. bad; em. upasthāyakā neka˚; prob. read, nearly with and Ḱ, upasthape (or ˚pesy? cf. above) ekavidhāṃ sa yānān, he provided vehicles of a single kind; (2) produces a mental state, idea, or emotion, in oneself: mātṛsaṃjñā upasthāpayitavyā, the notion must be formed that (other women) are as a mother; (vs) premagauravam upasthapitvanā (ger., so read with v.l. for text ˚pisva nā), having formed (in oneself) love and respect (for the Bodhisattva); with object smṛtim (cf. Pali parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā or ˚ṭṭhāp˚,,, surrounding oneself with heedfulness or ‘watchfulness of mind’,), abhimukhāṃ smṛtim upasthāpya; same with pratimukhīṃ (v.l. abhimukhāṃ); with abhimukhaḥ (read ˚khāṃ ?); smṛtim upasthāpayati; (3) causes to wait upon (someone), commands attendance (as caus. to Skt. upatiṣṭhati, waits upon): (bodhisattvena …) chandako … upasthāyako (text ˚pako) upasthāpito, upanāmehi me chandaka aśvaṃ kaṇṭhakam, the Bodhisattva summoned-into-attendance his servant Chandaka (saying): Bring me …; (4) sometimes such forms seem used in the sense of the simplex upatiṣṭhati, waits upon (): naitāḥ samarthā bodhisattvaṃ kālena kālam upasthāpayitum; (vs) mātāpitṛṣu vīro upasthapetvā tīvraṃ paricarati, in regard to his parents (the loc. is strange; acc. is to be expected), the hero served (them) sedulously, looking after their needs; (5) treats (medically), cures: vayan taṃ ṛṣikumāraṃ satyavākyena upasthāpeṣyāmaḥ, satyavākyena ca taṃ mṛgaviṣaṃ haniṣyāma. tasya rājño bhavati: … pratibalā ete tam upasthāpayitum; ibid. (15—)16 (taṃ karoma satyavacanaṃ yenāsya mṛgaviṣaṃ haniṣyāmaḥ jīvitaṃ) ca upasthapeṣyāmaḥ (v.l. ˚sthāpayiṣyāmaḥ); kena te upakaranena vaikalyaṃ upasthāpayiṣyāmi.

, m., f. ˚ikā; rarely (;;) m. ˚ika (once also upasthāka, q.v.; Skt. seems to have m. ˚ika very rarely, see, but no ˚aka; Pali only upaṭṭhāka recorded), servant, attendant: (vs) ˚kā nitya parasya; bhagavataś caite putrā bhagavataś copasthāyakā(ḥ); te buddhā bhagavanta upasthāyakadvitīyā upasthāyakatṛtīyā(ḥ);; (vs) upasthāyikās (f.) te vayaṃ, and 19; (vs), read, teṣa munina ye (ed. muninaye) upasthāyakāḥ; ˚yako; Ānando … upasthāyako (sc. of Śākyamuni) bhaviṣyati; teṣāṃ (of aged parents) nāsty anyo upasthāyako, and similarly; ˚yako, attendant of a Buddha (like Ānanda, above); f. ˚yikā; ˚yikāye (so read with v.l. for ˚yakāye); (chandako … bhagavato kumārabhūtasya) upasthāyako; vaidyabhaiṣajyopasthāyaka- … pratyayasaṃpadam; upasthāyaka; (glānopa˚); (buddhānāṃ); (Ānando nāma śramaṇagautamasya); in upasthāyikāś, n. pl. m., all mss., while in 29 below all have vaidyopasthāyakāś ca visarjitāḥ, of the same persons.
, m., n. of a brahman-village in the west, only in dvandva cpd. with Sthūṇa, q.v.: ˚ṇa-; (prose) ˚ṇaka-.
, damage, harm, in Bhvr. cpd. nir-upahatyaṃ nirupadravaṃ bhavet (prose) Cf. Skt. upahati, and (once in) upahatyā.

, m. (nt. once; = Skt., Pali, Pkt. id.), fundamentally gift, (loving) present, in BHS as elsewhere; e.g. (with change of gender) (prose) sarvopahārāṇi copaḍhaukitāni. In a passage beginning used repeatedly in a somewhat peculiar way which misled, who in two notes (,) offers three different interpretations, all wrong (the passage cited from contains a false reading; the ed. does not contain the word cited by, not even as a v.l.). In this passage, the word applies to various acts by which the Buddha miraculously intervenes to save someone from an intended grievous sin or to convert him from a dangerously false heresy. It should be rendered by something like (kindly or compassionate) favor, gift, beneficial service: introduces the detailed stories of specific acts called upahāra thus: paropahārāṃś ca … upaharanti (they present beneficial favors to others) samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ sattvānām anugrahārthaṃ. tad yathā, kaliṅgarājñaḥ kusumāye devyā paropahāraṃ bhagavāṃ vṛttavāṃ, dhruvasya śreṣṭhino vacanopahāraṃ (a benefit by spoken words) bhagavāṃ vṛttavāṃ; the cpd. paropa˚ also;; vacanopa˚ also. Other occurrences: (vs) etāṃ sarvāṃ pravakṣyāmi upahārāṃ manoramāṃ, tasya sattvapradhānasya śṛṇu vikrīḍitaṃ śubhaṃ; (vs) (koṭīyo dvādaśa muniḥ) mānuṣāṇāṃ vinayati, upahāro ayaṃ iti; upahāro vidhātavyo (to prevent Dhruva from burning his parents); (vs) (yat tasya parikarma tat …) tam āhur upahāro ti; (vs) (ye tatra nirmitā bhiksūḥ na caite bhikṣuṇo matā,) upahāraṃ vadanty etaṃ jinā śāstraviśāradāḥ.

(various mgs.) sopādāna (sa-up˚) adj., [Page145-a] having, characterized by up˚, and neg. an-up˚, nir-up˚, without up˚: (1) fuel (app. as the substratum or material cause) of fire: analo upādānaṃ (sc. bhasmīkaroti); (vs) te bhonti nirupādānā ihāmutra nirañjanāḥ; upādānam, foll. by granthaḥ, nīvaraṇam; upādāna-hetuḥ; sarvopādānaparigrahair anarthiko (of the Bodhisattva); (nāpi saṃskṛtānāṃ sāśravānāṃ) sopādānānāṃ dhyānasamādhisamāpattīnāṃ doṣo datto bhavet; (vs) yāsyanti nirupādānāḥ phalaprāptivaraṃ śubhaṃ; anādāno 'nupādāno 'vijñapto … (of Buddhaʼs dharma); abhinandanāyopādānāya adhyavasānāya (em.) saṃvartate (of a heretical opinion); (saṃskārair avaropitaṃ cittabījaṃ) sāsravaṃ sopādānam … bhavati; (3) clinging to existence, specifically (undoubtedly this is meant in some passages cited under 2); esp. as one of the links in the chain of the pratītyasamutpāda; it is produced by tṛṣṇā, and produces bhava (as in Pali, taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ, upādānapaccayā bhavo): tṛṣṇāpratyayam upādānaṃ, upādānapratyayo bhavo;;; modulations of the same formula;;; a peculiar one (vs) tṛṣṇāta sarva upajāyati duḥkhaskandhaḥ, (5) upādānato (read upa˚ m.c.) bhavati sarva bhavapravṛttiḥ, where obviously duḥkhaskandha = upādāna, see below, 4; also pañcopādāna-skandhāḥ (= Pali pañc' upādānakkhandhā), the five skandha which are the basis of clinging to existence (otherwise called simply the 5 skandha, q.v.);; pañcasu upādānaskandheṣu;; (listed as rūpa, vedanā, saṃjñā, saṃskāra, pl., vijñāna,;;;) skandhā sopādānā jñānena mayā parijñātā (vs); in the first of the 4 noble truths, saṃkṣepeṇa (˚pāt, saṃkṣiptena) pañcopādānaskandhā (˚dha-)duḥkham (duḥkhā);;; (4) in sorrow, misery (cf., cited under 3 above), prītīprāmodyajāto nir-upādāno (free from sorrow) vigata-nivaraṇo (see s.v. nivaraṇa), said of the man whose sons have been brought out of a burning house. cites Tib. as rendering upādāna here by mya ṅan, which regularly renders Skt. śoka, grief; and no other interpretation seems possible. It is an outgrowth of (3) as used in religious language.

, ger., postp. (= Pali id.; cf. upādāna, upādiyati; also samupādāya; note an-upādāya, used in a sense not corresponding to any known Pali or BHS mg. of upādāya; formally ger. of Skt. upa-ā-dā-, in BHS and Pali used in special senses), fundamentally (and in Skt.) taking to oneself, assuming, making use of, etc.; BHS meanings (probably all paralleled in Pali, see, whose article on this word is far better than that of): (1) on the basis of, with preceding acc.: (a) in view of, in consideration of, on the ground of, because of: dharmasya cātigambhīrodāratām upādāya, and in view (because) of the very profound nobility of the Law; pratītyasamutpannāṃ dharmāṃ (acc. pl.) … śāstā upādāya pratiniḥsargaṃ vijñapeti, on the ground of states-of-being as originating in dependence, the Teacher teaches abandonment (of them); (sa … sattvānāṃ …) praṇamati, dharmagrāhyatām upādāya, (he salutes creatures,) in view (because) of the fact that they must be made to grasp the Law; (b) making use of, employing: parikalpam upādāya;, making use of a hypothetical assumption, ‘to put an imaginary case’ (); anukampām upādāya (extremely common; also in Pali, ˚paṃ up˚), employing (manifesting, [Page145-b] showing) compassion, commonly preceded by a gen., or in comp., as a merciful favor to … (asmākam …); (lokasyānu˚), 21 (lokānu˚);;;;;;;;;;; etc. etc.; (c) with reference to: (katamā … viśuddhā arthacaryā? sā) daśavidhā draṣṭavyā; bahiḥśuddhim upādāya pañcavidhā, antaḥśuddhim upādāya pañcavidhā; (d) for the purpose of: (sudhanasya …)-paripākam upādāya; -vaśam upādāya = -vaśena or -vaśāt (see s.v. vaśa), the ger. up˚ being as it were the equivalent of the (causal) instr. or abl. ending, as is neatly shown by tathāgato 'parinirvāyann eva parinirvāṇam ārocayati, sattvānāṃ vaineyavaśam upādāya, the Tathāgata, not entering nirvāṇa at all, lets his nirvāṇa appear, for the sake of conversion of creatures (see s.vv. vaineya and vaśa), to which a close parallel in reads vaineyavaśena, or (v.l.) ˚vaśāt, omitting upādāya; in a very similar passage (na … tathāgataḥ parinirvṛto na parinirvāti na parinirvāsyati) … atyantaparinirvāṇenānyatra vainayikasattvavaśam upādāya, … except, for the sake of those who are to be converted by his (apparent or reputed) absolute complete nirvāṇa; (2) beginning from (orig. taking as basis), with prec. acc. (usually) or abl., once ā plus acc., once loc.; often followed by a complementary phrase, yāvat as far as (with following acc. or nom., once loc., in one doubtful case,, possibly abl.); when such phrases with yāvat occur in the examples below, they are quoted; equivalent to prabhṛti with prec. abl. or in comp., and exchanges with it in yad upādāya … tataḥ-prabhṛti, from what time … beginning from that time; (a) in expressions of time or temporal sequence: pūrvakaṃ tathāgatam upādāya yāvat paścimakas tathāgataḥ, so 'pi … abhūd, from the first Tathāgata to the last Tathāgata, even he was …; asaṃkhyeyān kalpān up˚; prathamāyāṃ bhūmau up˚ (the only case of loc. noted!), beginning with (in) the first (bodhisattva-)stage, but in below, prathamāṃ (mss. ˚mā) bhūmim up˚; and dīpaṃkaram up˚, from (the time of) Dīpaṃkara on; adya (mss. asya) saptarātraṃ up˚, from a week ago today; imaṃ divasam up˚; tam eva divasam up˚; garbhādānam (so text, read ˚dhānam?) up˚; the acc. preceded by ā, ā saptamaṃ yugam up˚, beginning from the seventh (previous) generation (so Chin.); yad upādāya rājā vipravāsito, tad up˚, ever since when …, ever since then …; instead of yad … tad, yataḥ … tataḥ, yata up˚ ṛṣikumāro vijñaprāpto tata up˚; and tata up˚ alone = tataḥ-prabhṛti,;;, cf., above; (b) in expressions of place or local sequence: ito brahmalokam (note mixture of abl. with acc.! Brahmā Sahāpati is speaking) up˚ yāvat trayatiṃśad- (so text! see s.v.)-bhavanam; adha-āpaskandham up˚ … yāvad brahmalokam; nadīṃ ca nairañjanām up˚ yāvad bodhimaṇḍo; pārṣṇi up˚ yāvad (? adhi-)kṛkāṭikā; pārṣṇi up˚ yāvat kṛkāṭikāto (abl.! but v.l. ˚ṭikā, nom., which should perhaps be read); bhūmitalam up˚ yāvad bhavāgraṃ; bhaumān devān up˚ yāvad brahmalokam; cāturmahārājikān up˚; bhūmyā devā (acc. pl.; v.l. ˚myāṃ devām) up˚; akaniṣṭhabhavanam up˚; bodhimūlam up˚; pṛthivītalam up˚; vṛddhāntam up˚ yāvan navakāntam; heṣṭā (adv.) upādāya bhavāgra-pūraṃ (instead of yāvad bhavāgraṃ, as in above); the abl. is less common, mūrdhāto upādāya yāvat pādeṣu (loc.; only case of this recorded); mūlato up˚ yāvat puṣpam; (c) in serial expressions, neither temporal nor spatial: sarve caite apekṣā-hetum upādāya pratiniyama-hetvantā hetavaḥ, and all these (are) causes, beginning with [Page146-a] apekṣā-cause and ending with pratiniyama-cause; a few instances included under (b) above might perhaps be placed here.

(Pali and BHS) print ubha(ya)to as separate word, wrongly; it modifies bhāga- directly, as part of the cpd. Tib. on gñis kaḥi cha las … from both parts; Pali = dvīhi bhāgehi vimutto, arūpasamāpattiyā rūpakāyato vimutto, maggena nāmakāyato (i.e. from the skhandha other than rūpa) vimutto. The has a different interpretation acc. to, delivered from the obstacle of the passions (impurities, kleśāvaraṇa), and from the obstacle to (the 8) vimokṣa (which is stated to be akarmaṇyatā, lʼimpuissance corporelle [Page148-a] et mentale). This seems to be a later reinterpretation; the Pali comms. make it simpler, referring to the physical and mental constituents. Which was meant in our texts is not clear from the contexts.

perhaps stirs (food, in cooking): ārabdhaḥ … khādyakāny ullāḍayitum; cf. AMg. ullāliya, ppp., struck, beaten, tossed or flung up (); note to suggests em. ulloḍayitum (cf. Skt. loḍayati, Pali ullola, commotion); but khādyakāny ullāḍayata; (text here ullāṭṭayata).

(to ullapati, q.v.; see also next two), (1) nt., shouting or yelling derisively, abusive derision (this may possibly be the mg. of Skt. ullāpa in khalollāpāḥ, for which Boehtlingk harte Worte von schlechten Menschen): ˚nam (follows uccagghanam) = Tib. (b)stiṅ pa, abuse, also rñiṅ pa (? for rñi, snare, trap? then belonging to mg. 2 below?); Chin. disdain, Jap. talking in a loud voice, abusing; nāsty uccagghanollāpana-dānam, see uccagghana; acc. to note, Tib. here brid, which means deceit(ful), (not wheedling, coaxing, with,) but it seems clear from uccagghana that this is an error; (2) adj., deceitful, deceptive: (vs) (saṃskāra …) bāla-ullāpana riktamuṣṭivat (so read, see this); (kāmāḥ …) ullāpanā riktamuṣṭivat (q.v.); bāllollāpanāḥ, deceiving fools, said of lusts; ˚nam; bāllollāpanaṃ, of worldly life, esp. royal pleasures; read so in for bālālāpanaṃ.

,) f. -ullocikā, ifc. Bhvr. (= Skt. Lex. and AMg. ulloca, AMg. also ulloya, canopy), canopy: svastikollocikā(ḥ) lājā(ḥ), canopied by a svastika (in a painting). See also mukhollocakaṃ.

Cf. also uṣṇi, apparently = uṣṇīṣa in this sense, and uṣṇiṣa. In comp. as one of the lakṣaṇa,;;;;;;; (2) m., one of ten Krodha:; (3) in aṣṭau uṣṇīṣarājānaḥ are mentioned as to be depicted in a rite; their names, given, are Cakravartin, Uṣṇīṣa, Abhyudgatoṣṇīṣa, Sitātapatra, Jayoṣṇīṣa, Kamaloṣṇīṣa, Tejorāśi, Unnatoṣṇīṣa. (ūrdhvāṅga-, ūrdhvaṃga-, ūrdhvaga-; also written ūrdhā˚ without v, see ūrdha-; for other variants see below) -roma(n), adj. (= Pali uddhaggaloma), having (body-)hair standing up, lit. with upright tips, one of the 32 lakṣaṇa, q.v. The form ūrdh(v)āgra-, supported by Pali, is prob. orig. (so,); it is found in; (mss. kṛtvāgra); (mss. ūrddhāgraromarājino or uddhā˚); but in mss. ūrddhaṃga, urddhaṃ ca (ūrdhvāgra). has ūrdhva-ga-romaḥ, but ūrdhvaṃga˚ (both going upward; cf. mss. in); and; also ūrdhvaṃga-(romā, adj.; romatā, subst.). In the ms. has the further change to ūrdhvāṅga-(romatāṃ; ed. em. ūrdhvaṃga), as if ūrdhva-aṅga-roma-; so ūrdhvāṅgaromā (Bhvr.); ūrdhvāṅga-(dakṣiṇāvarta-)-romakūpa(ḥ). Finally in there is great confusion; (only with B mss.) ūrdhāgrā(bhipradakṣiṇāvarta)-romāḥ (read ˚mā, Bhvr.); other mss. u(d)dhāṃgā˚, uccāśā˚ (ucca-āśā); Tib. obscure, yan lag gi spu gyas phyogs nas gyen du ḥkhyil ba, lit. hair of member(s), from (after) right direction (generally = diś or āśā), upward twist (generally = āvarta). As points out, is inaccurate. The expression (abhi-pra-)dakṣiṇāvarta is inserted here in the epithet only in (both passages); it is attached to the lakṣaṇa ekaikaroma(n) in and, and in the commentarial expansion of the latter; but Pali commentarial expansions of uddhaggaloma have a corresponding term,,.

Pali aruṇasmiṃ (mss.; ed. em. ˚smi, m.c.) ūhate (comm. gloss uggate).

(Vedic ohate, to root ūh- or oh-, see, [Page151-a] s.v.; not in this sense Skt.), heeds, pays attention to: parehi ukto paruṣaṃ punaḥ-punaḥ, prabhuḥ samāno kṣamate na ūhate (v.l. ūhyate, uhy˚), … he endures it, pays no attention.

(= Pali id.; cf.; Skt. uddhanti in this sense at most Ved. and, hardly Class. Skt.), removes, puts away, destroys, gets rid of: (adya sarvabhavamūlam aśeṣaṃ) ūhanāmi. Cf. ūhata, the ppp. to this (? or = Skt. uddhṛta).

(= Pali id.; whether it represents Skt. ud-, ava-, or upa-has- is a moot question), laughs (in joy): [Page151-b] = (vs), all mss. mahāhāsaṃ ca ūhati, kept by (see his note); I think we must read ūhasi (or ˚se), 3 sg. aor.; mahā-ūhasitaṃ ūhase (repeated several times), laughed a loud laugh; = (vs) ūhasāsi (seems guaranteed by meter and sense; mss. in ūhāsasi, ūhasari; in more remote; the laugh is one of joy over the following thought:) ayaṃ dānim eko bhavo paścimo (t)ti.
, nt. (orig. ppp. of prec.; cf. Pkt. ūhasiya, used as gloss on Deśī ūhaṭṭha), a laugh:, see ūhasati.
, hyper-Skt. for rikta-, in tucchata ṛktato 'sārato, cited; ṛkta- (prose);; and see riktamuṣṭi.
, nt., a high number, corruption for mṛgava, q.v. (but occurs 3 times):.
